News.title: 'I treat all these people like they are victims', says doctor who treated Krakow shooting suspect
News.content:
Professor Michal PÄdziwiatr, one of two surgeons who treated victims on the street in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, has spoken to the BBC about his experience.

Two doctors were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15.

"We rushed into the area and started our rescue" before the emergency services arrived, PÄdziwiatr said.

The pair raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator.

Read more about how the two doctors helped the Krakow shooting victims.

News.title: Nandy defends linking Erasmus student scheme to Remembrance Sunday after backlash
News.content:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has rejected accusations of politicising Remembrance Sunday after being criticised for linking the event to the UK rejoining the European Union's Erasmus scheme.

Her department announced on Saturday night that "as we mark Remembrance Sunday, Erasmus+ will give a new generation the chance to build connections across Europe".

That sparked a backlash from the Conservatives, who said "veterans did not fight for a student exchange scheme" and accused her of making an "EU membership pitch".

Nandy said she was "horrified" by the Tory response and insisted that the expanded EU scheme for study and work would help young Britons recognise wartime sacrifice.

The UK is rejoining the scheme in January, six years after leaving it as part of the Brexit deal.

On Saturday, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport drew comparisons between that scheme and events on Sunday to commemorate veterans who had died in conflict.

Referring to the scheme, Nandy said in her department's press release: "As we remember the immense courage of those who served our country, we honour them by building the best opportunities for the next generation through closeness and collaboration with our allies."

Conservative Party chairman Kevin Hollinrake described her comments as "tone deaf and frankly shameful" and called on Nandy to apologise.

He said the bonds that veterans forged "run far deeper" than Erasmus.

"It is not a day for a Labour minister to try to make an EU membership pitch," he added.

Reform leader Nigel Farage told the BBC: "For Lisa Nandy to use Remembrance Sunday to announce this and say it's all about peace, it's all about the war - I find that very, very poor taste."

Peter Sharples, chief executive of the Veterans Institute, told the Telegraph that people should "just honour the fallen" on Remembrance Sunday rather than discussing "party political matters".

Asked about the criticism on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, Nandy stood by her initial remarks.

"It was Winston Churchill after the Second World War who talked about extending the hand of friendship across Europe and making sure that we honoured the legacy of that generation," she said.

She said that after Brexit "we closed off opportunities for young people from this country to understand not just the impact that generation made here in the UK, but the way in which they went off and fought for the freedom of people across Europe".

Asked to respond to accusations she had chosen Remembrance Sunday to "promote part of the new deal the government has done with the EU", Nandy said she was "not choosing today or any day actually to promote a deal with the EU".

Pressed about linking the day to what the government believes are the cultural benefits of the scheme, Nandy said: "There was a time where that wouldn't have even raised an eyebrow as somehow political, it was just common sense - and it is common sense."

News.title: Woman says Al Fayed's brother drugged and sexually abused her at Highland estate
News.content:
Jill said escaping the situation was difficult and that she only gradually came to understand the extent of what had happened to her.

"By the time I got away, I was very aware of what he was doing and it took some effort to get away," she said.

"I was by then aware that I could not have been the only one.

"I tried to raise the alarm, I tried to warn people."

Salah Fayed was one of three Fayed brothers who purchased Harrods, the luxury Knightsbridge department store, in 1985.

After his death, Mohamed Al Fayed was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary Predator at Harrods that aired in 2024.

Since those allegations more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line.

Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.

In a statement, a police spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.

"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."

The Metropolitan Police is separately investigating allegations linked to Mohamed Al Fayed and those suspected of facilitating his offending.

It said it was one of the largest and most complex investigations it was currently undertaking.

"Seven suspects have so far been interviewed under caution on suspicion of offences including aiding and abetting rape and sexual assault, assisting the commission of sexual offences, and human trafficking for sexual exploitation," a Met Police statement said.

"To date, 168 victims have now come forward. We will continue to assess victim testimonies for evidence of human trafficking."

In a confidential note, shared with survivors, of a meeting between the Met and the All Party Parliamentary Group for Survivors of Fayed and Harrods, it said about 70 people had been referred to the Home Office as potential victims of trafficking.

News.title: Maya Jama steps down as host of reality TV show Love Island
News.content:
Presenter Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of reality TV show Love Island after three years.

The 32-year-old wrote on Instagram alongside a highlights reel of her on the programme that it was "time to throw myself into something new".

"While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I'll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever," the TV and radio presenter said.

Jama's announcement comes hot on the heels of an appearance as a contestant on Celebrity Traitors that won her praise and speculation in the Times, external that she could "get Â£1m per deal" thanks to her success.

Thanking fans and the production team on Love Island, she said she had an "unforgettable time" on the programme.

"I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the nine incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I've loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show.

But she added: "I've always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then."

Jama landed her biggest presenting role to date as the host of the reality TV show in 2023, taking over from Laura Whitmore.

The programme couples contestants together who then complete a range of tasks and keep swapping in the hope of meeting the love of their life.

An ITV spokesperson said: "Maya has been a fantastic and much loved host on Love Island - we thank her for everything she has brought to the show over the last three years and wish her every continued success."

Love Island is one of the most popular reality TV shows in the UK but the series has polarised viewers, with some arguing the show is misogynistic and raising concerns about the welfare of contestants.

News.title: Dense fog threatens Monday morning rush-hour disruption
News.content:
The Met Office has issued a yellow warning for dense fog across much of England and eastern Wales running from 18:00 on Sunday until 11:00 on Monday. A separate yellow fog warning has also been issued for Northern Ireland and runs from 22:00 on Sunday until 10:00 on Monday. See warning details here, external.

The larger fog warning for England and Wales covers an area of the southern UK stretching from Canterbury to Cardiff, Hull to St Asaph and Southampton to York, and includes London, Birmingham and parts of Greater Manchester.

Visibility could fall to less than 50m in places, making driving difficult. Bus, train, ferry and flight services could also face delays or cancellations.

News.title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says
News.content:
Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquiry looking into the issue has said.

The inquiry's first report, published this summer, concluded that once-in-a-generation reforms were needed to fix a system "not serving the interests of white working-class children".

The next phase will focus on early years children and teenagers aged 14 to 19, aiming for a stronger start at primary school and improving older students' routes through education into successful careers.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "backing" the inquiry to "get to the heart of the barriers holding children back".

Inquiry co-chair and former education secretary Baroness Morris said the next phase of the inquiry's work will consider "what needs to be done".

"This isn't just the responsibility of schools but calls for action from across society," she said.

The Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes, external was commissioned by the multi-academy trust Star Academies, and is supported by the Department for Education.

It spoke to thousands of young people and their parents, as well as hundreds of teachers.

Education data about white working class pupils was also analysed as part of the year-long review, looking at the 1.25 million young people in England who are white British and in receipt of free school meals.

News.title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse
News.content:
Dormouse numbers may be recovering in England and Wales after years of decline, offering a rare piece of good news for one of our best-loved mammals.

The animal has disappeared from much of the countryside with conservationists warning of a long-term collapse in its population.

However, new data suggests dormouse numbers increased between 2020-2025, a period that coincided with warmer springs and summers.

Scientists believe these conditions may help dormice survive, by boosting food supplies and reducing the time they spend asleep.

That gives the animals more opportunity to breed and build up fat reserves ahead of winter.

News.title: Government looking at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
News.content:
Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.

Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".

The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.

In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.

Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."

It came after the Sunday Times reported, external that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.

The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.

Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".

Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.

The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.

A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".

"When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.

An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".

"While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.

News.title: 'Time is up': Minister warns media industry to take abuse seriously in wake of Brand case
News.content:
Abuse in the media industry is probably still happening as organisations are not doing enough to protect women, the culture secretary has warned in the wake of Russell Brand's conviction.

Lisa Nandy told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme: "Time is up, it really is time for the media industry to take this seriously."

She added that since entering government, "many people" from within the industry had reached out to her "to allege that things have happened to them".

Brand is due to be sentenced on Monday after being convicted last week of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, following allegations from multiple women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009.

Nandy was asked whether she believed there was still exploitation and abuse within the media industry, following the Brand trial and cancellation of Channel 4 reality show Married at First Sight after the BBC revealed rape allegations.

She said: "I do not see that much has changed in terms of the way that institutions in the media industry and across public life, including politics, deal with women who very bravely come forward to allege abuse."

Nandy added that there was often no protection and a "very heavy cost" for women who speak up in industries such as media and politics, pointing to power imbalances and short-term contracts some staff members are given.

"Hand on heart, I can't say to you as the culture secretary that this is not happening today. In fact, if I had to wager, I would say it is," she said.

Nandy said many had come forward from within the industry, including from the BBC.

But she added that the BBC had been an "exemplar" in signing up to the industry body to protect whistleblowers - the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority - and urged other organisations to follow suit.

A BBC spokesperson said the broadcaster "has made a significant commitment to improve its culture, processes and standards".

"Last year, following an independent culture review, we set out the behavioural expectations for everyone who works with or for the BBC and we were clear action would be taken if these were not met," the spokesperson added.

News.title: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
News.content:
King Charles III led the nation in a solemn two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday in London to honour veterans who had died in conflict.

On a stone-grey autumn morning, he laid a wreath at the Cenotaph in Whitehall before a march-past by 10,000 armed forces veterans.

That included a shrinking number of World War Two veterans, with 12 taking part this year, including 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who described it as a "very emotional day".

Meanwhile, the number of former prime ministers reached a record high, with nine lined up to lay wreaths, while Andy Burnham attended for the first time as the current occupant of No 10 Downing Street.

And for the first time, the leader of Reform UK, Nigel Farage, had enough MPs in Parliament to qualify to lay a wreath alongside other major party leaders.

News.title: Briton among six killed in 'far-right' shooting in Krakow
News.content:
A gunman believed to have been inspired by far-right ideology has killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in an attack in the busy centre of Poland's second largest city.

Police said the attacker drove on to Main Market Square in Krakow, a popular tourist attraction, on Saturday afternoon and fired randomly at people.

Four women and two men were killed. Three were Polish, one was British and two have not been identified.

Among the 16 injured are five foreign nationals from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia and Britain.

Another three bodies were found when counter-terrorism police searched the suspect's home around 125 miles (200km) away, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

A massive armed police presence was deployed across Krakow on Saturday evening, as security measures were ramped up in the capital Warsaw and elsewhere.

A period of mourning has been declared in Krakow until 11 November.

Two police officers are also among those injured, one critically.

The suspect, who was equipped with military-style weapons and attire, is a 25-year-old Polish man - described by a minister as "ultra-nationalist".

Police shot and arrested him and he remains in hospital having undergone surgery.

Tusk said there were "strong indications" the two women and one man found dead at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec ÅwiÄtokrzyski were his immediate family members.

He said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism... that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow."

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I'm shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in KrakÃ³w today."

"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added.

The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in the historic centre of Krakow, an ornate square which has long been a draw for tourists.

Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out.

The glass front of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes.

Images from the scene show overturned tables and scattered belongings left behind as people ran for their lives.

Armed police officers pursued the attacker's car until it crashed, at which point they engaged him in a firefight.

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify captured the moment a police officer confronted the suspect as he lay on the ground.

The officer, who is visibly injured, can then be seen falling to the ground.

News.title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10
News.content:
Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught.

The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.

The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.

Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.

He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.

These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said: "The early years of secondary school should be a time when children are excited to go to school and engage in the specialist and much broader teaching on offer, and where they find their passion and develop a love of learning."

She added that ringfencing Key Stage 3 studies would allow for "more time to develop deeper understanding, as well as a richer experience that will engage more young people in their passions".

The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.

It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9, from 13% to 15%.

The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.

"The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said. "I'm putting a stop to that."

A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.

However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.

Reacting to the DfE's announcement on Sunday, Lib Dem education spokeswoman Munira Wilson MP said school was "more than drilling kids for exams" but cautioned against "micromanaging" teachers.

She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".

News.title: We face paying £9,000 tax even though our second home is in a war zone
News.content:
A Ukrainian woman who fled to Scotland after Russia invaded her homeland has been told she could face a Â£9,000 property tax charge because she still owns a flat in Kyiv.

Kateryna Stepanovych, 38, discovered the potential charge when she tried to buy a house in North Ayrshire with her Scottish partner Mattias Lindgren.

The couple were told the Additional Dwelling Supplement (ADS) charge would apply because she already owned a property overseas.

Kateryna bought the small flat in 2018, before Russia's invasion. She fled the war zone in 2023, leaving the property behind.

News.title: Two arrested after police officers hurt in brawl outside bare-knuckle fighting event
News.content:
Two men have been arrested and three police officers injured during a street disturbance outside a bare-knuckle fighting championship in Glasgow.

Footage circulating on social media shows a group of men trading punches in the street outside the Ovo Hydro where the event was held on Saturday evening.

More than 20 police vehicles and a police helicopter converged on the area. Three officers were hurt, two of them requiring medical treatment, as they responded to the disorder.

Police Scotland said two men, aged 32 and 27, had been arrested and charged with offences including assault, obstructing police and threatening and abusive behaviour.

News.title: I won't let my daughter's killer live in my head, says Sarah Payne's mum
News.content:
The mother of murdered schoolgirl Sarah Payne says she wants to change how people see victims of crime.

Sara Payne's daughter was abducted while playing with her siblings and murdered in July 2000, aged just eight.

Roy Whiting - a convicted sex offender - was jailed for life in December 2001 for her killing.

Sara told BBC South East there were many reasons behind how people behaved, but they "still have choices".

"You have to choose which path you're going to take," she said.

"I chose not to allow him [Whiting] to live in my head.

"It had to be her - so I keep Sarah."

Sarah's body was found 17 days after she went missing from a field near her grandparents' house in West Sussex.

Her disappearance prompted one of the most heavily publicised searches in UK history and led to landmark legal changes.

"I don't have anger. I don't have aggression. I don't want to bring back hanging or any of those things," Sara continued.

"I just want to go forward in a humane way and be human."

News.title: Veterans shouldn't sleep rough this Christmas, Burnham says
News.content:
No one who served in the UK armed forces should have to sleep on the streets this Christmas, Andy Burnham has said.

Downing Street said the PM would personally write to councils across England on Armistice Day (11 November) to urge them to draw up plans to offer accommodation for veterans sleeping rough ahead of the festive period.

He will say that national and local government should work under the "simple principle" that "no one who has served our country should ever be left to sleep rough on our streets".

The Conservatives have meanwhile criticised Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy for linking participation in an EU scheme for young people with the armed forces' sacrifices on Remembrance Sunday.

Burnham will ask local authorities to use part of the additional Â£874m already announced to tackle homelessness specifically for housing veterans.

"People who stepped forward prepared to put their lives on the line for the rest of us should never lack a roof over their head," Burnham said in a statement issued on Saturday.

"When they need help, the country owes them more than warm words. It owes them a bed every night, a proper plan and someone in their corner from day one."

The PM will ask councils to work with local organisations and charities to tackle homelessness amongst veterans.

Downing Street said an additional Â£8.7m in funding would be allocated to eight organisations across the UK to help housing providers offer assistance to veterans with complex needs, including those with health or addiction problems.

Among them are Veteran Housing Scotland, Launchpad and SSAFA, the Armed Forces Charity.

News.title: Leaders gather in Turkey for UN climate summit after a disastrous year of extreme weather
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

World leaders, delegates and climate activists on Monday will begin negotiations on curbing climate change, which in the last year has led to rising temperatures, deadly heat waves in Europe and beyond, and has played a role in disasters like the devastating floods in Nepal.

This U.N. climate summit, called the Conference of the Parties, or COP31, also comes as the war in Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, pushing up global prices of gasoline and oil and myriad products made with them, such as fertilizers and pesticides. The disruption has pushed governments to rethink energy policies, both in the short-term and long-term, including increased investment in renewable energy sources like wind and solar.

Delegates, meeting in the Turkish Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, will come under pressure to develop new pledges for climate action while implementing previous promises. The stakes are high: climate scientists say global average temperature rise will exceed 1.5 C (2.7 F) since the early 1800s.

Limiting temperature rise to that threshold was a goal established during the 2015 Paris Agreement. Since then, it's been a focus of international climate negotiations. That the goal is no longer realistic underscores how difficult it's been for the world to cut greenhouse gas emissions, which are released into the atmosphere when fossil fuels like oil, gas and coal are burned, leading to climate change.

“This is the first COP where it is clear beyond a reasonable doubt that the world will overshoot the 1.5-degree target,” said Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum. “We will not look away, and we will not lower our ambition.”

Kurum, the COP31 president, has said that rather than establishing new targets, he wants the summit to focus on turning previous climate commitments into action.

He has announced an “Action Agenda” that includes reducing methane, a greenhouse gas, and building climate-resilient cities, among other things. A central theme is electrification, with the aim of increasing the use of electricity — preferably from renewable energy such as solar and wind — from 21% to 35% by 2035, to reduce greenhouse emissions.

During the negotiations, scheduled Nov. 9-20, delegates are also expected to take up the issue of helping poorer countries pay to adapt to rising temperatures and extreme weather events, both tied to climate change, and transition away from fossil fuels.

The last two summits, COP30 in Brazil and COP29 in Azerbaijan, came under criticism for ending with little agreement on how to reduce greenhouse emissions. The final texts of those agreements didn't even mention fuels; at COP28 in Dubai, delegates agreed to transition away from fossil fuels.

Undermining the summit, the United States, which is the world’s second-largest polluter after China, will again be absent. During his first term, and again when he took office for a second time in January 2025, President Donald Trump withdrew the U.S. from climate negotiations.

“No single COP is a silver bullet that can stop climate change overnight,” said U.N. Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell. “But every recent COP has made essential progress. COP31 in Antalya will, too.”

In a change from previous summits, COP31 is being jointly organized by Turkey and Australia after the two jostled over which would be the host. As a compromise, Turkey is the official host while Australia is leading the negotiations. However, both countries have come under criticism for their strong reliance on coal.

News.title: Upgrading power grids to accommodate renewable energy is a key issue at climate talks
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Outdated power grids are a major hurdle in the transition to renewable energy, since older systems often can't absorb all the electricity from new, cleaner sources.

This threatens global efforts to curb climate change by reducing fossil fuels and switching to renewable energy such as solar and wind. At United Nations climate talks kicking off this week, co-hosts Turkey and Australia want more ambitious goals to slash fossil fuels, install renewables and upgrade grids.

Grid concerns are gaining urgency this year as nations race to improve their energy security following the Iran war. The U.N. recently launched a new initiative to rally funding for grid upgrades in Africa and Southeast Asia.

“There needs to be a massive, massive, massive scaling up of investments into grids if we are going to get close to meeting our climate, energy and development goals,” Selwin Hart, special adviser to the U.N. secretary-general on climate action, said.

Climate talks address grid bottleneck

At the U.N. climate talks, hosted in the Turkish resort city of Antalya, organizers describe modern and reliable electric grids as “the backbone of the clean energy system.”

But billions of dollars are needed to upgrade out-of-date grids. These steep costs could hinder further renewable energy installations.

During the U.N. General Assembly in September, the global body launched a Global Grids Accelerator to speed up international funding for electricity infrastructure in Africa and Southeast Asia.

“We’re very confident that the long-term trend is an acceleration of the pace of the energy transition, but we need the infrastructure, grids and storage, to really keep pace,” Hart said.

Annual investment in electricity generation, such as building new power plants, has risen by almost 70% since 2015, reaching $1 trillion a year, according to the International Energy Agency. Yet the agency noted annual grid spending has risen at less than half that pace.

To meet electricity demand through 2030, the IEA calculates annual grid investment must increase by about 50% from today’s $400 billion per year. Any delays will substantially increase global emissions by prolonging reliance on fossil fuels, the IEA warns.

“Power grids have not been readied enough for the scaleup of renewable electricity generation,” said Jan Rosenow, a professor of energy and climate policy at Oxford University. “We have been complacent in the past and now the grid has become a real bottleneck.”

Old grids slow energy transition

Power grids deliver electricity from power plants to homes through a network of transmission and distribution lines, substations and transformers.

Originally designed around large, centralized power plants, many of today's power grids were built like one-way roads, with producers sending electricity to consumers. These older one-directional grids are being overwhelmed by demand surges and a boom in renewables.

Grids have a maximum capacity of electricity that they can safely store, transport and distribute. If a grid is already at capacity, solar and wind farms can be instructed to limit their electricity output, a process known as curtailment.

China and India, which have installed impressive amounts of renewables, can't take full advantage of the massive buildout for this reason.

China curtailed 360 terawatt-hours — close to the equivalent of the United Kingdom's annual electricity demand — of wind and solar electricity in the first half of 2026, according to Global Energy Monitor and the Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air.

India curtailed 11 terawatt-hours of solar generation — enough electricity to power about 10 million homes — over the course of 15 months spanning 2025 and 2026 because of insufficient transmission and storage capacity, according to the energy think tank Ember.

Curtailing solar and wind generation while fossil fuels continue to supply electricity is a blow to climate efforts, especially since China and India are among the world's largest emitters, said James Abraham, with the New Delhi-based Council on Energy, Environment and Water.

To transition away from fossil fuels, he said, "you need a grid changeover. You need a grid transformation.”

Solutions exist, despite funding concerns

Upgrading existing grids to be more flexible could increase efficiency by allowing electricity flows to adjust to supply and demand. It could help areas with excess solar and wind energy send it to places with higher electricity demand and fewer energy resources.

Newer, more flexible grids could also make it easier for utility companies to exchange electricity with households that have solar panels or battery storage.

But many countries can't afford to take these steps, or at least not quickly enough, according to Abraham, who said “the need is now. It’s a time tension rather than anything else.”

Global energy security concerns deepen

The Iran war's energy shock built up momentum for the energy transition, especially in hard-hit regions like Southeast Asia, but investment in renewables is outpacing grid development, said Gahee Han, with the Seoul-based nonprofit Solutions for Our Climate.

“Unless we upgrade our power grid in Asia, Asia will have no choice but to rely on the conventional power plants, like gas or coal,” she said. “It’s nonsense to rely on those power plants, especially considering the energy crisis.”

One of the solutions being promoted by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations is an interconnected power grid that would allow countries to trade power more easily, adding a safeguard against future shocks.

Interest in the ambitious plan, which is still in its infancy, is growing, according to Abdul Razib Dawood, executive director of the ASEAN Center for Energy.

“We have this crisis that will unify the region. You need your neighbors," he said. “This is an opportunity for us to really strengthen the cooperation.”

News.title: Trump nearly comes to a realization why he got shellacked in the midterms only to quickly blame the media
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump almost came to a conclusive realization as to why his party got shellacked in Tuesday’s midterm election — but then he just blamed the media.

Trump has repeatedly said that the Republicans were defeated because he wasn’t on the ballot, despite pleading with supporters to vote as if he were on the ballot. But it also seemed to finally sink in when he admitted to some of his own errors with the eight-month-long war against Iran that he started.

“Two years ago, you won a big, some might say historic victory. Just now, the Republican Party in the midterms suffered a big, some might say historic defeat. Give me your political analysis of what just happened?” correspondent Ross Douthat asked Trump on 60 Minutes Sunday night.

“They didn't like the war. They didn't like the fact that gasoline went up because I had it down at a low. And there's a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel,” Trump replied.

The Iran war was unpopular with voters who saw gas prices skyrocket during the conflict. The national average for a gallon of gas was still above $4 on Sunday, about a dollar up from a year ago, according to the AAA Motor Club.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump almost came to a conclusive realization as to why his party got shellacked in Tuesday’s midterm election — but then he just blamed the media ( CBS News/60 Minutes )

But when asked about the overall negative view of the economy due to the war, Trump began blaming the media for poor coverage. The president has often made his disdain for the traditional press known, repeatedly lashing out at journalists, including The Independent’s Andrew Feinberg, for asking genuine questions and trying to ban several outlets from the White House.

“In poll after poll, people say they're unhappy with this economy in a way they weren't in the first term. Cost of living, inflation, and so on. Is that all just the Iran war?” Douthat asked.

“The press doesn't cover positive news for Republicans. They don't cover, certainly, positive news for me. So I have to do it myself,” Trump said. “I have to get it out there. We have historically good numbers. We have the highest stock market in history.”

The president spent all of last month hosting rallies to try to drum up support from his base. But on Tuesday, in what was dubbed a “blue tsunami,” Democrats took control of the House and the Senate and won key governors’ races.

When high-profile Senate candidates Trump had fiercely campaigned for, such as Texas’ Ken Paxton, Ohio’s Jon Husted and Kansas’ Roger Marshall, lost, the president initially refused to take any responsibility.

open image in gallery Trump has repeatedly said that the Republicans were defeated because he wasn’t on the ballot, despite pleading with supporters to vote as if he were on the ballot. But he also admitted to some of his own errors with the eight-month-long war against Iran that he started ( Getty Images )

“I wasn’t on the ballot, and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” he wrote on Truth Social on election night, despite having record-low approval ratings.

In the first major shakeup since the GOP’s shellacking, Trump replaced his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with her deputy, Stephen Miller, this week. Miller is known as the architect of Trump’s hardline immigration policies — the same policies that many Americans have found too aggressive.

Douthat asked Trump during his 60 Minutes interview, taped shortly before Wiles’ ouster, whether he expects to fire anyone.

“I do, a little bit,” Trump said. “I love my cabinet. I think they’re good. But I’ll be doing maybe a few changes. I don’t want to mention who.”

Douthat also asked whether Trump had confidence in Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth amid reports that either lawmakers will try to impeach him or the president may get rid of him on his own.

“I do,” the president said, mentioning the operation in Venezuela last January during which American forces covertly captured then-President Nicolás Maduro.

open image in gallery But when asked about the overall negative view of the economy, Trump began blaming the media for poor coverage, saying, ‘The press doesn't cover positive news for Republicans. They don't cover, certainly, positive news for me. So I have to do it myself’ ( Getty Images )

“You credit Pete Hegseth for that?” Douthat asked. “No, but he was a part of it,” Trump said.

Douthat probed Trump during the interview about how he would work with Democrats for the next two years of his presidency, mentioning his mocking nickname for Texas Senator-elect James Talarico.

“You did occasionally call him ‘Tala-freako,’” Douthat said. “Do you think you could work with the Democrats without insulting them consistently?”

Trump said he could, and then continued with the name-calling: “I also call many of them Dumocrats.”

“If it took six months of not insulting the Democrats to get a deal done, you think you could do it?” Douthat asked. “Very easily,” Trump replied.

News.title: Cruise ship employee found by fishermen treading water 20 miles off the California coast
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Royal Caribbean employee has been found by two Newport Beach fishermen treading water 20 miles off the California coast.

The cruise ship worker was rescued Friday after being spotted by Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, who had been fishing for marlin that morning.

"I'm like, 'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat. Let's get all of our lines in,’” Garrett recalled in an interview with CBS Los Angeles.

The employee, whose name has not been revealed, told the fishermen he was a pianist on Royal Caribbean’s 14-deck Ovation of the Seas ship.

Norton said he and Grant lifted the man, adding that the pianist was “in total shock.”

open image in gallery A Royal Caribbean employee was found Friday by two Newport Beach fishermen treading water 20 miles off the California coast ( Getty/iStock )

"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton said.

Once the man was safely out of the water, the fishermen put out an emergency call, and Newport Beach lifeguards responded.

Local authorities believe the man may have gone overboard roughly nine hours before he was found.

"It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean,” Newport Beach Lifeguard Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda told CBS LA.

A spokesperson for Royal Caribbean acknowledged the incident, telling The Independent, “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share."

open image in gallery Local authorities believe the man may have gone overboard roughly nine hours before he was found. He was hospitalized but is expected to survive, according to the Coast Guard ( Getty )

The rescue occurred during a particularly strong El Niño this fall that is keeping the Pacific Ocean warm off the coast of California.

"You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water's 76 degrees. A different year — no way he makes it,” Norton said.

The Coast Guard confirmed to The Independent that a “conscious individual” was rescued from the water. The man was reportedly hospitalized but is in stable condition, the Coast Guard said, adding that the incident is under investigation.

The Independent has reached out to the Newport Beach Fire Department for comment.

News.title: Rock band Muse revealed as third BST Hyde Park 2027 headliner
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Rock band Muse will headline British Summer Time (BST) Hyde Park on 26 June 2027.

The British trio, fronted by Matt Bellamy, is the latest headliner to be announced for the festival, and will also headline Roundhay Festival in Leeds on June 27.

Muse will be supported by indie band Nothing But Thieves and electronic trio Chvrches in London, with Nothing But Thieves also joining for the Leeds date.

Further support acts for both shows will be announced in due course.

The gigs come after Muse released their 10th studio album The Wow! Signal in June this year, which reached number one on the UK album chart.

open image in gallery Muse to headline British Summer Time (BST) Hyde Park next year ( BST Hyde Park )

They followed the record with a world tour, which will see its UK leg next month with performances at Manchester’s Co-op Live and London’s The O2.

Formed in Teignmouth, Devon, Muse have gone on to achieve four UK top 10 singles and eight UK number one albums, as well as winning two Grammy Awards.

They are best known for songs such as Supermassive Black Hole, Plug In Baby and Uprising.

The band’s line-up is made up of Bellamy on guitar and vocals, Chris Wolstenholme on bass and Dominic Howard on drums.

open image in gallery American rock band Bon Jovi was named as the first headliner ( AFP/Getty )

At BST, Muse will join rock band Bon Jovi, who will perform on June 24, and soul pop star Raye, who performs on July 10, on the bill.

Frontman Jon Bon Jovi said: "We have a storied history with performing at Hyde Park on previous tours and it's a full-circle moment to be returning to BST Hyde Park, 14 years after headlining the very first festival.

"The Forever Tour has been an incredible celebration of the music and the fans who have been with us all these years.

“There’s nothing quite like the energy of a UK crowd, and the joy and excitement we shared with our fans this summer was something truly special. To bring that energy back to Hyde Park means a lot to us. We’re grateful for every one of you and can’t wait to make more memories together.”

The 2026 headliners for BST Hyde Park included Garth Brooks, Ateez, Maroon 5, Mumford & Sons, Duran Duran, Pitbull and Lewis Capaldi.

Tickets for the BST Hyde Park show will go on general sale at 10am on November 13, at Roundhayfestival.com and Bst-hydepark.com.

News.title: Royal Navy launches its first autonomous squadron of uncrewed boats
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Royal Navy has created its first autonomous squadron to operate uncrewed boats on frontline operations.

The 1st Autonomous Squadron, which was formally launched on Thursday, is based at Portsmouth Naval Base and comprises about 180 personnel who will operate two craft – Rattler training vessels and the Kraken K3 Scout boats.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the force has been created in response to the changing face of modern warfare.

A Navy spokesperson said that the Rattlers are designed to perform a range of operations and have been trialled escorting warships in Scotland while being remotely piloted from 500 miles away.

The Kraken K3 Scout has a range of 600 miles, extendable to 1,100 miles, and has also been tested off the south coast “in force protection, surveillance and reconnaissance roles”, the spokesperson said.

open image in gallery Two Kraken and a Rattler Uncrewed Surface Vessel on display at Portsmouth Naval Base ( Ministry of Defence )

Mr Streeting said: “The threat environment we are facing is fundamentally different from that of recent decades. A major determinant of military power now is who can innovate fastest.

“That’s why we are using the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the Cold War to put the latest autonomous technology in the hands of our sailors, to help them protect our shores and those of our Nato allies.

“The more ready we are to fight and win, the less likely we are to have to.

“This investment strengthens our warfighting readiness and therefore our deterrence.”

open image in gallery Kraken unmanned surface vessels with HMS Queen Elizabeth in the background at Portsmouth Naval Base ( Ministry of Defence )

The creation of the new squadron is part of a move towards a “hybrid navy” with £1.5 billion being earmarked for the initiative over four years.

Royal Navy Fleet Commander Vice-Admiral Steve Moorhouse said: “For generations, the Fleet has been built around ships, submarines, and aircraft, manned by sailors and Royal Marines. From today, an autonomous squadron takes its place alongside them.

“The seas are becoming more contested, more dangerous and harder to operate in.

“A hybrid navy is about giving our people better tools. It means more reach, more striking power and more options.

“It will help make the Fleet more lethal, harder to knock out of the fight and quicker to adapt. People will remain at the heart of it.”

News.title: Greggs opens permanent luxury suite inside five-star UK hotel
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Greggs is days away from opening a luxury hotel room that includes a world-first “ring for a sausage roll” concierge service.

Reservations for the permanent suite at the five-star Hotel Gotham in Newcastle will open on Monday, with stays available as soon as Thursday.

Guests staying in the suite will have a dedicated rotary phone to request freshly baked Greggs favourites delivered directly to the room on a silver platter.

The ‘Greggs Suite’ – decorated in the bakery chain's brand colours of midnight blue and gold – sleeps two guests and will be available to book year-round.

Those staying in the first 96 days will also be given limited-edition merchandise to take home, including bespoke dressing gowns, slippers and eye masks.

open image in gallery The suite feature a world-first 'Ring for a Sausage Roll' concierge service ( Greggs )

A portion of proceeds from each stay will be donated annually to the Greggs Foundation which supports local community initiatives and schools via the Feeding Brighter Futures programme.

Greggs said the collaboration offered an “unexpected twist on top-tier hospitality, blending the high-end elegance of Hotel Gotham with the unmistakable high-street character of Greggs”.

Zoe Harris, customer director at Greggs, said: “We love finding unexpected ways to bring joy to our customers and partnering with Hotel Gotham has allowed us to create something that's both luxurious and delightfully Greggs.

“The suite offers a truly unique experience that could only happen in our hometown of Newcastle. We can’t wait to welcome guests through the doors and hear what they think.”

open image in gallery Those staying in the first 96 days will receive limited-edition merchandise to take home ( Greggs )

Hotel Gotham's general manager Chris Thompson said: “Hotel Gotham Newcastle was created to celebrate the bold spirit of this incredible city, so a collaboration with one of Newcastle's most recognisable brands feels like a natural fit.

“The Greggs Suite brings together our signature Art Deco glamour with Greggs' unmistakable sense of fun, creating a stay that feels uniquely Newcastle.

“We’re delighted to welcome it as part of the next chapter of Hotel Gotham Newcastle.”

To book, visit the Gotham website, or Greggs is offering the chance for two people to win an overnight stay at the hotel in a giveaway via its app.

The competition will take place every three months for the next two years.

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso disgusted after Chelsea bullied by Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Rees-Zammit delivers in best position but work to do for sloppy Wales
News.content:
Maybe it is an indication that Wales are improving that this latest close victory over Japan was greeted with a shrug instead of euphoria.

A year ago, almost to the day, Steve Tandy, the Welsh head coach jumped around and hugged his staff, after a one-point win over the Brave Blossoms and there were reports of red-shirted fans in this stadium crying in joy and relief.

Yet that was Wales’s first home success in 10 Tests and, despite the form since hardly raising itself anywhere near levels of excellence, much more was expected on this occasion.

Yes, Tandy’s men prevailed and it was a huge positive to watch player-of-the match Louis Rees-Zammit in great nick on the wing. Nobody should overestimate the Bristol man’s display because the game knows that he can operate even better, but after this there can now be no doubt that he is a wing rather than a full-back. The 25-year-old conjured five line breaks, beat 13 defenders and made 121 metres.

Yet most notably, Rees-Zammit scored his first try for his country in eight matches and that is exactly what he was put on the green-green grass to do. After assisting in fellow wing Josh Adams’s opening try – this other resurgent British and Irish Lion bagged a brace – Rees-Zammit showed his predatory instincts to go over after a wonderful deft offload from centre Eddie James.

Sports.title: Three points from Man Utd’s chaotic draw with Villa as Dalot at point of no return and defensive heart-surgery needed
Sports.content:
Next

THE chaos that comes with Manchester United surpassed all expectations as the final whistle blew in their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Alysson and Nicholas Jackson launched a brutal attack on the Red Devils, putting them two behind inside the first four minutes.



Bruno Fernandes’ spot-kick and Youri Tielemans‘ first United goal dragged the hosts level before another two-goal lead was imposed less than ten minutes later.

And if that was not enough, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu found the back of the net in injury time to help them take a point back to their digs in 18th.



SunSport’s Manchester United reporter Katherine Walsh talked through the three big points from the messy fixture.

FAN PROTESTS

Each Manchester United game just cranks up the heat on the club’s under-fire hierarchy.



New signs, chants, banners, failed walkout plans and tennis balls thrown on to the pitch.

Yesterday, there was a new sign on show that read, “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners”.

That was unfurled in the Stretford End, where Red Devils fans still sang boss Michael Carrick’s song.

SunSport was also sent pictures of “F*** the Glazers” spread across gold and green balloons — the colours of the original Newton Heath club.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Several balloons made their way over to the directors’ box in the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand, where director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada tried to ignore the hate.

Frustrated fans made their feelings clear with anti-Glazer hatred aimed at the missing American family, who are seemingly preoccupied with their Tampa Bay NFL team.

And minority co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe — who has his eyes set on a new ‘Wembley of the North’ to replace Old Trafford by 2035 — also faced flak.

How about fixing the issues on the pitch to avoid relegation?



The demonstrations reflected the growing unrest surrounding the club’s direction, with supporters demanding accountability and a clear plan to save the Red Devils from the dreaded drop.

For many supporters, a change in fortunes will not be enough.

LEAKY DEFENCE

United’s entire backline is a total shambles and the club now needs open-heart surgery to fix it.

The Red Devils have shipped 30 goals in all competitions this season — only Lens with 31 have a worse record across Europe’s top five leagues. It is a ­defensive crisis.



Their frontline showed admirable fight to haul them back into the contest against Aston Villa, but it was like trying to win a boxing match with both hands tied behind your back.

Whatever Carrick’s side produce going forward, their defenders look capable of throwing it all away.

They have now conceded 15 goals in their last five games — including a 4-1 humiliation in Como — with a trip to Liverpool now looming after the international break.

A defensive rebuild is promised for summer 2027 and I would struggle to find many who deserve to survive next season.



Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are all out of contract, while Diogo Dalot has reached the point of no return amid a Joshua Zirkzee-style humiliation.

There were huge, mocking cheers when the Portuguese full-back was replaced by Patrick Dorgu on 66 ­minutes — the Old Trafford reaction was reminiscent of the savage reception handed out to Zirkzee when he was hooked against Newcastle back in 2024.

Dalot was all at sea for Villa’s opener before gifting them a daft penalty shortly after the break.

Yet making him the fall guy misses the bigger picture. Changes are needed across the back, who are without a clean sheet in the league this season.



LACK OF LEADERS

Carrick’s struggling side play off moments, which is unsustainable in the Prem.

It is the hallmark of a side desperately short of structure, leadership and control.

It also explains why the fallen giants have found themselves in the relegation places.

Their attack has stepped up, with Matheus Cunha almost a one-man band, trying to inject the energy and urgency required.

And who would have predicted Danish wideman Dorgu becoming the unlikely saviour?



His goal and assist helped rescue a point and handed Carrick an eight-point haul from ten games.

Bruno Fernandes looked furious at the final whistle despite the comeback, which told its own story.

Even Cunha and Amad Diallo had the audacity to gesture towards the crowd for more noise, despite the wreck unfolding in front of them.

Old Trafford has shown it can roar when given something to believe in — and the players feed off that energy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But it should not be the supporters’ job to drag the team over the line.

United need to give their fans something to shout about — not keep demanding they help bail them out.



It was Villa who threw this one away.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace ready to sack Pierre Sage after woeful start to season with two immediate frontrunners to replace him

CRYSTAL PALACE are ready to SACK manager Pierre Sage after just 16 games in charge.

The Frenchman’s future is hanging by a thread following today’s 3-1 defeat to Liverpool at Selhurst Park.

Palace are set to part company with Sage, 47, just five months after appointing him as manager.



SunSport understands Thomas Frank and Sean Dyche are the two leading contenders to take over at Selhurst Park.

Sports.title: ‘This just can’t go on’ – Gary Neville fears Man Utd ‘causing themselves emotional damage’ with post-match antics
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE revealed his brutal worries concerning Michael Carrick’s Manchester United after their 4-4 thriller with Aston Villa.

The Red Devils trailed the Villans by two goals after just four minutes in their box office clash.



Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans dragged the hosts level, only for a quickfire Villa double after half-time to have them 4-2 down once more.

While two goals from United in injury time meant that both sides took away a point apiece, Neville is concerned about the “emotional damage” they are causing themselves.



After the final whistle blew, Carrick & Co. sauntered around the pitch, clapping the home fans – but the former Prem skipper is not convinced.

The 51-year-old said: “You have got to admire their persistence. They kept going.

“Their defensive errors were shocking.

“I played for Manchester United 602 times. I always appreciated the fans after the game.”

Neville admitted that the post-match “lap of honour”, particularly after the 3-0 Bournemouth result too, was “painful to watch”.

He said: “It’s almost like they’re causing themselves emotional damage.

“This just can’t go on, can it? It’s absolutely desperate.

“Michael will be proud of them.

“The fans are singing his name because they love him, but this is a really sorry situation.”



Before the game, the clash was viewed as a make or break for Carrick, but the draw just might be enough for him to survive the international break.

During the Villa game, Diogo Dalot was booed off by the United fans, but the boss insisted that he’s “giving everything” he’s got.

Carrick said: “We’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

“Diogo, he gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played left back, he’s played really well at times.

“Picking a team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision, but it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.”

United still only have one Premier League win to their name this season from a 5-2 home victory over Ipswich on August 30.

Sports.title: ‘Got to be careful’ – Michael Carrick warns Man Utd fans over their reaction to Diogo Dalot substitution

MICHAEL CARRICK has warned Manchester United supporters to “be careful” with how they treat players after Diogo Dalot was booed during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Dalot joined United from Porto in 2018 and is under contract until 2028, with the option of an additional year.

Dalot’s replacement, Patrick Dorgu, nodded in United’s 96th-minute equaliser.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick in tense exchange with Sky Sports reporter as he’s asked whether he would resign as Man Utd manager
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK will not quit as Manchester United manager despite one win from ten Premier League games.

Although United scored in the 92nd and 96th minute to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, they are 18th.

With United certain to be in the bottom three for a fortnight during the international break, it will be the longest the club has spent in the relegation zone since October 1986.



The United hierarchy resisted sacking Carrick in the wake of the 3-0 drubbing by Bournemouth a fortnight ago and United have since lost at Chelsea, beaten Roma and drawn with Villa.



Carrick is due to oversee some training sessions at the club’s Carrington training complex this week but his future remains mired in uncertainty.

The 45-year-old gave little away in his post-match debriefs and had a prickly exchange with Sky Sports pitchside reporter Patrick Davison when the topic of Carrick’s future surfaced.

When asked if he could walk away, Carrick stressed: “It’s not going to happen, no.”

Carrick then disputed whether he would hold discussions with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

At his post-match press conference, Carrick added: “I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games.

“Yeah, 100%, yeah [I’ve seen enough to turn things around]. I think there’s more than enough.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Goals change games and you’ve got to deal with it, and it’s part of something we have to improve on drastically, but there’s more than enough.



“We’re just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times.”

Carrick all but acknowledged that the international break had come at a convenient time for United, who have won three games from 15 this term.

United’s next Premier League fixture is at Liverpool on November 22 before they had to Lisbon to face Sporting in the Champions League.

By the time United kick off at Anfield, they could be bottom. “It’s been a right mixed week, or two or three really, if you’re looking at the events,” Carrick said. “But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

“Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.



“But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training, we’ll have one or two days off, not too much, but we’ll train and we’ll get ready for the next game.”
