Sports.title: Man Utd finally show fight in Aston Villa thriller - but Michael Carrick's fate hangs in the balance
Sports.content:
Manchester United staged a dramatic late fightback to salvage a point against Aston Villa in a thrilling 4-4 draw despite defensive collapses at the start of both halves, with the result still likely to leave Michael Carrick's position hanging in the balance.

United had slipped into the relegation zone before a ball had even been kicked courtesy of Nottingham Forest's victory over Manchester City on Saturday evening and their fortunes did not improve once they took to the field, instead worsening instantly.

Alysson required less than 60 seconds to slot the ball through Senne Lammens legs to leave Old Trafford shellshocked. The stunned silence that filled the air swiftly turned to anger as Nicolas Jackson doubled Villa's lead just two minutes later after Lammens palmed the ball into his path, condemning Manchester United to the worst possible start.

With the fans' anger ringing in their ears, United dragged themselves back off the canvas after that devastating one-two to hit back, first from the penalty spot after Glen Kamara wiped out Matheus Cunha. Bruno Fernandes, so often United's saviour in years gone by, made no mistake from the spot.

‌



The comeback was complete just before half-time when Youri Tielemans netted against his old club, but United imploded spectacularly once again after the break. First, Diogo Dalot lost all leave of his senses to give away a needless penalty which John McGinn converted with aplomb.

Another episode of calamity saw Villa restore their two goal advantage with Leon Goretzka tapping home after shoddy defending.

It didn't feel like there would be any way back for United this time. But they fought back once more with Joshua Zirkzee netting in the 92nd minute to spark a late barrage which resulted in a last-gasp goal from Patrick Dorgu.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

UNITED FINALLY SHOW FIGHT

View 4 Images John McGinn celebrates after notching Aston Villa's third goal (Image: Ed Sykes/Allstar)

Just when you think things can't get any worse for Manchester United, Aston Villa go and stick two goals past Lammens inside four minutes to turn Old Trafford toxic. It certainly wasn't the start United or Michael Carrick would have envisaged, but it did, at least, trigger a response from their struggling stars.

‌



Kamara didn't need to scythe down Cunha to gift United a route back into the game via the penalty spot. But they did, finally, show some fight to haul themselves back into the game - only to then throw that away with another unforgivable start to the second half.

United have now shipped 30 goals in all competitions - the joint worst in Europe's top five leagues - and started the game languishing in 19th place in the Premier League. But they rallied to snatch a point at the death.

CARRICK'S FATE IN THE BALANCE

View 4 Images Michael Carrick is likely to pay the price for another poor result (Image: James Gill/Danehouse)

‌



For a long time, this felt like the point of no return for Manchester United's beleaguered head coach. And in truth, even United's rousing late fightback may not be enough to save his job.

Carrick should not be the only figure to pay for United's plight, but it's hard to lay out a case for him staying in his post with his team just one point away from propping up the table. He and his staff looked utterly bewildered on the bench following Villa's early goals, as did Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands.

One thing that is clear after Sunday's game is that the players are still playing for him. Fightback or not, though, it's still been a ludicrous start to the season - just one league win in 10 - and while Carrick is not the root of United's problems, he is not the solution, either.

EMERY'S OLD TRAFFORD ANGER

‌



If Manchester United do spend the international break shopping for a new manager, you wonder whether they will cast their eye in the direction of Unai Emery.

A combination of the gargantuan compensation fee it would take to prise him away from Villa Park - said to be around £20million - and United's sorry plight probably makes that a rather unrealistic prospect just now. And while that may be bad news for United, it's great news for Villa, who are looking upwardly mobile under the Spaniard after a transitional summer.

But an irate Emery let his anger get the better off him in the final seconds, storming off following United's late leveller after it was allowed to stand.

POST-MATCH SCENES SPEAK VOLUMES

‌



View 4 Images Manchester United players look on after conceding (Image: Carl Recine)

Once the euphoria had died down, the pictures at the final whistle best told the story.

On the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson's appointment, United may have struck in Fergie time to salvage a point but you wouldn't have guessed it from the players' faces.

The mood was sombre given this result was still not the tonic United or Carrick needed heading into the international break, which will only bring further scrutiny with United in the relegation zone.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans' brutal reaction to Dalot Dalot substitution speaks volumes after shambolic display
Sports.content:
Man Utd fans' brutal reaction to Dalot Dalot substitution speaks volumes after shambolic display

Manchester United defender Diogo Dalot was hauled off in the second half of their chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday - and the Old Trafford crowd's reaction was brutal

View 2 Images Diogo Dalot was hauled off in the second half against Aston Villa (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Manchester United supporters greeted the substitution of Diogo Dalot with loud cheers during their drama-packed 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday.

‌



‌



Dalot was taken off alongside Youri Tielemans and Amad Diallo in the 66th minute at Old Trafford. Michael Carrick brought on Patrick Dorgu, Mason Mount and Shea Lacey to try and turn things around, with the score at 4-2 to Villa.

‌



Carrick came into the match desperate for a win, with the two-week international break looming. United's miserable season looked like continuing, with some embarrassing defending giving Villa a helping hand before a remarkable comeback.

‌



Goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson inside the opening four minutes had Villa in control before United fought back through Bruno Fernandes' penalty and Tielemans' equaliser to go in level at 2-2 at the break.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

But United once again shot themselves in the foot to hand Villa the initiative again. Just two minutes into the second half, Dalot clumsily tripped Alysson in the box, allowing John McGinn to make it 3-2 from the spot before even more comical defending made it 4-2.

Leny Yoro headed a free-kick towards his own goal, forcing Senne Lammens into a save, with the loose ball dropping to Leon Goretzka to score.

‌



Dorgu teed up fellow substitute Joshua Zirkzee to make it 4-3 in injury time before the Denmark international provided a late equaliser, heading in a deep corner after Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki missed the cross.

Carrick tried to freshen things up through his triple substitution and Dalot's withdrawal after a rotten performance at left-back summed up the discontent inside Old Trafford. United have now conceded 30 goals in all competitions this season, the most of any side in Europe's top five leagues, level with Crystal Palace and Sassuolo, but they at least avoided defeat.

‌



View 2 Images Diogo Dalot was consoled by Joshua Zirkzee after being substituted (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The match started with the second protest against owners the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe in a week. Supporters, who protested during the 3-2 win over Roma on Tuesday, released green and gold balloons and chanted about the owners.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were in attendance at Old Trafford. And the chaotic comeback to secure a point leaves Carrick's future unclear heading into the international break.

Sports.title: Defiant Pierre Sage responds to sack pressure after Crystal Palace hit rock bottom
Sports.content:
Defiant Pierre Sage responds to sack pressure after Crystal Palace hit rock bottom

Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parrish has been left with a decision to make on manager Pierre Sage after defeat by Liverpool left the club bottom of the Premier League

View 2 Images Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage could be sacked in the international break (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

Pierre Sage is on the brink of losing his job after Crystal Palace hit rock bottom.

‌



‌



Under-pressure Sage could be axed in the next 24 hours after Sunday's 3-1 defeat by Liverpool. Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank are strong contenders to take over, with chairman Steve Parish ready to make a call on the managerial situation.

‌



Sage insisted after Palace’s latest defeat that he could turn the situation around but the result left the club bottom of the Premier League for the first time in nine years.

‌



When asked whether he wanted to remain in charge for the forthcoming games with Coventry and Hull, Sage said: “100 per cent. I have always confidence in myself. If I’m not 100 per cent involved in what I have to do, it’s a big, big mistake.

Liverpool's patience with Alexander Isak pays off as win puts Pierre Sage on the brink READ MORE :

“I think I’m not in this situation, but for the moment how we convert what we work is not at the level we expect but I know we have to continue.

‌



“It’s not from a dream to a nightmare. I don’t have this feeling. I’m focused on my job and finding a solution. I was really happy to join this club but at the moment the results are not at the level. I know I have to push more on those things.

“I know the condition of the job, how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. I don’t have to convince people. I do my job and my job is the way to convince people, for me it’s the best thing. They just have to believe in that. If it’s not the case, they will take a decision.”

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images Liverpool went 3-0 up before Palace's late consolation (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola praised in-form Alexander Isak - who has got eight goals in all competitions - and also Alisson Becker who produced a string of fine saves. Iraola said: “Alisson was key for us with some great saves and it’s not just goals with Alex. His movement and his runs were so important.

“You want to finish with a win. It puts us in a better position but we need to keep improving. Now we are all praying because the last international break we lost three players and now, it is the last thing we need. I hope everything goes well and we don't lose anyone this time.”

But Iraola admitted there are concerns over Dominik Szoboszlai who limped off injured and is a doubt for international duty with Hungary.

Iraola added: “He did not feel 100 per cent, that’s for sure. Let’s see. He is always desperate to report up for his country. But we will make checks with the medical staff. Last time, we lost three players in the international break and we have to be careful this time.”

Sports.title: Furious Andoni Iraola slams VAR again despite Liverpool winning - 'I'm very upset'
Sports.content:
Furious Andoni Iraola slams VAR again despite Liverpool winning - 'I'm very upset'

Liverpool head into the international break on the back of a win over Crystal Palace, but Andoni Iraola refused to let Palace's late consolation from the penalty spot slide

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was furious at the decision to give Crystal Palace a penalty (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola was "very upset" after a controversial penalty decision cost Liverpool a clean sheet in victory at Crystal Palace.

‌



‌



Liverpool head into the international break fourth in the Premier League thanks to a 3-1 win at Selhurst Park. Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak made sure of the points before Eddie Nketiah netted from the spot in injury time.

‌



The consolation goal for Palace came after Milos Kerkez was penalised following a clash of heads with Dario Osorio in the box. Referee Tony Harrington pointed to the spot after the clash which occurred while both players tried to head a bouncing ball.

‌



His call was confirmed by VAR Michael Salisbury and Nketiah beat Alisson from 12 yards to get on the scoresheet. Iraola was furious last weekend after Isak was not given a penalty in the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal for a clear shirt-pull by Jurrien Timber and he made his case once again on Sunday.

"I am very upset because the ones in our box they are calling penalties and in the other box they are not. I know we are 3-0 and it's the 95th minute but I'm very upset," he told Sky Sports.

"It's a head to head but even then it's Osario to Milos. It's a clash of heads. You can say it's 3-0 but, for me, there is more because it is not the first time this season and you compare... I'm really upset.

"The VAR took a lot of time. When you call a penalty and they are two minutes. Two repetitions, three repetitions, they are finding a way not to be called by the VAR. A clean sheet is not cheap in the Premier League and we wanted to win 3-0. It is not just because of this penalty, it's because of a lot of things."

Liverpool took the lead through Mac Allister's flicked header at the near post before Wirtz tucked in Bradley Barcola's cutback on the break for 2-0. Isak showed a cool head to bury his seventh Premier League goal in nine appearances to make the points safe.

Sports.title: 'Not many sports teams have done it' - Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround
Sports.content:
Toto Wolff says he's "proud" of Mercedes' turnaround to win the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship and feels very few sports teams have bounced back so quickly.

Mercedes won their ninth constructors' title on Sunday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, five years after their last championship, which was their eighth in a row at the time.

Regulation changes in 2022 ended Mercedes' dominance as they struggled to get on top of the so-called ground effect cars, but they have won the first season of the new 2026 cars, and also wrapped up the Drivers' Championship earlier this month with Kimi Antonelli.

"The thing is when you are in these difficult moments, like we all are sometimes in our lives, it's not that easy to keep going," said Wolff.

"Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation'. But when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel.

"I think those last four years were very difficult between getting it wrong, then kind of understanding why it was wrong and then realising no we didn't understand. That was a bit back and forth.

"But we will be looking back in 10 or 20 years. When you look at the statistics, it wasn't that we were complete losers over those four years, because we finished second, (second), third, fourth [in the championship], we won races, won many races. So it wasn't that bad at all when you look at the sheer numbers, but it felt not good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff reacts to Mercedes winning the Constructors' Championship in Brazil

As Wolff points out, Mercedes still won races between 2022 and 2025, with George Russell and Lewis Hamilton winning seven Grands Prix between them.

"The resilience of the team, the people that held together in those tough times, is a factor, I think," continued Wolff.

"It feels really good sealing those two titles. Not many sports teams have done that after consecutive run of championships, then a difficult spell and then coming back, so I'm really proud that we are part of this very small group of teams that have done that in all sports."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix

Wolff: Mercedes has 2,500 superstars

Mercedes move level with Williams on nine constructors' titles - only McLaren (10) and Ferrari (16) have more in Formula 1 history.

Wolff says his pride comes from the hard work in Mercedes' UK factories in Brackley and Brixworth to produce the best car, on average, this season.

"Sometimes the drivers, or myself, we are so visible because we are in in front of the TV cameras, but there's so many people that are part of this," he told Sky Sports F1.

"I always say there are not two superstars, the drivers, but there are 2,500 superstars, all of them delivering a great job, being all of us contributing to such a championship."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reacts to Mercedes claiming their ninth world constructors championship

Mercedes were unable to finish with either of their drivers on the podium in Brazil as Lando Norris dominated in mixed conditions, while Antonelli and Russell both spun.

Russell finished in fourth, just ahead of Antonelli who says everyone at Mercedes "deserves" this year's success.

"They have done an incredible year and it's an amazing group of people, who push every day to do their best and give us the best opportunity to fight for wins and championships," the Italian told Sky Sports F1.

"This year they have done an incredible job and that's why they deserve this championship and we will enjoy it together."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell says Mercedes would've liked to win the Constructors' Championship title in style after both cars finished fourth and fifth respectively

Russell added: "We achieved what we came here to do and won the Constructors' Championship. We would have liked to have done it in a bit more style, but it's an incredible achievement for everyone in the team.

"We've had four difficult years and the whole organisation put so much work into getting us back into this position. When I joined Mercedes in 2022, we hoped we'd be fighting for championships regularly, so to have gone through that journey and now get back to the top is something we should all be incredibly proud of."

Sports.title: Hamilton says he overrode Ferrari pit call due to 'lack of information'
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says a lack of information led to him overriding Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits as rain fell during the closing stages of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Hamilton was running in eighth at Interlagos when heavy rain began to fall with 10 laps to go. While the leaders had already passed the pit entry by the time the rain intensified, Mercedes brought in George Russell from fifth.

Ferrari instructed Hamilton to come in, but he decided to do the opposite to the car just in front of him at the time, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc, running just behind him, came into the pits.

The seven-time world champion spun on the next lap in the treacherous conditions, before pitting at the end of it to follow his rivals onto intermediates.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

While there was little at stake, as Hamilton ultimately finished ninth rather than claiming what could have been seventh if he had got past Lawson, it was the latest example of imperfect execution from the British driver and his Italia team.

Speaking to Sky Italy after the race, Hamilton said: "The last bit of information I got was that the rain was going to stay the same, and in those conditions my grip was feeling pretty good.

"And I was like, 'ah, I'm catching.' And I was coming out the last corner, just before the pit lane they asked me to box, and I was right behind Lawson.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following a disappointing race, Lewis Hamilton reflects on 'tough' Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

"He went in, and I ended up staying (out). They didn't say it's raining more in the first half of the lap. If I'd have known that I would have come in.

"As soon as I got to Turn 1, I realised it was wet. So, it just lacked a little bit of information there.

"And ultimately, that's on me. Sorry for the team, for that. I gave it everything. We just didn't have the pace today unfortunately."

'A really tough day for the whole team'

Hamilton had come into the weekend off the back of a major controversy with his team-mate in Mexico last weekend, as he was angered by a first-lap clash between the pair that he felt cost him victory and the team a one-two.

While Hamilton revealed on Saturday that the pair had "squashed" their issues, the precious nature of their winning opportunity in Mexico City was highlighted by their struggles in Brazil.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two,

Both Hamilton and Leclerc were compromised by grid penalties that saw them start from 20th and 14th, respectively, but neither appeared to have the pace to match McLaren's race winner Lando Norris or Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "Really tough day and weekend for the whole team. They have done a really great job.

"All the mechanics did such a great job switching out the engine and making sure the car was as good as it could be."

Hamilton had a great start as he climbed to ninth on the first lap, and successfully pulled off being the first driver to switch from intermediates to slicks as the track dried early in the race, but didn't have the pace to take advantage of either moment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli passes Lando Norris for the lead in the opening lap at Sao Paulo GP.

He added: "We struggled in the dry but I had a great start. Unfortunately, the rear tyres just ballooned and overheated and I struggled.

"After that, I was pushing to go onto the slicks, which I eventually got on, I think I was one of the earlier ones [to switch to that tyre].

"I was feeling pretty good. It was very tricky in those conditions. We ended up having an extra stop, which ultimately, I had a lot of ground to cover there."

Sports.title: Norris wins wet Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes seal constructors' title
Sports.content:
McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship.

Max Verstappen produced a signature stunning drive in the wet to come from 21st on the grid to finish second, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar completing a double-podium for Red Bull.

Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli had looked on course for victory after taking the lead at the start but ultimately had to settle for fifth behind his team-mate George Russell, which was more than enough for Mercedes to establish an unassailable lead over Ferrari in the constructors' standings with three rounds to spare.

A ninth constructors' title for Mercedes, their first since claiming eight in a row from 2014-2021, brings the Silver Arrows level with Williams in third on the sport's all-time list of winners.

"It's amazing," Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said. "We have taken a few years to be back at the top spot. Not many teams have been able to come back from such a situation and it just shows the great work, the great people we have in our organisation and it's great to be among them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes party on the podium after sealing their ninth Constructors' Championship title.

Norris lost the lead to Antonelli at the start as the pole-sitter dropped to third on the opening lap, but a early-race switch to slick tyres as the track dried swung the race.

Antonelli had led by six seconds before the stops but delayed pitting by a lap and then struggled with his tyre temperatures, spinning off to give the lead back to Norris before also being overtaken by both Red Bulls.

The rain returned in the closing stages to force the entire field back onto intermediate tyres, but Norris handled the conditions masterfully to take the chequered flag just short of 15 seconds clear of Verstappen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli loses the lead by going off track twice to slip to third.

"It was a very tough race, very very tough," Norris said. "I didn't have the best of launches off the line. A lot of challenges today with the conditions and going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you are pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit.

"The main thing today was I kept it cool and didn't make any mistakes and had the pace when I needed to. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well."

Sao Paulo GP Result: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



4) George Russell, Mercedes



5) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



6) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



7) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



8) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari*



9) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



10) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



*Leclerc demoted a position by five-second penalty

Norris' team-mate Oscar Piastri claimed sixth, which meant McLaren matched Red Bull's haul of 33 points from the race and stayed 17 points behind them in the battle for third in the constructors' standings.

Charles Leclerc finished seventh after passing Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson during a final-lap scrap, but their positions were reversed as the Ferrari driver was given a five-second penalty for causing a collision between the pair during the overtake.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc and Liam Lawson touch on lap 70 as they battle for seventh!

Lewis Hamilton surged from 20th on the grid up to ninth on the first lap, but was ultimately unable to improve on that position after struggling for pace amid a couple of tyre gambles as the conditions changed.

Nico Hulkenberg took the final point in 10th for Audi, holding onto the position despite having to serve a penalty late in the race for forcing Alpine's Franco Colapinto off track in an earlier battle.

Rafael Camara was last of the cars to take the chequered flag in 20th for Haas as he made his grand prix debut at his home race following the team's fall out with Esteban Ocon at last weekend's race in Mexico City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris shatters champagne bottle after attempting his trademark podium celebration after winning Sao Paulo GP.

Norris stages recovery to return to winning ways

Having been the only team to bring a significant upgrade to Brazil at this late stage of the season, McLaren arrived in Sao Paulo hopeful of taking a step forward.

Norris had taken full advantage of the team's earlier upgrades to win back-to-back races either side of F1's summer break, but after being unlucky to miss out a third victory in Madrid, the Woking squad's pace has faded.

The Brit was adamant that the wet conditions qualifying took place in on Saturday were more crucial than the upgrades in enabling him to take pole, and he got his wish as the rain returned on Sunday.

However, the start was far from ideal as a poor getaway saw him fall behind both Antonelli and Lawson, who was starting from third after being promoted by grid penalties for several others.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli passes Lando Norris for the lead in the opening lap at Sao Paulo GP.

It wasn't until lap six that Norris got his tyres working well enough to pass Lawson, but he was still losing time to Antonelli, who at one point extended his lead beyond eight seconds.

As the track dried, Norris began to close the gap, before Hamilton became the first driver to switch from intermediates to soft slick tyres at the end of lap 14.

Reacting to Hamilton's strong pace, Norris pitted on lap 16, while leader Antonelli opted to stay out.

That proved to be a mistake from Mercedes as when Antonelli pitted a lap later, he came out only a second ahead of Norris, with the McLaren driver's tyres fired up and working much better than the leaders.

Just a week on from becoming F1's youngest ever world champion, the 20-year-old sounded distressed over team radio as he expressed concern that his car wasn't working properly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris wins the Sao Paulo GP ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

That soon told as he spun off at Turn 1, allowing Norris to ease into the lead, and soon allowing the Red Bulls to follow through.

Norris never looked like relinquishing the lead from that moment, showing consistently strong pace to extend his lead before calmly managing the switch back to intermediates with 10 laps to go.

Verstappen is renowned for his pace in the wet, but Norris was more than a match in the final stages, maintaining and then extending his lead to join the Dutchman and Russell on three race wins for the season.

Verstappen the star of 'reverse grid' race

Unlike some of its junior categories, F1 has not introduced a reverse grid race, where cars start in the opposite order that they have qualified.

However, there was something of a 'reverse' feel to Sunday's grid with several of the drivers at the top of the championship serving penalties for exceeding their engine part allowance for the season.

Hamilton and Verstappen were starting from 20th and 21st respectively, with Russell seventh and Leclerc 14th.

Hamilton made an incredible start to jump to ninth on the first lap, while Verstappen wasn't far behind, slotting into 10th behind the Ferrari by lap three.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok looks at how Max Verstappen went from 21st to 2nd at Interlagos.

A mistake from Hamilton allowed Verstappen past, and from that point on their races went in vastly different directions.

While Hamilton struggled for pace and had to give back one of the positions he'd gained illegally on the first lap from Haas' Oliver Bearman, Verstappen continued to surge forward.

The four-time world champion was soon up to fifth, and was gifted another place as Russell spun in the pit lane on his way back out to the track having switched to slick tyres.

Antonelli's struggles gave him another place, before Red Bull ordered Hadjar to allow his team-mate past on lap 38 as Verstappen closed in.

While there was no victory this time around, Verstappen made it eight podiums in a row and 10 in his last 11 races, a run of form that is likely to see the 29-year-old go into the winter as the favourite for next year's title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen says that despite his progression from P21 to P2 at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, his car was 'not working'.

"It was a challenging race," Verstappen said. "The first few laps were, of course, very important and I overtook a lot of cars. Actually, that first stint on the stints was very, very strong.

Sports.title: Frank leading candidate for Palace job with Sage likely to be sacked
Sports.content:
Thomas Frank has emerged as a leading candidate to take over as Crystal Palace manager if the Eagles decide to sack Pierre Sage.

Other candidates that Palace are interested in include Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Vitor Pereira, Kim Hellberg, Vitor Matos and Tony Popovic.

No decision has been taken at Palace yet, but Sage is likely to lose his position following a seventh league defeat of the season.

Frank is amongst a list of names that Palace considered in the summer. The former Brentford boss is expected to be among the frontrunners if as expected the club decide to make a managerial change.

Frank had great success at Brentford during his seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, getting the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a top-flight club, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

He then moved to Tottenham last season to replace Ange Postecolgou as head coach, but was sacked after less than eight months in charge with the club in 16th place, five points above the relegation zone.

Image: Frank's time at Tottenham was littered with setbacks

Spurs only sealed survival from relegation on the final day of last season, after Igor Tudor and Roberto De Zerbi replaced Frank as head coach.

Frank failed to win over the Tottenham faithful, with his short tenure littered with setbacks, including drinking from a coffee cup which carried the badge of rivals Arsenal.

Carragher expects Palace to sack Sage

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher speaking after Palace's 3-1 loss to Liverpool:

"I think that would have been one of the best Crystal Palace performances this season. Liverpool won 3-1 away from home but their goalkeeper was their best player. That tells you how well Palace did.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Crystal Palace’s match against Liverpool in the Premier League.

"But I don't think you can hang your hat on the performance, especially with a new guy into the Premier League. He's really struggled so far.

"I don't think you can take the risk as an owner when you think of the finances involved. Palace - 14 seasons in the Premier League, we don't expect them to be [bottom]. They're an established Premier League club.

"I think the decision will be made, unfortunately for Pierre Sage. I think Palace will have a new manager the next time they play in the Premier League"

Sage: 'We haven't had our rewards'

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage to Sky Sports after the loss to Liverpool:

"I always say the same thing about what we deserve and what we have.

"We start really well, we create a lot of chances but without scoring and taking this goal [against] after a set-piece with the consequence of transition, it's really difficult against Liverpool because they have a lot of speed and are really efficient in transition.

"That's why we suffered more in the second half. We tried to make it 1-1 but we left too much space and they took it.

"Football is about efficiency. If we create these chances, it's a good step. But the next step is to score. If not, it's as [if] you did nothing.

"I'm really frustrated, especially for the fans and the players, because I think we're able to do better."

Sports.title: Man Utd in relegation zone but boss Carrick 'expects' to stay on
Sports.content:
Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick "expects" to stay on despite his side sitting in the relegation zone after Sunday's dramatic 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa.

Man Utd scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point against Villa, but the draw leaves Carrick's side third-bottom and a point from safety.

Man Utd's 18th-place position is their lowest after 10 top-flight games since 1986/87, when they were 20th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester United and Aston Villa

The draw against Villa extends Man Utd's winless run in the league to eight games - a club record in the Premier League era - raising further doubts over Carrick's position heading into the two-week November international break.

When questioned on his future by Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick engaged in a tetchy back-and-forth, insisting he would remain in charge.

PD: "What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? If you thought walking away was the best thing, you'd probably do it."

MC: "It's not going to happen, no."

PD: "What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?

MC: "Is there?"

PD: "You would assume so, right?

MC: "Would you?"

PD: "What do you think, Michael?"

MC: "You're telling me what you think, aren't you?"

PD: "I'm asking you what you think? What do you expect to happen?"

MC: "We understand the situation; we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward and keep working on things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man Utd fans show their love for Michael Carrick at full-time after the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa

Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season.

"One hundred per cent," he said. "I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and we've got to deal with it and it's something we have to improve on drastically. But there's more than enough, we're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times…

"I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We've just got to win games."

"Football is about moments, football is about what happens in both boxes in the end," Carrick added.

"Take (away) the moments and the totally avoidable goals we've given away, I actually thought we played pretty well, we were the better team for the most part and I'm disappointed we haven't won the game."

Neville: 'Ownership don't have a clue what to do' on Carrick

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Gary Neville, speaking on NBC, delivered a scathing assessment of Manchester United's leadership

Sky Sports' Gary Neville on NBC:

"You can keep changing the manager and thinking that's going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years - that's not the answer.

"Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don't know. The ownership don't have a clue what to do.

"It's rinse and repeat. (Ruben) Amorim, (Erik) Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick - some of them are world-class managers who have had success; there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well.

"None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you've got a poor performance department, a poor recruitment department, you've not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club, you will fail.

"Every organisation in the world will fail if you've not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom - your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

"There are real issues within that football club; you've got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions."

Keane: 'Politician' Carrick 'better get moving' on improvements

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ex-Man Utd players Roy Keane and Ashley Young discuss whether top players would still consider joining the club

Sky Sports' Roy Keane:

"It's obviously difficult for the manager. Under pressure, no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn't say much. I don't know if that's a tactic. Like a politician.

"He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there's things we need to work on, but they better get moving on that.

"It's the worst start in how many years; all these stats aren't very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it's just going to continue.

"What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.

"I admire people who are maybe casual. I wish I was casual like that! I see Carrick, and he's like, 'We just have to tighten up'. I'm going, 'Tighten up? You should be banging heads!'

"We're all different, but put it this way, they're going to Liverpool in a few weeks. How many chances are Liverpool going to get? I don't think this is a top Liverpool team, but do you believe United are going to roll their sleeves up and get a clean sheet? Dig in deep? Be hard to beat? Start quick? Well, good luck with that one.

"I don't see that as an honest dressing room. The really top players put demands on each other. They all seem to be tiptoeing around each other.

"They are certainly lacking leaders in the dressing room."

Sports.title: Villa boss Emery explains why he went down tunnel before full-time
Sports.content:
A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end.

Villa threw away two separate two-goal leads to draw 4-4 with United in a Super Sunday thriller - but the 97th-minute equaliser from Michael Carrick's side, scored by Patrick Dorgu, brought about a strange reaction from Emery.

The Villa manager was seen walking down the tunnel before the full-time whistle, with the match continuing for another two minutes before it ended.

Image: Unai Emery went down the Old Trafford tunnel before the full-time whistle

Villa have complained about the legitimacy of United's fourth goal - with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens accused of impeding with Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he competed with Dorgu for the corner.

Asked if Emery walking down the tunnel was due to the emotional about the goal standing "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing."

When asked if he felt the goal being awarded was unfair, Emery replied: "No, no. Not unfair. Please.

"They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off."

Full transcript of Emery's prickly interview

Sky reporter Patrick Davison: Does today happen because you're a new team or young side? It is an experience they have to learn from?

Unai Emery: "I don't know."

PD: Does history play a part, we spoke before the match that Aston Villa don't have a good record here.

UE: "We are in our way and we might be positive, even with this defeat [draw]. We have to be moving on with the process we have."

PD: We saw you left...

UE: "More, more, more questions?"

PD: Last one Unai, we saw you left before the end while VAR were...

UE: "They scored in minute 96!"

PD: Just emotion?

UE: "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I think the match was finishing."

PD: You brought something up that I wasn't expecting. Did you think the goal was unfair?

UE: "No, no. Not unfair. Please."

PD: Ok, I'm listening.

UE: "They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.

"My English is so poor, but it's clear or not?"

PD: No, you've explained it well.

UE: "Ok. Thank you, thank you very much. More questions?"

PD: No all done.

UE: "No? Thank you very much. Have a good Sunday."

Villa chief complains about equaliser standing

Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany took to social media to show his dismay at United's last-gasp equaliser against his team being allowed to stand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane and Ashley Young analyse whether Senne Lammens impeded Zion Suzuki in the build-up to Manchester Utd's late equaliser against Aston Villa.

United goalkeeper Lammens - who went up for the corner - made contact with Suzuki whilst not looking at the ball, which left Villa furious. VAR checked and cleared Lammens' involvement in the goal.

Sky Sports' Roy Keane says "football is a contact sport" which means the goal should be allowed to stand.

However, Vidagany posted on X: "To put in context this convenient narrative of 'contact sport' we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

"Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

"Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve.

"But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact."

Is Emery angry with his players?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester United and Aston Villa.

Emery admitted his anger at seeing Villa throw away their significant advantages at Old Trafford - but revealed his anger was not directed at his players.

"Angry, of course," he said in his press conference. "To accept to lose in the last minutes two goals, it is difficult.

"I am angry for the situation, not with the players. We lost the opportunity to have two points more."

Asked how United were allowed to come back into the game, Emery replied: "They did the same here against Roma with the supporters pushing, they were playing with heart.

"The last moments when we were close to finishing the match, with [Patrick] Dorgu left side, we couldn't defend him good.

"The last corner we were focusing on the adaptation, protecting them to try to avoid the block. Zion [Suzuki] is going to improve, adapting to the Premier League, but during the process we conceded one more.

"But Zion is very fantastic how he is performing."

Sports.title: ‘I expect to move forward’: Carrick denies risk of Manchester United sack
Sports.content:
A tetchy Michael Carrick dismissed a suggestion he could resign as head coach for the good of the team after Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left Manchester United in the relegation zone heading into the international window.

Carrick’s side sit in 18th place with eight points from 10 games and have won only once, in August at home to Ipswich, in the league this season. It is now a club record eight Premier League games without a win.His job remains in the balance due to the dismal run of form.

Carrick was asked on Sky Sports if he was considering his position. “I’m not,” said the 45-year-old, who was curt when the interviewer said that it was clear there would be conversations regarding his future before United’s next game, which is away to Liverpool on 22 November.

“Is there?” he replied. “You’re telling me. I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games. We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on and showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.”

Quick Guide How do I 

Carrick insisted he is seeing enough in United’s play. “Yeah, 100%. I think there’s more than enough,” he said. “Goals change games and you’ve got to deal with it, and it’s part of something we have to improve on drastically, but there’s more than enough. We’re just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times.”

Villa scored after 59 seconds through Alysson before Nicolas Jackson gave them a 2-0 lead after just four minutes – with goalkeeper Senne Lammens culpable for both goals.

Despite Bruno Fernandes, from the penalty spot, and Youri Tielemans pulling United back all square by the break, further mistakes from Diogo Dalot and Leny Yoro allowed John McGinn and Leon Goretzka to make it 4-2 to Villa. Dalot’s clumsy foul on Alysson conceded a penalty that McGinn converted and Yoro’s header towards his own goal led to Villa’s messy fourth for Goretzka.

In stoppage time, goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued an unlikely point for United.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

When Dalot was replaced in the second half, the makeshift left-back was jeered by some United fans. The manager was asked if he could understand the supporters’ reaction. Carrick said: “We’ve got to be careful with that, I understand the frustration of the supporters, so I get it. We’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that. Diogo, he gives absolutely everything.”

Unai Emery was also left upset, Villa’s manager suggesting that Dorgu’s 96th-minute headed equaliser should not have stood as Lammens, up for a last-gasp corner, knocked into his opposite number, Zion Suzuki. Emery said: “How we lost [our way] the last six minutes at the time, conceding two goals is very frustrating. The keeper, as well, is adapting but he still has work to do and how we have to defend when they are blocking us. In another country, maybe it’s a foul but here it’s not.

“I am disappointed but we move on. I have to analyse this match. It is very important to analyse deeply. First half, we started very good, but they were pushing. We were resilient. We tried to change. We started very well, scoring two goals again.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace poised to sack Pierre Sage and target Frank after Liverpool defeat
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace are poised to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday’s defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017, with Thomas Frank emerging as the main candidate to succeed him.

The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has been under mounting pressure since a 5-0 defeat by Brighton last month. There have been few signs of improvement as Palace have slumped to four successive league defeats.

Sage has guided Palace to only two wins from their 10 Premier League games this season and they have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far. Although there were promising moments during the 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, their habit of conceding goals from set pieces has not been rectified and it is understood the patience of the club’s hierarchy has worn thin despite Sage only being at the helm for 16 matches.

He is expected to become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season on Monday. Palace are already believed to have started the process of bringing in his replacement. Frank, who was dismissed by Tottenham in February, spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford.

The former Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche also has his backers at Palace and would be seen as a safe pair of hands given his vast experience in the Premier League. Vítor Pereira, another former Forest manager, could be an alternative.

Sage signed a three-year contract in south London after leaving Lens, where he won the Coupe de France and qualified for the Champions League in his final season. Palace have lost their two main central defenders this year, Marc Guéhi moving to Manchester City in January and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea in the summer. Two loan players – Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor – were signed as replacements. Palace did not land one of Sage’s top targets, Malick Fofana.

Sage denied after the Liverpool game that his dream job had turned into a “nightmare” but suggested that Palace’s squad needed investment in January. “We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions,” he said.

Sports.title: Le Fée’s penalty stuns Chelsea and breathes life into defiant Sunderland
Sports.content:
A lot can change in five‑and‑a‑half months, but as an early winter chill descended on Wearside last week – both meteorologically and ­metaphorically – Sunderland were determined that some things should remain the same. Just as they had beaten Chelsea on the final day of last season to ensure European qualification for the first time in 53 years, they did so again on Sunday to lift themselves off the bottom of the Premier League.

The Sunderland performance was certainly familiar to their head coach, Régis Le Bris – “the identity, the intensity, the togetherness, the way we managed the game” – on the way to three crucial points.

Ultimately a patched-up defence, ­without the injured Dan Ballard and the banned Omar Alderete, kept ­Chelsea at enough distance to allow Robin Roefs a tranquil ­afternoon amid the tumult. Chelsea may be ­developing into a ­chaotic must‑watch under Xabi Alonso but they were ­subdued here and have fallen out of the top four. “We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win,” Alonso said. “We lacked a bit of patience and creativity.”

Margins were paper-thin in a game decided by two first-half penalty calls, the first not awarded to Chelsea after Luke O’Nien’s clumsy challenge on Cole Palmer, deemed after video assistant referee consideration to be fractionally outside the area, and the second given to the hosts by Jarred Gillett after Levi Colwill brought down the ebullient Brian Brobbey; the defender argued, not without justification, that the Dutch striker had a handful of his shirt too but the award stood.

Alonso, as ever, made no excuses, ­focusing not on the officiating and more on how he was “not happy with how we defended that situation”. Enzo Le Fée had been equally unequi­vocal just beyond the half‑hour, sending Mike Penders the wrong way and dispatching into the goalkeeper’s bottom-right corner for the game’s only goal.

Europe may be a blessing for Sunderland but the full-time mood had been bleak after the latest alarming performance in the home defeat against Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday. It had felt like a season watershed and only the captain, Granit Xhaka, Thomas Meunier and Roefs survived the cull here. That the talismanic Xhaka, the subject of strong summer interest from his former coach Alonso, had his afternoon truncated by injury after less than three ­minutes, felt like yet more of the ill fortune dogging Sunderland.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland’s Reinildo Mandava attempts to wrestle the ball away from Morgan Rogers. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

There was no feeling sorry for themselves, though. With this the start of a challenging quartet of fixtures leading into the Tyne‑Wear derby next month, it felt like this match had to be attacked to prevent an early-season hiccup turning into a full mid‑season tangle with relegation trouble. And Chelsea were greeted with determination and ­aggression, with Xhaka’s withdrawal not ­blowing that plan off course. Two zesty ­incisions by Chemsdine Talbi in the opening quarter-hour, in his first ­Premier League start this season, caused Alonso’s men flutters, the first leading to a blocked Trai Hume shot and the second presenting Brobbey with a clear opening that he would have expected to convert.

The passion was there, the precision maybe less so. O’Nien’s challenge on Palmer elicited a penalty appeal that did not end up being costly after the VAR check and Morgan Rogers headed wide from a Marco Palestra cross, but Chelsea could not capitalise on any potential home nerves. If anyone was prone to belated Halloween frights it was the Blues, particularly at the hands of Brobbey, who led the line with enormous presence. He took on and beat the last man Wesley Fofana before steering his shot just too high, past Penders’ near post, and then won the penalty that led to Le Fée’s winner. “He is stoppable,” Alonso said, “but only when you defend better than we did.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Such was Chelsea’s bluntness in the first 45 that the coach opted for not just a substitution but a reshuffle at the break, with Estêvão replacing the injured Colwill, beefing up the attack with Moisés Caicedo slotting into the defence. Sunderland continued to fight tooth and nail in a game that threatened occasionally to bubble over. Meunier was booked for a late tackle on Caicedo and shortly afterwards Brobbey was cautioned for wrestling Roméo Lavia to the ground, a continuation of an ongoing feud between the pair. When he was substituted, spent, for the ­enduringly ­popular Wilson Isidor halfway through the second half Chelsea must have breathed a sigh of relief.

Estêvão made one burst through the middle on to a Rogers pass but Reinildo Mandava stepped across to snuff out the opportunity. Yet even with little possession Sunderland looked sharper. A ball broke for Isidor after Chelsea failed to clear Le Fée’s through ball, Penders saving and the rebound not breaking for the Frenchman before Pep Chavarría cleared.

As the last 10 minutes approached Alonso sent on Geovany Quenda for Chavarría, and the young winger finally conjured a goal attempt worthy of the description, fizzing a shot just wide of Roefs’s far post via deflection. Talbi, finishing as he started, pinged one just wide from distance on the break as the home side still looked more likely, even with a third of possession. Sunderland had rewarded their crowd’s vociferous faith.

Sports.title: Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second
Sports.content:
Who can stop Brighton’s ­ascension in English and European football? They are setting standards, ­practices ­leaving almost everybody else ­trailing in their wake. A ­second‑place position in the ­Premier League would once have read like a glitch in a ­Football ­Manager ­session. Not in November 2026, where they appear the only team capable of throwing down any sort of challenge to Arsenal.

Under low winter sun, Brentford, an opposition to which Brighton are often, if lazily, compared, were ­swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’s team, and their fans at the Amex ­Stadium, could level blame at a couple of ­refereeing decisions, they received little chance of rescuing anything. Brighton squeezed them, toyed with them.

If Pascal Gross, scorer of a perfectly hit penalty, attempted to dampen expectations of a title challenge, his manager, Fabian Hürzeler, allowed fans to dream. “They should always be excited, it’s our job to make them excited,” he said.

A successful return to the Amex Stadium following five Brighton away trips, more than 5,000 miles on the road including victories at ­Manchester City and Getafe over the past two outings. Brentford returned to a stadium where they have never won in the Premier League. Normal service was duly resumed, any Brighton negatives coming in a failure to add to their first-half goals.

An up-and-under straight from the kick-off was a rare Brentford foray into the Brighton box. Bart Verburggen catching it on the full prefaced an easy afternoon for the Brighton goalkeeper. There are many further dimensions to ­Hürzeler’s team. Last week Paul Scholes, an unlikely ­progressive, declared himself an admirer of a “level of ­coaching” he suggested is ­unsurpassed in ­English football. “The one thing that is non‑negotiable is to always put the team first,” Hürzeler said.

View image in fullscreen Brighton were already 1-0 down when the VAR upgraded Igor Thiago’s yellow card to a red. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Diego Gómez’s opener was not as spectacular as the halfway-line goal of the season against Crystal Palace but a beauty nonetheless. Caressing the ball first with his left and then with his right, he laid up a thrash past Caoimhín Kelleher. Its trajectory was unerring, unstoppable. Hürzeler revealed: “Yesterday, he changed to shooting with [his] left foot … I couldn’t see him scoring with his left foot. I asked him after where this quality came from.”

The path to a commanding win opened up. Igor Thiago did not last many ­minutes beyond his failed attempt to lob ­Verburggen. Scuffling in midfield with Chema Andrés, his shove was first ruled a yellow by the referee, Michael Oliver. In stepped the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell: “violent conduct” and “with force” was the verdict from Stockley Park.

Afterwards, Andrews was ­visibly unhappy: “We’ve lost two games and both when down to 10 men. So we need to analyse ourselves first. In both scenarios we can do better. In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation.”

Infact, both Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt were dismissed against Liverpool, and if Andrews rues such lapses of discipline he was more unhappy at the initial decision’s video-assisted overturn: “The game is in a state now of a place I don’t particularly like.”

Straying beyond the confines of his technical area in a manner likely to add him to Mikel Arteta’s “massive storage of images” of such breaches, Andrews asked his team to dig deep but Brighton’s dominance of possession became near-total.

Luka Vuskovic, ­serving ­previously as a deep-lying playmaker, won the penalty. Keane Lewis-Potter’s ­panicked response to a physical 18-yard box mismatch was to snatch at the ­Croatian’s shirt. Gross’s penalty was struck as truly as Gómez’s goal. “We need to be cuter,” Andrews said. “I take real pride in the way we defend set pieces and we need to do better because that wasn’t good.”
