View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross’ penalty was unsaveable. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Andrews’s half-time ­adjustments, bringing on Yarmolyuk and Nathan Collins, was an attempt to protect Brentford’s goal difference. Brighton continued to pile on pressure, their ­possession share reaching beyond 75%. A set piece became Brentford’s sole route back, though Mathias Jensen’s diagonal into ­Verbruggen’s hands would not have passed muster in rugby’s Nations Championship.

Ironic cheers from the away end came when Brentford won a corner, and then another – rare excitement at Brighton’s defenders being asked to do something other than build an attack. The visitors’ fighting spirit at least sustained, though threatened to spill over. When Kevin Schade shoved ­Vuskovic to the ground by the touchline, another red card was a possibility, only for Oliver and Attwell to rule a yellow as sufficient this time.

Brighton’s push for honours and further horizons will require more than spectacular goals. “You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results – we are not ­getting carried away yet,” Gross said. “Every game we have to suffer a lot.”

Hürzeler, like Andrews constantly straying beyond the confines of his technical area, does not countenance any let-ups. When Brighton meet the unstinting demands of their coach, so many are left in their wing mirrors.

Sports.title: Evanilson ignites eighth straight Bournemouth win at blundering Ipswich
Sports.content:
Marco Rose paid tribute to his Bournemouth side after a hard‑fought 2-1 victory at Ipswich equalled the club’s record of eight consecutive wins.

Evanilson got the ball rolling after five minutes, scoring for a fifth successive Premier League match. With seven goals this season, he has already beaten his tally from the whole of last season.

His latest was a gift from the Ipswich goalkeeper, Christian Walton, who tried and failed to dribble past ­him in the area, and Bournemouth went two up after 27 seconds of the second half when Leif Davis could only deflect Ryan Christie’s strike into his own net.

Lewis Cook tripped Abdoul ­Ouattara in the area to provide the hosts with a lifeline and Jack Clarke scored the penalty with 17 minutes left to set up a grandstand finish at Portman Road.

However, Bournemouth stood firm to make it eight wins in a row and match the record set under Eddie Howe in 2012-13, a season which ended with promotion from League One.

Speaking after a win which came three days after a victorious journey to Sparta Prague, Rose said: “I am pleased with the first 70 minutes because we went two up and I didn’t feel like we struggled or can get any problems, but it’s [the] Premier League and one goal changed the momentum of the game.

“That is why I am much more pleased with the last 20 minutes. We suffered but we did it together.”

A slow start last month at Chelsea proved costly for Bournemouth, and even in last weekend’s 2-0 home win against Leeds the visitors had an effort ruled out after 11 minutes. That made goals at the start of each half particularly sweet for Rose.

“Last week I said we start slow and this week I said we start quite quick and score an early goal. I am a magician!” the German said with a smile. “No, we know we have to be ready in this league. We played Chelsea four weeks ago and we were two down after three minutes. That’s why we learned and always good to score an early goal.

“We were sharp, we were good and that’s what I really appreciate. I said before this week that it’s going to be really demanding for a team that is not used to have this kind of [­European] situation.”

Julio Enciso went close late on with two free‑kicks, but this defeat means Ipswich have only won one of their last seven in all competitions.

Gary O’Neil, their manager, said: “[We are] gutted with the result, firstly, because it’s what we are here for and probably performance-wise not much in it. To lose a football match you’ve not been outclassed in is hard to take. But if you give the ball to the opposition No 9 twice, it’s going to be difficult and that was the story of the game really.

“It’s the level so we have to find a way of not only being competitive in games, but can we now find a way to make sure these Hull [a 2-2 draw] and Bournemouth performances are four points and not one.”

Sports.title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid
Sports.content:
They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, in which they might have wondered if something was not right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test and a proper game, 10 World Cup winners on the field and first place awaiting the winner, and at the end of an intense enjoyable night, that was Hansi Flick’s side.

At a noisy Metropolitano, the atmosphere matching the occasion, against a frenetic Atlético side that went for the throat, Barcelona trailed to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frenzied first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of the break leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond the points. It hadn’t been easy but they had made it; ultimately, they might conclude they had found a way to manage it too, some satisfaction in the suffering, in how they resisted and re-established control amid the chaos.

“The lesson is that when you can finish it, you have to,” Jan Oblak said afterwards but there was no real reproach. The Atlético goalkeeper insisted that his team would do it again, and that they weren’t going to give up. After seven successive wins, they lost but they had certainly competed; another lesson might be that both of these teams are in the title race, not just Barcelona. Simeone Sr might agree with his son that in the first half the plan had been executed to “perfection”. He might also concede that in the second they found the ball taken from them.

Atlético flew into this, fuelled by the noise. They did more inside three minutes than in 90 against Bayern Munich in midweek. A superb clearance from Pau Cubarsí denied them in the first minute. Álex Baena curled wide in the second. And they forced a corner in the third. Barcelona were overwhelmed and exposed, unable to settle, and Diego Simeone’s side could sense it.

They could see it too, all that space behind the visiting defence, and soon Koke released Julián Álvarez into it. He had a long way to run and a long time to think. Perhaps too long. Was this the moment for the striker who had wanted to join Barcelona in the summer but been forced to stay, redemption and forgiveness laid before him? As he raced into the area, he opted to go round Joan García but the goalkeeper stretched and just about Álvarez was facing the goal again, sufficient Barcelona players had recovered to clear.

Quick Guide European roundup: Fans injured after stand gave way Show A Norwegian top-tier match between Tromso and Bodø/Glimt was interrupted yesterday when a panel in the away fans’ stand gave way, sending some supporters tumbling below. Norwegian broadcaster NRK said several Bodø/Glimt supporters fell through, with four receiving medical attention including one who was hospitalised. The game at Tromso’s stadium later resumed after the incident in the 41st minute, with Bodø/Glimt going on to win 2-0. “Four people were confirmed to be involved, and one of them has been taken to the hospital,” a Tromso statement said. The family of the hospitalised man told NRK that he had sustained fractured ribs. In Serie A, Inter brought Como crashing down to earth as first-half goals from Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram earned them a 2-0 home win. Como continued their remarkable debut season in Europe on Wednesday by thrashing Lens 9-1, but Cesc Fabregas’ side turned in a lacklustre display at San Siro as their six-game winning run in all competitions was halted. The victory means Inter are only one point behind leaders Lazio, who drew 1-1 away to Napoli. The Rome side remain unbeaten after nine matches, despite an own goal from Alfonso Pedraza in the second half. That came after Davide Frattesi had scored a first-half goal to put the visitors ahead. Milan are up to fourth place after beating Genoa 2-1, with Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic scoring the goals inside the first 20 minutes. Equalisers from Nick Woltemade and Gleison Bremer earned Juventus a 2-2 draw against Fiorentina. Lille remain two points behind Ligue 1 leaders Paris Saint-Germain after beating Rennes 2-1, while Monaco were denied victory against Le Mans after a 90th-minute equaliser from Erwan Colas. Lens’ week did not improve, with Marseille claiming a late winner in a 2-1 victory. In the Bundesliga, Freiburg climbed to third with a 2-0 win against struggling Union Berlin, while Bayer Leverkusen were 2-1 winners away at Cologne. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Not for long. From the corner, Marc Pubill thudded a header against the bar and although Barcelona did the same at the other end when Lamine Yamal and Pedri combined for the latter to shoot, Atlético soon had the lead. It started with a superb crossfield ball to open up the right wing where Marcos Llorente and Lee Kang-in worked the space for the Korean to guide a pass to Álvarez coming in off the other wing. He immediately returned it across the face of the box where Simeone Jr was thundering in at top speed, which is the speed he always runs at. From seven yards, without breaking his frantic stride, he scored.

The Metropolitano erupted. They had only been playing 10 minutes but this was no more than Atlético deserved and they kept on coming back for more. Every time they changed the direction of play, space yawned before them. Baena was going at Barcelona on the left, Alejandro Grimaldo joining him. Lee did the same on the right, Llorente with him. Pablo Barrios was taking a grip in the middle. As for Simeone, he was everywhere, screeching about the pitch like a cartoon whirlwind, arms and legs occasionally visible sticking out of a wild dust cloud. As for Álvarez, he moved smartly through the chaos.

Álvarez might have added a goal to his assist, his shot escaping under García and almost over the line. He also set up a wonderful opportunity for David Hancko, alone in front of goal, but the effort slipped just wide. Then Lee’s shot was stopped by García.

View image in fullscreen Giuliano Simeone fires Atlético Madrid into a first-half lead. Photograph: Susana Vera/Reuters

Barcelona could be grateful the lead was only one still. Would be, in fact. They were almost level on half an hour when Lamine Yamal slipped in – the angle was tight and from close range he hit the side-netting – and on 45 minutes, they were level. There was still a vulnerability when Atlético leapt out, but Barcelona had begun to get a bit of the ball, edging their way into the game and equalising it too. Pedri drove at the Atlético defence, neat footwork taking him through a tight passageway to find Fermín. There was fortune in the deflection off Pubill but the finish was superb.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Half-time came as a reset; with the storm seen out and Frenkie de Jong introduced, Barcelona started the second period better. Pushing Atlético back, the press better applied now, the ball was moved with more precision and more comfort too. Twice Lamine Yamal let fly and twice Pubill had to intercept as Barcelona began to impose.

And yet the best opportunity in those opening minutes fell to Álvarez on 55. Running through, he lifted his shot over García and over the bar, his shot at redemption gone and replaced by frustration and renewed doubts instead. Baena would be played in by Álvarez too but, as if shocked to find the ball landing at his feet all alone by the far post, he hesitated. Unsure what to do, his attempt at scooping the ball up to Alexander Sørloth didn’t come off.

Tiredness afforded Barcelona a little more time and space now, the threat from Atlético far less insistent while theirs increased: by fulltime they would have racked up 19 shots. And when Fermín made yet another sharp, darting run on 66 minutes, Lamine Yamal played a clever, perfectly weighted pass into the area for him to cut the shot past Oblak for his second of the night, his eighth of the season.

It wasn’t over, the feeling that the olés from the visiting fans were premature and tempting fate reinforced when Pubill ran through and found Álvarez, whose deflected shot looped over. Yet Flick’s side had this where they wanted it, his changes underlining that the priority now was a control which they exercised to the end, Atlético’s fire put out. At the whistle, they embraced, exhausted as an ovation went round. They had been in a fight and there will be more to come, but Barcelona were still standing top at the end of it.

Sports.title: Russo on target again as double fires under-pressure Arsenal to vital WSL win at Liverpool
Sports.content:
If a good striker can always get their team out of a hole, Alessia Russo is doing her best to drag Arsenal out of a deep chasm of uncertainty. Her two goals gave the ­under‑pressure Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, some brief respite with a much-needed, albeit still rather unconvincing victory.

Russo’s double took her impressive recent tally to seven goals in her past four appearances. Her goals were priceless for an Arsenal team who arrived on Merseyside with just one win in their previous seven Women’s Super League games. They will be relieved to have won after Liverpool posed plenty of problems and the hosts were unhappy about a ­disallowed goal.

Arsenal began the match brightly, with Lisa Baum’s effort deflecting on to the bar and Olivia Smith firing over from a tight angle. They were rewarded when a good move down their right led to Emily Fox’s cross being angled into the net by Russo’s incisive first-time finish.

Liverpool were level six minutes later, though, and from a defensive point of view it was a familiarly exasperating story for Arsenal, who have conceded from simple long balls through the middle ­several times this season.

They exerted very little pressure as Liverpool found Natalia Ramos in space and her direct ball picked out Beata Olsson up front, with the Arsenal centre-backs Steph Catley and Leah Williamson positioned so far apart that they were almost in different time zones, ­playing Olsson onside. Liverpool’s central striker did enough to keep the ball away from Williamson and lash her strike into the bottom corner.

A curling Ramos free-kick was tipped on to the bar by the Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez, before the game’s most contentious moment left Liverpool feeling ­understandably aggrieved. Jenna Clark tucked the ball into the net at the far post after ­Arsenal failed to clear a corner, but the assistant referee disallowed the goal for offside against Vivien ­Endemann, despite the delivery towards the player having been ­inadvertently played off an Arsenal foot rather than being a deliberate forward pass from the home side, who looked baffled.

That seemed to wake Arsenal from their slumber, however, and ­Caitlin Foord went close before Russo restored Arsenal’s lead in the final minute of the first half, as her downward header from Baum’s cross was too precise for Khiara Keating to reach. Slegers praised Russo, as she said: “She’s in top form. The two goals are such clean finishes. She picks up really good positions in the box.”

After a very watchable first half for neutrals, the second half was comparatively less entertaining but still tense as Liverpool fought to try to force an equaliser. They almost found it in the 89th minute but Gareth Taylor had his head in his hands in disbelief after Cornelia Kapocs volleyed wide from a glorious, unmarked position in front of goal. Arsenal clung on.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool are now winless in five league games but their defender Grace Fisk, who signed a new contract on Saturday, said: “There were so many positives. We made them very uncomfortable for large parts of the game. It’s just the bits in both boxes right now that are letting us down.” ­Taylor, Liverpool’s head coach, agreed: “­Performance‑wise, I couldn’t ask for any more from the girls.”

Slegers, who next has a ­daunting trip to face the European champions Barcelona, said: “The way we defended at the end of the game, for our lives, with so much passion and pride for the shirt, that ball wasn’t going to go in.”

Sports.title: FA Cup roundup: Seventh-tier Wimborne shock Crawley to reach second round
Sports.content:
Seventh-tier Wimborne heaped more misery on Crawley as the bottom side in the Football League lost 2-0 in the biggest upset of the FA Cup first round.

The Dorset part-timers took the lead after only nine minutes when the property surveyor Yang Seung-woo curled a superb strike from just inside the penalty area into the top corner.

Crawley came close to equalising when Kai Jennings flashed a low shot narrowly wide before Jonny Russell headed tamely into the arms of the home goalkeeper Cam Plain.

Crawley’s interim manager, Kevin Blackwell, made a triple change at half-time and Charlie Barker fired inches wide for the team 57 places above their hosts in the pyramid. The Southern Premier League South side got a huge slice of luck to seal victory 11 minutes from time. Jackson King’s shot hit Cameron Munn to send the ball squirming beyond the former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone.

Will Sutton scored a dramatic extra-time winner for Oldham as Dave Challinor’s first game in charge of Sheffield Wednesday ended in an upset. The homegrown central defender was up for a free-kick which the Owls failed to clear, with Sutton left completely free to nod home from six yards and secure a 2-1 win.

Calum Kavanagh put Oldham ahead in the 66th minute with a fierce drive after Mike Fondop headed on Noah Chilvers’ right-wing cross. Wednesday equalised 10 minutes later through the former Oldham forward Davis Keillor-Dunn.

The match ignited further in the 84th minute following a touchline fracas involving a large number of players. The Oldham manager, Micky Mellon, was sent off and Sheffield Wednesday’s Callum Slattery was booked. After Sutton’s winning goal, Oldham defended resolutely to close out the game.

Stafford Rangers were denied a historic win after losing 3-2 on penalties to Grimsby after they drew 3-3 after extra time. Two goals from firefighter Darrhyl Mason and one from the Aston Villa youth coach Jack Birch got the eighth-tier side – 89 places below League Two Grimsby – to a shootout.

Mason and Birch had put Rangers 2-0 ahead in front of a crowd of 3,130 at the Stan Robinson Stadium as they chased the second round for the first time since 2007. But set-piece headers inside three minutes from Harvey Rodgers and Maldini Kacurri sent the tie into extra time, where Mason and Géza Turi traded goals.

View image in fullscreen Stafford Rangers’ Luca Navarro (right) appears dejected after missing the deciding penalty. Photograph: Gary Oakley/PA

The home debutant Luca Navarro had to score to send the tie into sudden death but saw his spot-kick saved by Harvey Cartwright to end Rangers’ nine-match Cup marathon.

Lewis Fiorini’s extra-time penalty sent Stockport, who are second in League One, into the second round after they came from two goals down with 10 men to win 3-2 against Cray Wanderers.

Despite being 112 places below their opponents in the pyramid, it was the Isthmian Premier side Cray who took the lead after 21 minutes when Sammie MacLeod found the bottom corner.

Stockport were then reduced to 10 men in the 31st minute as goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond was sent off for a dangerous challenge on John Ufuah. Alex Hernández bent a brilliant strike into the top corner from the resulting free-kick.

Depleted Stockport pulled one back in the 81st minute when Kyle Wootton tscored with a header. And the Hatters then sent the tie into extra time when Mikael Mandron was in the right place to nod home Jack Diamond’s cross. The decisive moment came in the 101st minute when Cray goalkeeper JJ Briggs clattered into Mandron to give away a penalty, which was dispatched by Fiorini.

Charlie Savage scored against his father’s team as Reading eased into the second round with a 5-0 rout of Peterborough at the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

This all-League One tie turned out to be one of the most one-sided of the day, with the Peterborough manager, Robbie Savage, watching on in disbelief as his side were pulled apart.

Reading went ahead after 26 minutes as slick passing led to Andy Rinomhota playing in Daniel Kyerewaa, who found the bottom corner via a deflection. Reading doubled their lead in the 34th minute when a cross from Haydon Roberts was met by a diving header from top scorer Jack Marriott.

It was in effect game over in first-half stoppage time as Savage deepened his father’s misery when he took possession after the ball ran off Marriott, his deflected effort finding the top corner.

Jamie Reid added a fourth for the visitors in the 72nd minute when Paudie O’Connor nodded Savage’s free-kick into his path for him to lift over the Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass. Reading struck yet again four minutes later when Liam Fraser’s pass put Reid clean through to score his second.

Non-league Kidderminster breezed into the second round with a convincing 3-0 victory over League One Doncaster.

The National League club opened the scoring after 22 minutes when Maz Kouhyar pulled the ball back to Lewis Walker, and he fired home at the second attempt after his initial shot had hit the upright.

View image in fullscreen David Davis celebrates a goal in Kidderminster’s FA Cup upset victory. Photograph: Matty Paddock

The Harriers striker continued to cause problems, putting an effort over the bar and another just wide, but in the 36th minute he turned provider, charging upfield before teeing up Kouhyar and the on-loan Notts County midfielder slotted home. Kouhyar was again involved in the third goal, having a shot that Josh Clarke could only parry and David Davis turned in the rebound.

The Kidderminster manager, Paul Wotton, said: “We started well, scored the goal and got the crowd up. It was just a really good day. They are a League One team at the end of the day, no matter what the scoreline suggests. They are two leagues higher than us, so they are going to have moments in the game, but we stood up to it.”

League Two Exeter pulled off an upset with a 2-1 win away to League One leaders Huddersfield. Exeter took the lead after 12 minutes, thanks to a perfectly delivered cross from the left from Luca Woodhouse, with centre-back Jack Taylor stealing in at the far post to finish it off.

Huddersfield looked a different team in the second half and found an equaliser within eight minutes of the restart as Ibane Bowat headed home Cameron Humphreys’ corner at the back post.

Charlie Cummins grabbed the winner nine minutes from time at the end of a well-worked move up the right, culminating in Reece Cole’s cutback and a good finish.

View image in fullscreen Exeter’s Charlie Cummins celebrates after his late winner against Huddersfield. Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Altrincham were denied another famous FA Cup upset as they conceded an 84-minute equaliser against Notts County before bowing out in a penalty shootout.

County took the lead through Jacob Bedeau in the 28th minute but Altrincham responded well with Lucas Weaver grabbing an equaliser six minutes before half-time. Lewis Banks gave the hosts the lead just before the hour but Callum Roberts dashed Altrincham’s hopes of another cup scalp, having beaten 17 Football League sides in the competition, scoring with a first-time strike to force extra-time.

With neither side able to make a breakthrough in extra-time the game went to penalties and Aidan Barlow, Sam Taylor and Eddy Jones all missed from the spot for Altrincham as County triumphed 3-2.

Blackpool survived a scare at Hornchurch, needing to rely on a 118th-minute winner from Josh Bowler to secure a 2-1 comeback victory at the Hornchurch Stadium.

Fleetwood’s hopes of following up their memorable Carabao Cup upset against Premier League champions Arsenal with a long FA Cup run are over after a 2-1 home defeat by fellow League Two side Rochdale. Baba Adeeko’s goal in extra time at Highbury sent the visitors through.

Chesterfield withstood a second-half comeback from Yeovil Town to secure their place in the second round with a 4-3 victory. Yeovil recovered from 3-1 down to level at 3-3 before Joel Randall struck the winner for the Spireites a minute from time.

Late Mansfield goals from Rhys Oates and Jordan Bowery ended the plucky Cup resistance of National League North Macclesfield. Nathan Moriah-Welsh gave Mansfield a first-half lead but the Silkmen were still in the tie under Oates made it 2-0 in the 72nd minute. Bowery added a third three minutes into added time to wrap up victory for the Stags.

League One Plymouth eased through thanks to three goals in a late 11-minute spell in a 4-0 win against Southern League Premier Central battlers Alvechurch. Will Evans finally broke the deadlock after 50 minutes, winning the ball from Jessy Bavanganga before driving a low angled shot into the far corner. Further goals from Evans, Michael Baidoo and Ronan Curtis saw the Pilgrims through.

View image in fullscreen Michael Baidoo makes it 3-0 to Plymouth as they overcome Alvechurch. Photograph: Dave Rowntree/PPAUK/Shutterstock

League One strugglers Barnsley booked their spot in the second round with a 7-2 win over Aldershot at Oakwell, with Cameron McGeehan grabbing a hat-trick.

Leyton Orient held off Harborough 5-1 to progress into the second round while League Two high-flyers Crewe beat Wimbledon 2-1.

Nick Powell and Adam Phillips scored twice as Bradford thrashed National League North side Marine 7-0, while a late goal from Joel Randall helped Cheltenham close out a dramatic 4-3 win over National League Yeovil.

Last season’s quarter-finalists Port Vale booked their place in the second round with a 4-2 victory over National League strugglers Scunthorpe United at Vale Park. MK Dons avoided an upset as they ground out a 2-1 win over League Two Swindon.

Southern League Premier Central team Worcester’s hopes of an upset were ended in a 1-0 defeat at League Two Colchester while Jack Bates scored twice in the first half as Dover progressed with a 2-0 win over Wealdstone.

Ollie Pearce scored after 10 seconds as York sealed a 4-0 win over Northampton. The City captain also scored a second before Alex Hunt and Josh Stones completed the rout.

Jordan Thewlis’s stoppage-time penalty gave seventh-tier Guiseley a 1-0 win over Sutton at Nethermoor Park as Carlisle beat League Two leaders Salford 1-0. Ryan Graydon missed a penalty for the visitors before David Ajiboye’s goal just before the break proved enough to send the Cumbrians through.

Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds slipped to a 4-0 defeat at Burton. Will Collar and Borges Rodrigues scored for the Brewers in the first half, with Charlie Webster and Zac Scutt adding two more late on.

Nathan Odokonyero scored twice as National League South Salisbury saw off seventh-tier Sholing 6-0 to take their place in round two for the first time since reforming in 2015.

Sports.title: Man United are a rotten, shambolic mess. They lack intelligence, look uncoached and fumbling, failing Michael Carrick is not the man to arrest this trauma, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Manchester United do not have a football team, more a collection of adrenaline junkies. Over time, it will not be enough. So deficient are Michael Carrick's players that they surely can't keep their manager in a job for much longer. For the most part United are shambolic, a mess. At times they play football so devoid of intelligence and competence that it's almost impossible to fathom. They look uncoached. Yet here they were for the second night running at Old Trafford, completing a lap of honour at full-time while their supporters sang the name of Carrick as he completed his own journey in front of the Stretford End towards the tunnel. United – it's worth pointing out – are third bottom of the Premier League. They haven't won in the league since August and have conceded more goals across all competitions – 30 – than any team bar Crystal Palace in Europe's top divisions. But at Old Trafford they will cling to anything to help them look in the mirror without laughing and currently the currency is comebacks. There was one against Roma in the Champions League last Tuesday and here – quite remarkably – there were two in one game. None of it should really mean anything in the grand scheme. United are rotten, capable of playing effectively only when something gives them an energy spike with which to roll. It makes for quite hypnotic theatre but has inadequacy and desperation at its core. Patrick Dorgu (centre) scored a late equaliser as troubled Man United drew 4-4 vs Aston Villa Dorgu scored in the 96th-minute with this header but United sit 18th in the Premier League Despite the draw, Michael Carrick's position as United head coach looks increasingly doubtful It won't sustain them or indeed their fumbling, failing manager. But for the moment it's what they have and what they are. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Mazraoui 4, Yoro 6, Maguire 5 (Heaven 46, 5), Dalot 3 (Dorgu 66, 8); Tielemans 6 (Mount 66, 5), Mainoo 6; Amad 5 (Lacey 66, 7), Fernandes 6, Cunha 7; Mbeumo 5 (Zirkzee 83, 7) Goals: Fernandes (16 pen), Tielemans (44), Zirkzee (90+2), Dorgu (90+6) Booked: Heaven Manager: Michael Carrick 6 ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 5, Lindelof 6, Torres 6, Maatsen 4; Goretzka 6 (Mbaye 78, 6), Kamara 4; Alysson 7 (Barkley 71, 6), McGinn 8 (Hemmings 71, 6), Manzambi 6; Jackson 6 (Madjo 86) Goals: Alysson (1), Jackson (4), McGinn (48 pen), Goretzka (53) Manager: Unai Emery 5 Referee: Chris Kavanagh 5 Att: 74,114 Here, they twice trailed by two, at the start of both halves. They were 2-0 down after only four minutes and 4-2 behind after 53. Somehow they managed not to lose. The two goals United scored in added time at the end of the game came from absolutely nowhere. On the touchline Carrick – free from total humiliation for the second time in six days – raised a single finger to the sky. In the directors' box – where the TV companies seem to have a camera permanently trained these days – fist pumps were in evidence from those in United blazers. This was another uncomfortable afternoon for Messrs Ratcliffe, Wilcox and Berrada. A collection of new banners in the crowd made feelings known. For now, Carrick is being spared any of the blame. That is strange and wrong but tells us much about the confused nature of the modern United. If they blame one of their own then they really do have nowhere left to go in search of self-respect. United's opening against Roma last week had been traumatic enough. This was even worse but the root of it was desperately familiar – incompetent football. The hapless United full-back Diogo Dalot was to blame for the first goal as Villa's Brazilian Alysson blasted his shot through the Portuguese's limp challenge. Later – after conceding a second half penalty – Dalot was booed off by his own fans. That was painful and unedifying but completely understandable. Dalot has played more than 250 games for United yet has never even been good enough. Aston Villa took the lead after just 59 seconds when Alysson (centre) scored at Old Trafford Nicolas Jackson (centre) doubled the visitors' lead on four minutes as they made a dream start Bruno Fernandes pulled one back for the hosts with a penalty on 16 minutes in a crazy start For goal two, goalkeeper Senne Lammens was culpable as he pushed Alysson's shot into the path of Nicolas Jackson. Once again United were in sink or swim territory. Once again, amazingly, they kept their heads above water – at least for a while. Boubacar Kamara's 13th minute challenge on Matheus Cunha was stupid as the Brazilian was heading away from goal. But the Bruno Fernandes penalty that followed was calm and precise and the shot of belief United needed was theirs. For the next 20 minutes or so, Carrick's team played well off the back of it. It was the only part of their game that will look good on the highlights. The United front four pressed and harried the Villa defence to the extent that Unai Emery's team couldn't get up the field. Villa keeper Zion Suzuki saved well from a Cunha curler while subsequent shots from Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Amad Diallo took deflections and narrowly missed the target. At some stage it felt as though United's energy must drop. Over time it did. But then they equalised. Moments after seeing Suzuki save one of his own efforts, Amad found space to pull the ball back for Youri Tielemans who placed his first United goal in from 18 yards against his old club. Carrick's team deserved to be level at that stage and had played some enterprising football to get there. But their self-harm gene surfaced again before long. Youri Tielemans (right) brought United level before half-time with this strike vs his old club John McGinn put Villa ahead again just minutes after half-time from the penalty spot Leon Goretkza (left) made it 4-2 to Villa with this close-range strike as they looked set to win Joshua Zirkzee (left) pulled one back in second-half stoppage-time with this finish for United Alysson had almost scored with the last big moment of the first half and in the 47th minute he drew an utterly dumb foul from Dalot and John McGinn scored the penalty firmly. United are beyond compare in the Premier League when it comes to this kind of thing. Who else in the top flight concedes the kind of goals they do? A case in point came in the 53rd minute. McGinn's free-kick was heading across goal and away when United defender Leny Yoro inexplicably headed it towards his own goal. Lammens somehow touched the ball on to the bar but when it dropped Leon Goretzka poked it in. That was the 16th goal United had conceded in the last five games and this time the attempt at a fightback was more muted. There were some half chances – shots from Cunha and Fernandes – and some territory in which to play. But this was a game Villa were now able to control rather better and they looked set to ease home until Patrick Dorgu crossed for Joshua Zirkzee to ease a goal in from out of nothing in the 2nd minute of added time. Old Trafford was emptying fast by the time Dorgu headed in a 96th equaliser from a corner. But by then the collective blood was up once more and it was enough. Villa appealed for a foul on goalkeeper Suzuki and it's true Lammens had gone looking for him. Was the contact between the two 'keepers significant enough to warrant VAR intervention? Probably not. United had their draw and they had a point. If the season ended today, they would be down. Yet they were cheered off. Some things you just can't make up. Sports.title: Leeds defender Jayden Bogle victim of racial abuse online after escaping red card for challenge on Tottenham's Mathys Tel
Sports.content:
Leeds defender Jayden Bogle victim of racial abuse online after escaping red card for challenge on Tottenham's Mathys Tel

Jayden Bogle has been racially abused online after Leeds’ Premier League win over Tottenham on Saturday.

His club have promised to push for ‘the strongest possible action’ if those responsible for the posts can be identified.

Leeds’ statement read: ‘Leeds United are appalled at the disgusting, racist social media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered following Saturday’s Premier League victory against Tottenham Hotspur.

‘Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

‘The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

‘Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse.’

Jayden Bogle has been the victim of sickening racial abuse after avoiding a red card for this challenge against Tottenham on Saturday

Leeds have promised to push for legal action to be taken against the abusers if they can be identified

Along with the racist and highly offensive messages, the posts, believed to have come from four separate accounts, featured emojis of monkeys and bananas.

Bogle was involved in a controversial incident during the Tottenham game. The 26-year-old escaped a red card when his studs made heavy contact with the ankle of Mathys Tel, forcing the Spurs player to go off injured.

After the game, Leeds boss Daniel Farke said: ‘Jayden is one of the fairest players in the country.

He is more like a butterfly than an eagle and he would not even foul a player on purpose, let alone injure them. It was never intentional and maybe this is why the VAR said it was not a red card.’

Sports.title: Crystal Palace set to SACK Pierre Sage: Thomas Frank leads race to replace struggling French boss with club bottom of the Premier League
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace set to SACK Pierre Sage: Thomas Frank leads race to replace struggling French boss with club bottom of the Premier League

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is facing the sack after his side dropped to the bottom of the Premier League with Thomas Frank in pole position to replace him.

Palace have won just two of their ten league matches this season, with Sunday's 3-1 defeat to Liverpool leaving them at the foot of the league for the first time in nearly nine years.

Sage is expected to become the first Premier League manager sacked this season and former Spurs boss Frank is considered the frontrunner to take over.

Sean Dyche, though, also has his admirers at Selhurst Park.

However, Sage believes his side have been unlucky with results this season and has requested the hierarchy remain patient.

The 47-year-old, who left RC Lens for Palace in the summer to succeed Oliver Glasner, also admitted the Palace squad needs strengthening - perhaps to absolve himself of some blame.

Crystal Palace are set to sack Pierre Sage with the club bottom of the Premier League

'You can create the links between these two things,' Sage replied when asked whether being bottom of the league heading into the international break could see him sacked.

'But a lot of times I've said we deserved better and it was the case again on Sunday.

'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

'I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in that, and if it's not the case, they will take a decision.

'I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100% involved in what I have to do.

'We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be okay.'

Sports.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix in the rain: Brit holds off a flying Max Verstappen - after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spins out of the lead
Sports.content:
Lando Norris scored a superb victory in a rain-affected Sao Paulo GP as he overcame tricky conditions to log his third win of a difficult 2026 season for his McLaren team.

Just a week after ceding the F1 crown to Kimi Antonelli, Norris reminded everyone of his world champion's class with a great performance in a race that saw wet conditions both at the start and in the closing stages.

Although the race win slipped away from Antonelli it was a good afternoon in Brazil for Mercedes as the team followed up the Italian youngster's drivers' title by securing the prestigious constructors' version – the first for the Brackley-based organisation since 2021.

This was always going to be an exciting race after a raft of power unit grid penalties created a mixed-up grid, and left some big players starting down the order – notably Charles Leclerc in 13th, Lewis Hamilton in 20th, and Max Verstappen in 21st.

Drizzle before the start ensured that everyone committed to intermediate tyres for the damp opening laps. The big question was how long they would last on a drying track, and who would lead the charge to change to slicks.

The tricky conditions at the start played to the strengths of the very best drivers – in other words the guys who had the supreme confidence to test the limits of grip. Kimi Antonelli charged past pole man Norris into the lead, the latter not getting away well.

Lando Norris won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spun out of the lead

Lando Norris holds the trophy aloft after winning his third Grand Prix of the season

Further back Hamilton had a storming first lap, gaining 11 places as he scythed through the field, and in his wake Verstappen moved up eight spots.

As Antonelli continued to lead Hamilton's intermediate tyres wore out quickly as the track dried, and the Briton slipped down the order. At one stage he briefly found himself in a hectic dice with Ferrari team mate Charles Leclerc for a humble 11th place.

Fortunately both men appeared to have taken note of Thursday's summit meeting with team boss Fred Vasseur, and any controversy was avoided.

A frustrated Hamilton was keen to change to dry tyres, and after a heated debate with his race engineer he was finally allowed to pit.

His pace on his fresh slicks alerted others to the fact that they were now the ideal choice, and the rest of the field soon followed Hamilton's lead and pitted.

For George Russell a hugely embarrassing moment followed. After a good early charge from a penalised P7 on the grid to third he spun in the tight pit exit, losing several places before he could resume. It was not what he needed at a time when all the focus is on his mercurial team mate.

Antonelli initially led after the stops, but the Italian complained of a handling issue with his Mercedes, and when he subsequently spun off the road at the first turn he lost the lead to the charging Norris.

After another off track moment he fell back to fourth, behind the Red Bulls of Isack Hadjar and the flying Verstappen, who later swapped places.

The second half of the race was again about tyres, and this time was it possible to make it to the end on a single set of slick tyres. One by one the leading contenders decided it wasn't and came in, with only Russell resolutely staying out.

Then in the closing laps the rain returned, and there was a rush to return to intermediate tyres, led by Russell – who gained by having not made an extra stop earlier.

Norris safely retained his lead on the slippery track and duly crossed the line well clear of Verstappen and Hadjar.

'It was a very tough race,' said Norris. 'Obviously not the best of launches off the line. A lot of challenges today, the conditions, going onto slicks in the wet is tough. The main thing today is I kept it cool, and didn't make any mistakes.

Lewis Hamilton completed his 400th Grand Prix but only managed a ninth place finish

Max Verstappen started the race in 21st but incredibly managed to finish in second place

'This weekend, we had an opportunity to get a pole yesterday, an opportunity to win. And this year when I've had an opportunity, I've mostly taken it.'

Russell gained some redemption for his earlier error by recovering to fourth and beating Antonelli.

'Not really too sure what happened,' he said when asked by the Daily Mail about his bizarre pitlane spin. 'I went quite high risk, because I smelt an opportunity, and paid the price.

'It's in those moments where you either gain a lot or you lose a lot. This time it went against us. Ironically, because of that, I didn't pit [a second time] and kind of brought myself back into the race.'

It was a difficult afternoon for Hamilton, who struggled for pace in the mixed conditions and eventually finished ninth. He even survived a late spin and contact with the barrier when the rain returned, and he initially tried to stay out.

'I get to Turn One, and it's drenched, and so I didn't get that information,' when asked by the Daily Mail about the incident. 'So a bit unfortunate with that. And then I was just trailing around trying to bring the car back. So I was lucky it wasn't in the wall. Sorry to the team on that.'

After a hectic run of six races in seven weekends, F1 action will resume in Las Vegas in a fortnight.

Meanwhile, Formula 1 and the FIA are expected to make a call early this week on the end of season schedule.

One option is to cancel the Qatar and Abu Dhabi events, due to be held on November 29 and December 6 respectively, and greenlight a substitute race at Imola on the latter date.

The other is to formally abandon any plan to go to Italy due to time constraints, and stick with the Middle East events. If they do ultimately have to be canned the season would thus end in Las Vegas on November 21.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer wastes his chance to respond to Thomas Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer wastes his chance to respond to Thomas Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL

When searching for why Chelsea were beaten by the side who were sitting bottom of the Premier League, the temptation from Xabi Alonso might be to describe this defeat as a tale of two penalties.

First, Chelsea were denied one when Cole Palmer was sandwiched by Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka as he entered the Sunderland area, with the officials concluding the contact occurred outside of the box.

Then, Sunderland were awarded one when Brian Brobbey was brought down by Levi Colwill. The striker had hold of the defender at the same time, and arguably clipped his own heel upon second viewing, but Enzo Le Fee gladly accepted the opportunity to score the game's only goal.

However, it would be wrong to blame this deserved defeat on those two decisions alone. Referee Jarred Gillett and VAR Nick Hopton were weak but not the reason that Chelsea lost.

This was actually a tale of two strikers. Sunderland had one in the brilliant bully that is Brobbey, whereas Chelsea had nobody after Alonso yet again decided against starting Danny Welbeck.

In the three Premier League games played since Joao Pedro's injury – against Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and now Sunderland – Alonso has gone with Morgan Rogers as a false nine once and Pedro Neto twice. Welbeck was on the bench in all of those matches.

Sunderland handed Chelsea a brutal reality check as they climbed off the foot of the table

The visitors fell victim to two questionable penalty calls at the Stadium of Light

We are not saying the 35-year-old is the answer to all of Alonso's problems, but he is an actual No9 who scored 13 times in the Premier League for Brighton last season.

Neto was hardly going to have a high success rate when wrestling with centre backs for the long balls which were coming from Colwill and Co. It is a question that needs asking, therefore, especially after another loss.

Why did Chelsea sign Welbeck if not to play when Joao Pedro is injured?

Welbeck came on in the 62nd minute here, but by then, a familiar feeling was washing over Chelsea.

They lost 2-1 here at the very end of last season. Malo Gusto scored an own goal, Wesley Fofana was red carded, and Chelsea, managed by Calum McFarlane in the interim, failed to qualify for any form of European football.

They smacked of an utterly unserious side then, and resembled it here, too.

Chelsea had a week to prepare for this Premier League clash while Sunderland were playing – and losing – to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League.

Regis Le Bris' side had not won in the league since August. Yet they were the sharper of the two teams here.

It hardly helped Alonso that Chelsea's attackers never appeared at it individually.

Cole Palmer had a stinker. This was supposed to be an opportunity to show why Thomas Tuchel made a mistake in not naming him in his latest England squad. If anything, he helped make sure those accusations cannot be levelled at Tuchel over this break.

Xabi Alonso tinkered with his line-up and it failed to pay off in a second defeat in three games

Cole Palmer had a stinker in a woeful response to Thomas Tuchel's England snub

Rogers' performance was best summed up by the time he simply sprinted out of play with the ball to gift Sunderland a goal-kick. He and Palmer resembled no-shows.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 7, Mukiele 7, O'Nien 6, Mandava 7; Xhaka 6 (Ahoka 4, 6), Sadiki 7; Meunier 6, Talbi 6 (Rigg 88), Le Fee 6 (Angulo 88); Brobbey 8 (Isidor 67, 6) Subs (not used): Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Fofana, Tutierov Scorers: Le Fee (36 pen) Booked: Ahoka, Meunier, Brobbey, O'Nien, Angulo Manager: Regis Le Bris 7 Chelsea (4-3-3): Penders 6; Palestra 5 (Gusto 62, 5), Fofana 5, Colwill 4 (Estevao 45, 6), Chavarria 5 (Quenda 79); Caicedo 6, Lavia 6, Henderson 6 (Emegha 87); Palmer 4, Neto 5 (Welbeck 62, 5), Rogers 4 Subs (not used): Sharman-Lowe, Barco, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli Booked: Colwill, Neto, Caicedo, Fofana Manager: Xabi Alonso 4 Referee: Jarred Gillett 4

Neto looked like a lost little boy trying to lead Chelsea's line in the absence of Joao Pedro.

The half-time statistics said Chelsea had sent more open-play crosses into Sunderland's box in the opening 45 minutes than in their entire games v Fulham, Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Except, they had no striker for Alonso's full backs Marco Palestra or Pep Chavarria to try to find. Just 5ft 8in Neto and the odd other box-crasher.

Trailing 1-0 at half-time here, Alonso made a singular substitution. It was to introduce Estevao for Colwill, who had been tormented by Brobbey.

Le Bris was asked in his post-match press conference if there is another player like his striker in the Premier League. He thought long and hard before answering: 'What do you think? I don't think so. His physicality, his intensity, it's impressive, that's for sure. The build-up is so important to have a target man.'

Alonso chipped in on Brobbey: 'He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but only when you defend better than we did.' On his own attack, he added: 'We didn't produce enough to deserve to win.'

Sunderland's tactic of hoofing the ball up to Brobbey worked wonders. He scared the daylights out of Chelsea's centre backs. When Fofana first arrived at the Stadium of Light, a Chelsea fan shouted at him as he got off the bus. 'Fofana, please be on the bench,' he said. Fofana may have been wishing he was a substitute as well whenever he was wrestling with Brobbey.

It was the long-ball approach which led to Sunderland winning their penalty. They smashed it towards the top of the pitch and Brobbey bullied Colwill. Sunderland won their spot-kick and, in truth, deserved the lead for the sheer energy they brought to this match.

Alonso is ten Premier League games into his Chelsea career. The honeymoon period is over. Sunderland lost their captain Granit Xhaka to an injury after two minutes here. Chelsea had named a line-up featuring three midfielders. But they never showed any signs of control, and for that, Alonso should be looking at himself and his own side rather than the refereeing team.

Sports.title: Prickly Unai Emery fires back at 'more questions' from Sky Sports reporter in awkward interview after storming down Old Trafford tunnel before full time
Sports.content:
Prickly Unai Emery fires back at 'more questions' from Sky Sports reporter in awkward interview after storming down Old Trafford tunnel before full time

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery was in a prickly mood as he bit back at Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davison in a fiery end to his post-match interview at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Emery had just seen his Villa side twice throw away a two-goal lead against Manchester United – with Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scoring in stoppage time to secure a remarkable 4-4 draw.

The Villa boss was spotted storming down the touchline before the full-time whistle and after Dorgu's dramatic 97th-minute equaliser – with play continuing for another two minutes.

And the Villa boss, already exasperated at being asked 'more questions,' did not take kindly to being asked if he was emotional about the late equaliser or if he felt it was unfair.

When asked if his walking off was an emotional reaction, he responded: 'No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing.'

And then when asked whether the award of the goal was unfair, he replied: 'No, no. Not unfair. Please.

Unai Emery was in a prickly mood towards the end of his post match interview with Sky Sports

Emery had just stormed down the tunnel at Old Trafford after Aston Villa threw away a 4-2 lead in stoppage time

Emery took exception to being asked 'more questions' by Sky reporter Patrick Davison

'They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.'

Emery ended the interview making light of his 'poor' English, and then sarcastically asking if there were 'more questions' before an ironic 'Have a good Sunday' as he walked out of the interview.

Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany complained on social media about the legitimacy of United's last-gasp equaliser.

He accused United goalkeeper Senne Lammens – who went up for the corner – of impeding his Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he looked to punch the ball clear.

After Roy Keane said 'football is a contact sport,' he posted on X: 'To put in context this convenient narrative of "contact sport" we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

'Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

'Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve.

'But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.'

Michael Carrick was involved in a spiky interview with Sky Sports about his Man United future

Sky Sports' Davison's brush with Emery came just minutes after a spiky interview with beleaguered United boss Michael Carrick.

When the future of his own position was put to him by Davison, Carrick took exception to the question.

'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? You've been asked time and again about your future? I know you have said that you walking away was the best for the club, you'd probably do it,' Davison asked Carrick.

'It's not going to happen, no,' Carrick replied.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week. They conceded twice at the start of each half against Villa, and have now let in 30 goals in all competitions – the joint highest in Europe's top five leagues.

Sports.title: Dominant victory over Australia was England's best display of the year: This sweeping, attacking style should now become their blueprint under Steve Borthwick, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
Henry Pollock pulled out his pulse check celebration and suddenly Steve Borthwick's heart rate could settle.

This was the performance England's under-fire coach desperately needed.

Days after Borthwick was accused of overseeing a toxic environment, his players delivered their best performance of the year.

'Do it for Steve,' was the message from Borthwick's senior players, who were left seething after reports of a split in the camp.

Maro Itoje interrupted the live post-match press conference to double down on the squad's support.

Finally, Borthwick had a reason to smile.

Henry Pollock (left) scored two tries in two minutes as England thumped Australia 45-22

Pollock crosses the whitewash to score his first, and England's fifth of seven, in a dominant win

The traditional back-row player came on as winger and made an impact at the Allianz Stadium

Pollock and Borthwick are unlikely bedfellows but it was the peroxide youngster who stole the show.

The 21-year-old was providing emergency backline cover from the bench when he was called into action in response to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's first-half injury.

Playing in the unfamiliar position on the right wing, he scored twice in the second-half, chasing a hat-trick as the final whistle blew on England's record points haul against the Wallabies.

At one point, the versatile flanker nutmegged Australian full-back Tom Wright – counterintuitively, perhaps – consolidating his status as England's super sub.

'We now have to bear Henry Pollock saying playing on the wing is easy,' joked Borthwick. 'And we now have to bear Henry Pollock saying he can play anywhere on the pitch.

'We suggested the front row and he said 'No!' He was excellent. When you're making the decision about a 6-2 or a 5-3 split on the bench, you look at your assistant coaches and say, 'Can he genuinely play there?' He proved that today.'

It is little surprise the Rugby Football Union (RFU) are working on projects to find the next Pollock.

They want to create a centralised academy pathway, complete with branding experts, to manufacture more young box office talent.

They have even pulled up the 1995 Nike commercial starring tennis rivals Andre Agassi and Pete Sampras as inspiration.

Pollock stole the show, as he so often does, but this was by no means a one-man effort. England hurt the Wallabies with their sweeping attacking play which should become their blueprint. George Furbank and Henry Slade combined to add an additional wave of threats with ball in hand.

Fin Smith kicked 10 points for England in the Nations Championship clash against the Wallabies

Hosts' win was soured by Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's (right) injury which saw Pollock come on

Itoje leaps to Borthwick's defence Maro Itoje launched an impassioned defence of his 'world class' England coach Steve Borthwick after a 45-22 hammering of Australia. Ahead of his team's November opener, a newspaper report claimed the national squad had 'lost faith' in their boss after a run of five defeats in seven Tests. There were also allegations of player bust-ups and staff quitting. England's on-field response was impressive. Their seven-try rout was the most points they've scored against the Wallabies and their second biggest ever win against them. 'From a players' point of view, we have full support in Steve,' said captain Itoje. 'The article doesn't represent the environment I recognise. That's not the man I recognise. Often, criticism is attached to the coach too much. 'We as players are the ones who have to perform. There have been times we haven't done that. I'm delighted to get the win. Steve is a world-class coach and we're lucky to have him. 'It's never nice getting criticism. But if we were scared of criticism, we shouldn't be here.' Back-row substitute Henry Pollock played the second-half on the wing, scoring twice after replacing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso who suffered an ankle injury. Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who limped off with a hip problem, are now both doubts for Saturday's meeting with Japan who are led by former England coach Eddie Jones. 'In the last couple of days, a number of my predecessors have reached out and contacted me. They've been supportive,' said Borthwick. 'The gist was to focus on the rugby. 'That's what I've done this week. I think there is another gear in this team. I'm excited about the players taking it to another level.' England's attack was much improved, their back-line dovetailing nicely with centre Henry Slade named player of the match. Australia, by contrast, were woeful. 'We're definitely satisfied. That article came out and it made us a bit tighter but we're not the finished product,' said Pollock. 'Pressure is a privilege. I've played a little bit of wing for Northampton, but this was a big step-up. I loved it.' Australia captain Harry Wilson said: 'We didn't fire a shot. I'm really disappointed because I expect better from us. Three defeats on the trot isn't good enough. 'We need to be better. We know when we play well, we can beat any team in the world. But we haven't been doing that consistently enough.' By Alex Bywater

Maro Itoje looked rejuvenated after his summer off. He disrupted the ruck and made life miserable for Australia's half-backs, who barely fired a shot until the game broke up in the final quarter. England made 81 tackles in the first half and missed just two, with Ben Curry winning a turnover.

At the World Rugby coaching meeting last Sunday, Borthwick made clear that England have been putting hours of work into their driving maul. It paid off as Jamie George scored a set-piece try in the eighth minute that put England on track for victory. His cathartic celebration spoke a thousand words.

In his pre-tournament briefing this week, RFU CEO Bill Sweeney defiantly stated that England are the second best team in the world when they keep 15 players on the pitch. Given the team were hit with a record-breaking 14 yellow cards in eight Tests – one of which was a 20-minute red – it felt like the executive was clutching at straws.

It would be wise now for Sweeney and Borthwick to club together to bring in a refereeing coach. Jaco Peyper and Jerome Garces are firmly embedded in the South African and French camps. England have invited Christophe Ridley to officiate team sessions but they have stopped short of a full-time appointment.

Crucially, England managed to concede no more yellow cards – although a couple of first-half penalties meant the game was still in the balance before Pollock's second-half introduction.

Instead, it was Wallaby prop Angus Bell who was sinbinned for a hip drop tackle on Immanuel Feyi-Waboso in the 33rd minute. Feyi-Waboso had been England's most dangerous player. He made 138m from eight carries in the first-half but his ankle never recovered from Bell's tackle.

England captain Maro Itoje looks rejuvenated after missing the summer internationals

Tries from Ollie Chessum and Joe Heyes had built up England's lead but Feyi-Waboso's day was over when he struggled to chase down Max Jorgensen's interception try on the stroke of half time.

Pollock came to the rescue. Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus has been the biggest advocate of utility players. He has turned South African centre Andre Esterhuizen into a flanker and now Borthwick is using a similar trick.

It is no secret that Pollock loves the camera. His manager, Eddie Hearn, will vouch for that. He bounced around on the wing and charged out of his half with his first touch of the ball. It led to a bonus-point try for Jack van Poortvliet.

The youngster showed the Midas touch. Punishing the Wallabies for a poor clearance kick, the youngster picked up a bouncing ball to score in the 56th minute, after a failed interception by Jorgensen. He scored his second moments later, showcasing his speed to charge down the right wing. Even Borthwick could allow himself a smile at that one.

England flaunted their depth, deploying props Ellis Genge and Will Stuart from the bench. The Pom Squad were reunited although, worryingly, centre Seb Atkinson joined Feyi-Waboso in the medical room. Both will now be doubts for next week's meeting with Eddie Jones's Japan.

A late exchange of tries kept the crowd entertained but they had no effect on the outcome – this was a convincing victory that reminded us that England have the ability to cause damage when they play the right way.

Sports.title: Astonishing moment manager HEADBUTTS opposition player and is sent off, sparking mass brawl as FA Cup first round clash descends into chaos
Sports.content:
Oldham boss Micky Mellon was sent off for headbutting Sheffield Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery as their FA Cup first round clash descended into a mass brawl at Boundary Park. League Two Oldham pulled off a shock over their League One opponents, but the result was overshadowed by the altercation which occurred six minutes from the end of normal time. The former Blackpool and Burnley midfielder appeared to grab Slattery by the back of the neck and pulled him closer to his face, before pushing his head into the rival player’s face and knocking him over. The touchline soon descended into chaos with players and staff from both teams grappling with each other in a farcical melee. Eventually the two warring sides were separated giving referee Martin Woods the opportunity to approach Mellon and present him with a thoroughly deserved red card. Oldham, now with their manager in the stands, played on and incredibly nicked a 110th minute winner through Will Sutton. Oldham Athletic manager Micky Mellon is shown a red card for moving his head towards Wednesday's Callum Slattery 🟥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/5QMxgLt0dO — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 8, 2026 Oldham manager Micky Mellon was sent off for an astonishing headbutt on Sheffield Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery The scene soon descended into chaos as both players and staff from both sides entered the melee Eventually Mellon was shown a red card and will serve a three match touchline ban Wednesday piled on the pressure in the final minutes desperately trying to find an equaliser but to no avail as Oldham held on and advanced into the next round. Mellon, however, will now have to serve a three-match touchline ban meaning he will miss his side's next appearance in this year's FA Cup. Calum Kavanagh had put Oldham ahead in the 66th minute with a fierce drive after Mike Fondop headed on Noah Chilvers’ right-wing cross – his sixth goal of the season. Wednesday equalised ten minutes later through former Oldham forward Davis Keillor-Dunn. Elsewhere in the FA Cup on Sunday, seventh-tier Wimborne Town stunned League Two Crawley 2-0 to reach the second round for the first time in their history. The Dorset part-timers of the Southern League Premier Division South took the lead through Yang Seung-woo’s stunning strike after nine minutes, with Cameron Munn deflecting in Jackson King’s shot 11 minutes from time to seal the upset. Stockport survived a scare to beat Cray Wanderers of the Isthmian League Premier Division 3-2. The League One high-flyers were facing a shock exit when they fell two goals behind in the first half, a situation not helped by a red card for goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond for a foul outside the box. From the free-kick, defender Alex Hernandez found the top corner to make it 2-0, but Stockport staged a late fightback, Kyle Wootton and, in added time, Mikael Mandron scoring to take the tie to extra time before Lewis Fiorini’s penalty won it. Eighth-tier Stafford Rangers also led EFL opposition 2-0 before bowing out, Grimsby finding themselves facing an embarrassing exit against a team four divisions lower before hitting back to make it 3-3 after extra time, eventually going through on penalties.
