World.title: Lagos governorship candidates clash over waste management, defend political records
World.content:
Lagos governorship candidates on Sunday disagreed over how to address the state’s waste management crisis, with proposals ranging from returning a greater role to local governments to investing in recycling and waste recovery facilities.

The candidates spoke at a governorship debate in Lagos, where they also faced questions about their political records, experience in public office, party affiliations and the 2020 #EndSARS protests.

Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) described Lagos as a state that stinks, blaming years of poor management for the deterioration in refuse collection.

He rejected the argument that population growth was mainly responsible, saying the state had managed its waste more effectively in the past despite the increasing number of residents.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour said Lagos had about 1,000 waste collection trucks under former Governor Babatunde Fashola, but that the number had fallen to about 200, according to information available to him.

He blamed the decline partly on the centralisation of waste management, which he said had weakened the role of local governments.

“We don’t actually have a waste management system. We have a waste pick and dump system,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He proposed involving local governments in refuse collection and requiring households to separate their waste so that recyclable materials could be collected and processed.

He said the arrangement would create economic opportunities and allow residents and the different levels of government to benefit from waste recycling.

Lagos introduced its Private Sector Participation (PSP) scheme for domestic waste collection in 1997, beginning with a pilot in Kosofe and Bariga local government areas. The scheme was later extended across the state, with the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) taking over its management in 2007. LAWMA has identified unreliable service delivery and difficulties enforcing standards as among the scheme’s weaknesses.

Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, defended the government’s approach, saying Lagos was moving away from the practice of collecting refuse and dumping it in landfills.

He said the volume of waste generated in the state, coupled with limited land for disposal, made it necessary to invest in facilities that could recover useful materials.

Mr Hamzat said the government was developing Olusosun and Solous 3 in Alimosho as transfer stations, while a material recovery facility had been established at Erekiti. Similar facilities, he added, were planned for Kinsinki and Chikurudu.

The explanation came against the backdrop of the state’s continuing waste collection problems. In September, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu declared a state of emergency on waste collection after acknowledging delays in refuse evacuation.

During an inspection of the Olusosun dumpsite, the governor announced plans to increase disposal capacity, deploy additional equipment and improve the operations of PSP operators. Transfer-loading stations were also proposed for Olusosun and Solous 3.

Responding to the description of Lagos as a smelly city, Mr Hamzat said it would be unfair to apply that description to the entire state, although he acknowledged that some areas had unpleasant odours.

He admitted that waste management remained a challenge, pointing to inadequate collection trucks, reception facilities and transfer stations.

Funso Doherty, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, said waste was accumulating faster than it was being collected.

He argued that the problem extended beyond household refuse to liquid and human waste, and raised concerns about pollution from the Olusosun dumpsite and its effects on nearby communities.

Candidates defend political records

Beyond waste management, the candidates faced questions about their political histories and whether their experience prepared them to govern Lagos.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour, who came second in the 2023 governorship election on the Labour Party platform before moving to the ADC, was asked whether his performance in that election and subsequent defection could affect his chances in 2027.

He said he was focused on reaching voters and learning from the mistakes of his previous campaign. He also questioned the conduct of the 2023 election, arguing that a credible process would be important in determining the outcome of the next poll.

The Independent National Electoral Commission declared Mr Sanwo-Olu the winner in 2023 with 762,134 votes. Mr Rhodes-Vivour polled 312,329 votes, while the Peoples Democratic Party candidate, Abdul-Azeez Adediran, popularly known as Jandor, secured 62,449 votes.

On his preparedness for office, Mr Rhodes-Vivour pointed to his work in urban development and housing, including proposals for low-income housing developed with the Chinese and American governments and Temple Housing.

He also challenged the emphasis on previous executive experience, citing former Lagos Governor Lateef Jakande as an example of a leader whose vision and commitment shaped his administration.

Mr Hamzat faced questions about whether he would govern independently or remain under the influence of the political establishment that has controlled Lagos since 1999.

He defended his capacity to make independent decisions, citing his academic and professional background, including earning a PhD at 27 and serving as an executive director in an American organisation. He also referred to his family’s political background and his experience in public administration, transport and budgeting.

His record in government also came under scrutiny, with questions about why residents should trust him to tackle flooding, traffic congestion, housing shortages, waste collection and the rising cost of living after nearly eight years as deputy governor and in previous positions in the state government.

Mr Hamzat said he was proud of the state’s achievements but acknowledged that more needed to be done.

He cited the Lekki-Ikoyi Bridge, which he said was delivered while he served as commissioner for transport and works, as well as the Bus Rapid Transit system and the establishment of transport agencies.

He attributed the pressure on public infrastructure to Lagos’s growing population, which he said was approaching 25 million, while the state’s land area remained unchanged.

Hamzat questioned over #EndSARS

The 20 October 2020 shooting at the Lekki Toll Gate also featured in the debate, with Mr Hamzat asked what he knew about the incident and what he did as deputy governor at the time.

He described the day as a sad one and said the Lagos State Government established an independent judicial panel of inquiry, funded its work and later published a White Paper on its recommendations.

Mr Hamzat argued that responsibility for the military rested with the Federal Government but maintained that the state government had not ignored the pain caused by the incident.

In November 2021, the Lagos government said it had accepted 11 of the panel’s 32 recommendations, accepted six with modifications, rejected one and referred 14 to the Federal Government, saying they fell outside the state’s powers.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour, in his closing remarks, recalled being tear-gassed while laying flowers at the Lekki Toll Gate. He criticised what he described as violence against opposition figures and questioned the treatment of people who participated in the protests despite political leaders’ public statements about #EndSARS.

Funso Doherty addresses NDC primary dispute

The NDC candidate also faced questions about a dispute over the party’s governorship primary.

The moderator raised an allegation by Naheem Balogun that he had won the primary but was subsequently displaced.

Mr Doherty rejected the allegation, insisting that he had won the ticket. He said anyone dissatisfied with the outcome could approach the courts.

His movement between political parties also came under scrutiny, with questions about whether it was consistent with the principled leadership he promised Lagos residents.

Mr Doherty argued that opposition parties operated in a difficult political environment, where court cases and interference sometimes made it difficult for politicians to pursue their ambitions on their original platforms.

His political movements have included leaving the ADC for the PDP in 2024, returning to the ADC and later joining the NDC in May 2026.

In announcing his latest move, he said he had initially hoped the ADC would unite the opposition but concluded that it would no longer serve that purpose.

Deji Doherty speaks on Wike’s influence

The PDP candidate, Deji Doherty, was challenged over his relationship with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and whether it would undermine his independence if elected governor.

Mr Wike remains a member of the PDP but serves in the APC-led Federal Government and has publicly declared support for President Bola Tinubu.

Mr Doherty attributed his emergence as the PDP candidate to 26 years of political activity and grassroots support, rather than the influence of any individual.

However, he described Mr Wike as his national leader and said he would continue to recognise him in that capacity.

He argued that political cooperation could bring benefits to Lagos, including improved funding and development.

On his business background, Mr Doherty said his business group was established in 1986 and would mark its 40th anniversary in December.

He said he had worked with major organisations and experienced financial difficulties, including a period when he owed banks about N3.8 billion.

Describing himself as a debt manager, he argued that his experience handling business debts would help him manage the state’s finances.

Candidates make final appeals

In their closing remarks, the candidates returned to their campaign promises.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour called for people-centred policies, greater investment in human development and a government that would protect residents’ welfare and rights.

Mr Hamzat asked voters to assess him against the commitments in his manifesto, The Lagos Promise.

Mr Doherty of the NDC urged residents to decide whether they were satisfied with Lagos after 27 years of political dominance by the same political bloc or wanted a change in direction. He described his party’s programme as The New Way.

Mr Doherty of the PDP promised to remove some levies imposed on residents, including what he described as solar and pothole levies. He also called for a review of charges imposed on minors receiving treatment in hospitals.

He pledged to prioritise education and improve support for teachers and medical workers.

World.title: I’m impressed with Gov Lawal’s performance in Zamfara, says Emir of Kano
World.content:
The Emir of Kano, His Royal Highness Khalifah Muhammad Sunusi II, has expressed satisfaction with Governor Dauda Lawal’s performance in Zamfara State.

The Emir was the guest of honour at the commissioning of the rebuilt and equipped Zawiyya Mosque and Islamiyya School in Gusau.

The Zawiyya is one of the oldest Islamic institutions in Zamfara, with a long history of producing scholars across various fields.

In his Friday sermon at the rebuilt mosque, Professor Ibrahim Maqari emphasised peaceful coexistence among people and the importance of cleanliness, particularly in places of worship.

At the commissioning ceremony, the Emir of Kano, Khalifah Muhammadu Sunusi II, said that only those familiar with the Zawiyya’s former structure could fully appreciate the scale and quality of Governor Lawal’s work.

He also emphasised the importance of keeping the rebuilt mosque clean and well maintained.

He said, “The mosque should be kept clean and in good condition. We must maintain cleanliness when we come here because the mosque is a symbol of Islam.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I am delighted with this work. May Almighty Allah reward His Excellency.

“I can see the good work you are doing in Zamfara State in education, health, security, and infrastructure.

“I am not surprised, as I have known your governor since his days in the banking industry. I know his capabilities, and I am impressed by his performance and happy to see him doing such wonderful work as governor.”

World.title: Lagos governorship candidates offer competing plans on transport, healthcare
World.content:
Candidates in the Lagos State governorship debate have outlined different approaches to tackling traffic congestion and improving healthcare, with proposals ranging from expanding public transportation to increasing hospital funding and providing free treatment for mothers and children.

The World Bank has identified traffic congestion as a persistent problem in Lagos, where commuters spend an average of about four hours daily travelling. Its September 2025 brief examined the city’s public transport challenges and efforts to expand mass transit.

African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour on Sunday at the debate said poor urban planning and an inadequate transport network were partly responsible for the long hours residents spend commuting.

He stated that traffic had become so much a part of daily life that residents had come to accept spending several hours travelling to and from work, often at the expense of time with their families.

“Traffic is not a lifestyle and we should not have to work to get to work,” Mr Rhodes-Vivour said.

He proposed spreading development across the state and expanding the rail network with private-sector funding.

According to him, infrastructure finance companies could provide the money for the expansion, allowing the projects to be completed within two and a half years and repaid over 30 years without placing the entire financial burden on the state government.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also proposed shorter bridges linking the eastern foreshore with the Ibeju-Lekki axis to provide alternative routes for motorists.

On water transportation, Mr Rhodes-Vivour called for more ferry services, accessible terminals and cable cars to complement the rail network. He said commuters should be able to park their vehicles at ferry terminals and continue their journeys by water.

He also proposed dedicated bicycle lanes, improved roads within communities and the development of local centres across local governments to reduce the need for residents to travel long distances to access basic services.

Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, said his administration would build on the existing bus rapid transit (BRT) system and improve connections between road, rail and water transportation.

He noted that the BRT system had recorded 77 million passenger journeys since its introduction. He proposed increasing the number of buses from about 1,000 to 4,000, mainly using compressed natural gas (CNG), to move about one million passengers daily.

Mr Hamzat also proposed dedicated BRT lanes linking Marina with Epe and Badagry, among other routes.

He said commuters should be able to use ferries, trains and BRT buses with a single payment system, allowing them to move between different transport services without making separate payments.

He proposed deploying electric ferries to reduce operating costs and increase passenger capacity, with routes linking Oworonshoki, Ikorodu, Epe and Badagry.

Mr Hamzat added that the government had identified traffic junctions for intervention to ease congestion.

The proposals are linked to the Lagos State Government’s broader transport plans. The Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority (LAMATA) says its Strategic Transport Master Plan provides for an integrated system involving rail, BRT, waterways and other transport services.

Disagreement over rail financing

The candidates disagreed over whether private investors could finance the expansion of Lagos’s rail network without substantial government funding.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour said private financing was possible, adding that he had held discussions with infrastructure financiers who had presented proposals to the Lagos State Government.

He argued that the project was commercially viable and should not take decades to complete.

Mr Hamzat disagreed, saying no sub-national government in Africa had successfully built a rail network entirely through private-sector financing.

He recalled that the Lagos government spent three years under former Governor Babatunde Fashola seeking private investors to finance the Blue and Red rail lines but was unsuccessful.

He stated that government must first invest in rail infrastructure before considering concessions to private operators.

Mr Hamzat also warned that relying on passenger fares alone to finance rail projects could make transportation too expensive for ordinary residents.

Agbero system and public transportation

Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) blamed part of Lagos’s traffic problem on poor management of existing infrastructure and the failure to modernise public transportation.

He criticised the condition of commercial buses operating in the state, describing many as dilapidated and poorly managed. He said the government needed to replace the fragmented system with modern buses that offered safer and more comfortable journeys.

Mr Doherty also alleged that vested interests had benefited from the existing transport arrangement and that political considerations had prevented successive administrations from confronting the informal network associated with transport union levies and touts.

He noted that he would have the political will to reform the system because his administration would depend on voters rather than the informal transport network for political support.

Research by the International Growth Centre has examined the effects of Lagos’s Bus Reform Initiative on private minibus operators. A 2025 study found that the introduction of public buses affected minibus services and drivers’ earnings, highlighting the need to consider informal operators when planning transport reforms.

Deji Doherty of the People Democratic Party (PDP) also identified heavy-duty truck movements, transport union activities, poor roads and delays in completing the Fourth Mainland Bridge as factors contributing to congestion.

He said several local government areas had roads in poor condition, making it difficult to ease traffic without improving the road network.

He proposed additional bridges, including routes linking Oworonshoki with Epe and Ibeju-Lekki, to provide alternative routes for motorists.

Mr Doherty stated that Lagos’s population meant commercial buses, motorcycles, tricycles and private vehicles would continue to operate, making it necessary to improve roads and provide more options for commuters.

On the informal transport system, the NDC candidate said reform would require addressing the livelihoods of people who depended on it.

He proposed expanding vocational and skills acquisition programmes to help them find alternative sources of income.

He also said modernising public transportation would create jobs for drivers, conductors, mechanics and other workers, providing opportunities for some people currently working in the informal system to move into more organised employment.

Fact-checkers challenge candidates’ claims

The debate’s independent fact-checking team challenged some of the candidates’ claims, including statements about Lagos’s revenue and elevation above sea level.

The team rated as false a claim attributed to the NDC candidate that Lagos’s internally generated revenue (IGR) was higher than the combined revenue of 31 other states.

According to figures presented by the fact-checkers, Lagos generated N1.77 trillion in 2025, while all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory generated a combined N5.15 trillion.

The other 35 states and the FCT accounted for N3.38 trillion, meaning Lagos contributed about 34 per cent of the total.

The National Bureau of Statistics’ 2025 IGR figures, reported by PREMIUM TIMES, also showed that Lagos generated N1.77 trillion out of the combined N5.15 trillion.

The fact-checking team also rated

Mr Hamzat’s claim that Lagos was two metres below sea level as false. It said the state was a low-lying coastal area but was not below sea level.

Candidates differ over healthcare funding

On healthcare, the candidates proposed different ways to address funding shortages, improve hospital services and make treatment more accessible to residents.

The moderator raised concerns about Lagos’s health budget, noting that the state allocated between five and eight per cent of its annual budget to healthcare, below the 15 per cent target under the Abuja Declaration.

The candidates were asked how they would increase funding and ensure that allocations were released and properly spent.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour proposed establishing emergency response centres in all 245 wards, each equipped with two ambulances.

He said the centres would reduce the time residents spend moving between hospitals in search of beds, oxygen and other emergency services.

He also proposed preventive healthcare programmes to identify illnesses early and provide basic health education at the ward level. The centres, he said, would include wellness facilities where residents, particularly older people and pensioners, could exercise and receive guidance on healthy living.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour said he would increase healthcare funding towards 15 per cent of the state budget, improve doctors’ salaries, train support staff and introduce artificial intelligence to support diagnosis and healthcare delivery.

Mr Hamzat stated that his administration would expand health insurance coverage, increase hospital capacity and upgrade primary healthcare centres.

He said the Ilera Eko health insurance scheme currently covered about 1.4 million people and proposed extending coverage to one in every three Lagos residents.

He also cited ongoing hospital projects, including a 150-bed general hospital and the Massey Street children’s hospital, as part of efforts to increase capacity.

Mr Hamzat said Lagos had more than 300 primary healthcare centres, but only 87 were operating as flagship facilities. He proposed increasing the number to about 150 and expanding round-the-clock services so residents could access medical attention at any time.

He also proposed establishing a new university of medicine, with a target of producing up to 1,000 doctors.

However, he said increasing the number of trained doctors alone would not address the problem unless the government also improved hospital facilities and working conditions to retain medical professionals.

The state government has acknowledged the funding challenges. At a ministerial briefing in May 2026, Commissioner for Health Akin Abayomi said Lagos spent about eight per cent of its budget on health and faced an estimated N100 billion gap between available funding and projected healthcare needs.

The NDC candidate called for increased government spending on healthcare and education, proposing that their combined allocation should rise from about 15 per cent to 28 per cent of the state budget during his first term.

He also promised free maternal and child healthcare, including drugs and diagnostic tests.

Mr Doherty said some government hospitals provided consultations but required patients to obtain tests elsewhere and buy prescribed drugs themselves, making treatment unaffordable for many families.

He argued that free healthcare should cover essential treatment rather than depend mainly on insurance schemes. While acknowledging the role of health insurance in expanding coverage, he said the government should directly fund treatment for residents who could not afford medical expenses.

The PDP candidate said improving healthcare would require more investment in medical personnel, hospital equipment and pharmaceutical production.

He called for the training of more doctors and nurses, saying the available number of medical professionals and hospitals was inadequate for a state with an estimated population of 25 million.

He also proposed supporting local manufacturers of hospital beds, medical equipment and drugs.

Mr Doherty said reducing charges imposed on pharmaceutical manufacturers would encourage local production and make medicines more affordable.

He identified malaria, cancer, hypertension and HIV as health challenges requiring greater attention from the state.

World.title: 2027: APC chieftain laments 73% voter apathy in Aramoko
World.content:
By Rotimi Ojomoyela

ADO-EKITI — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and member of the President Bola Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, Engineer Atinuke Owolabi, has expressed concern over the low voter turnout in Aramoko-Ekiti during the 2023 presidential election, saying about 73 per cent of registered voters in the community did not participate.

Owolabi, who is also the convener of PBAT-MOB Aramoko Community Engagement, spoke during an APC voter education exercise and community engagement in Aramoko, Ekiti Central Senatorial District, over the weekend.

The programme, organised in support of the re-election bids of President Tinubu and Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, was held under the theme, “My Vote, My Voice”.

She also represents the South-West as a member of the North Central Development Commission.

Owolabi said voter education was essential to strengthening democracy, particularly in rural communities where inadequate information about electoral procedures could discourage participation or lead to invalid votes.

Presenting figures from the 2023 presidential election, she said Ekiti State had 988,923 registered voters, out of whom 315,058 were accredited, while 308,171 valid votes were recorded and 6,301 ballots were rejected.

She said available ward-level records for Aramoko I and Aramoko II showed a combined 17,426 registered voters, compared with 4,680 votes reportedly cast during the presidential election.

According to her, the figures indicated that approximately 12,746 registered voters did not participate, representing about 73 per cent of the electorate in the two wards.

She urged residents to improve their participation in future elections, stressing the need for the community to translate its voting strength into meaningful democratic engagement.

Owolabi said the exercise was designed to educate residents on voting procedures, encourage participation and reduce the number of rejected ballots.

The programme also featured the unveiling of a voter education handbook intended to guide residents on electoral processes, identification of polling units and the proper use of their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

She said: “I believe voter education is key. If we cannot completely eliminate rejected votes, we should at least be able to reduce them in Ekiti State, particularly in Aramoko, my community.

“We are here to sensitise our people on the correct way to vote. When they go to the polling units, they must ensure that they vote correctly.

“We have the population, and we have the voters. What is really lacking is adequate information. Our people need to understand the right way to vote.

“Today, we have unveiled a voter education handbook, which is a welcome development. Through this handbook, our people will be taught what elections are all about. They will understand how to identify their polling units and how to participate in the electoral process.”

She also urged residents to consider the 2023 election figures as a basis for improving participation in subsequent elections.

Meanwhile, the Regent of Aramoko-Ekiti, Princess Owolabi Adeyemi, acknowledged the efforts of President Tinubu and Bamidele in grassroots development.

She, however, appealed to the Federal Government to address the deplorable condition of roads in the community to ease the difficulties faced by residents and commuters.

World.title: Aba South establishes commercial farms to boost revenue, create jobs
World.content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA — Aba South Local Government Area of Abia State has established commercial poultry and piggery farms as part of efforts to boost its internally generated revenue (IGR), create jobs and equip residents with skills in animal husbandry.

The Executive Chairman of the council, Chief Obialo Anyanwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on his administration’s two-year achievements, explaining that the initiative was aimed at making the local government more financially self-reliant.

Anyanwu said his administration was exploring sustainable revenue sources to strengthen the council’s capacity to deliver services rather than depend entirely on external funding.

He explained that the farms would also serve as training centres where residents would acquire practical skills in animal farming, enabling them to establish their own businesses and employ others.

He said: “We don’t believe in all these 10kg of rice empowerment. What we want in Aba South is giving our people that level of empowerment that will make them self-sustaining and employ others. So, we’ll teach the techniques needed to succeed in the business.

“The three buildings in the poultry section are up, two are already roofed, and the staff quarters are at the lintel stage because it’s a proper farm and people must reside there.

“Possibly by the end of the year, everything will take off. So, we’re envisaging such a future. We, as the third tier of government, must stand for ourselves, and it has pushed us into doing commercial poultry and commercial pig farming.”

The chairman disclosed that the poultry farm occupies 14 plots of land, while the piggery farm covers seven plots.

He added that the projects would generate revenue for the council, create employment opportunities and provide practical agricultural training for residents, including staff of the council’s agriculture department.

On healthcare, Anyanwu said the council had established and equipped 22 Glycoster World Primary Healthcare Centres in partnership with the Abia State Government.

He said the facilities had been commissioned and made operational, adding that the council had also organised free medical tests and treatments for residents.

On education, the chairman said the council was supporting Governor Alex Otti’s free back-to-school programme through the distribution of 4,000 school bags to pupils in primary schools across the local government area.

He explained that the initial target was 10,000 beneficiaries but that the distribution would be carried out in phases after an enumeration exercise showed that the number of eligible pupils exceeded the target.

Anyanwu also disclosed that the council was partnering with the state government on primary school development, including the ongoing construction of a smart school along Etche Road.

He said the administration had equally invested in digital skills training, with more than 130 residents trained in three cohorts.

According to him, the first cohort graduated 50 participants, the second had 30, while the third produced another 50 graduates.

On road infrastructure, Anyanwu said the council commenced road grading shortly after he assumed office on November 4, 2024.

He disclosed that more than 20 kilometres of roads across the 12 wards were graded between late November 2024 and early January 2025, while another 28 kilometres were covered by the end of 2025.

The chairman commended security agencies in the area for their professionalism and commitment, saying Aba South had remained peaceful.

He identified the removal of individuals and companies allegedly operating unauthorised revenue collection arrangements as one of his administration’s major achievements.

“One of the biggest achievements we’ve made in this administration so far was the chasing out of one revenue vampire with one company called Chicotax out of the Aba South LGA. He has been doing this for several years, but this time around, we’ve arrested the situation, and we’ve moved on,” he said.

Anyanwu described the relationship between the council and the state government as cordial, commending Otti for supporting road infrastructure projects in Aba South.

He expressed optimism that ongoing and planned road projects would improve transportation and access to several communities in the council area.

He specifically mentioned the ongoing work on Obohia Road, which he said included a drainage system designed to channel floodwater from different parts of Aba into the river.

He also listed Umuebeke Road, Uratta Road and Old Express Road among the projects expected to improve road connectivity in the area.

The chairman said the projects, when completed, would improve access to communities and enable the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA) to extend its operations to previously inaccessible areas.

World.title: Trump admits his mass deportation policy was ‘too tough’
World.content:
Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

US President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was “too tough,” according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired Sunday.

Asked about his deportation policy, Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes”: “I think it was too tough…I think it might be too tough.”

The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later Sunday. It was recorded after the Republican Party’s heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday.

While Trump has won some domestic support for securing the US southern border, his administration’s aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism.

However, Trump on Friday appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff on Friday, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss.

Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year.

World.title: Fan rushed to hospital after stadium stand collapses during Bodo/Glimt match
World.content:
A fan of Norwegian football club Bodo/Glimt has been hospitalised after the away end partially collapsed during their team’s fixture at Tromso, police said on Sunday.

“Four people were confirmed to be involved, and one of them has been taken to the hospital,” the statement said.

The family of the hospitalised man told public broadcaster NRK that he had sustained fractured ribs.

The incident occurred shortly before the end of the first half of the match involving Bodo/Glimt, who are competing in the Champions League.

World.title: Obi’ll win presidential election by landslide — Ex-Rep, Nkole
World.content:
By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA—Former member of the House of Representatives, Uko Nkole, has predicted a landslide victory for the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, in the 2027 general elections.



Nkole, who is the NDC senatorial candidate for Abia North, said Obi’s economic management record, national appeal and popularity among youths positioned him to win the presidency.



He spoke during a political debate at the grand finale of the 2026 Press Week organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Abia State, in Umuahia.

He predicted the defeat of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), blaming its economic policies for the hardship facing Nigerians.

Nkole also vowed to unseat incumbent Abia North Senator, Orji Uzor Kalu, accusing him of failing to deliver meaningful development to the district.

He urged Kalu to support Obi’s presidential ambition rather than President Bola Tinubu, saying both politicians belonged to the same political generation.

“President Bola Tinubu is his mate. They were governors of the 1999 class. It’s very wrong for him to be clapping for his mate. The challenge all of us have today is how to produce a Nigerian President of Igbo extraction, which Obi represents,” he said.

Unveiling an eight-point development agenda, Nkole promised 20 town hall meetings annually across the five local government areas of Abia North, revival of 217 primary healthcare centres, intervention in 415 public schools, restoration of 15 regional water schemes and completion of abandoned federal projects.

He also pledged to attract a Federal Medical Centre, facilitate 1,000 federal jobs for youths within four years and pursue the establishment of the proposed Federal Polytechnic, Abiriba.

Meanwhile, the PDP senatorial candidate for Abia North, Jude Udeachara, promised to sponsor legislation compelling mining and construction companies to rehabilitate lands degraded by their operations.

He also pledged monthly accountability briefings to journalists, including disclosure of project costs, contractors and contract details.

The NDC House of Representatives candidate for Isuikwuato/Umunneochi, Evangeline Iwenjiora, also promised improved infrastructure, youth and women empowerment and quality representation.

Earlier, Chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel, Deacon Steve Oko, urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to consider engaging experienced journalists with proven integrity as ad-hoc electoral officials, particularly returning officers, in the 2027 elections.

He said journalists’ experience in observation, documentation and verification could strengthen electoral credibility.

Oko also demanded real-time transmission of polling unit results, improved electoral logistics and better security and insurance for journalists covering the elections.

He disclosed that the Chapel had trained more than 50 journalists at a two-day retreat on artificial intelligence, disinformation, fact-checking, election reporting and journalists’ safety.

Delivering the keynote address, Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Prof. Christopher Okoro, cautioned journalists against spreading fake news, urging them to deploy technology and artificial intelligence responsibly.

The Chapel also honoured Prof. Nnenna Oti, the Returning Officer in the 2023 Abia governorship election, for her conduct during the poll.

World.title: Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday
World.content:
Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, the Sultan of Sokoto and President General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA)

By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO – The Sultanate Council of Sokoto has called on Muslims across Nigeria to search for the new crescent moon of Jumada Assaniya 1448AH on Monday, November 9, 2026.

The directive was contained in a statement dated November 8, 2026, signed by Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu and made available to journalists on Sunday.

According to the statement, the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council identified Monday as the 29th day of Jumada al-Ula 1448AH and the appropriate date for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise.

The council urged Muslims across the country to actively participate in the exercise by looking out for the new crescent moon after sunset on Monday.

It specifically requested anyone who sights the crescent to promptly report the observation to the nearest District or Village Head for onward transmission to His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, CFR, mni, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA).

The council stressed the importance of timely and credible reports of confirmed sightings to enable the Sultan to make the appropriate religious announcement on the commencement of the new Islamic month.

It noted that the Sultan remains the recognised authority responsible for communicating the outcome of the moon-sighting exercise to Muslims across the country.

The announcement underscores the role of the Sultanate Council in coordinating Islamic religious affairs and guiding the Muslim Ummah on matters concerning the Islamic lunar calendar.

In a prayer, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu, Waziri and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council, asked Allah (SWT) to grant Muslims the guidance and strength to discharge the religious responsibility successfully.

The council also prayed for divine assistance and acceptance of the exercise, urging Muslims to approach the assignment with sincerity, vigilance and a strong sense of religious commitment.

World.title: Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico
World.content:
Barcelona’s players celebrate victory at the end of the Spanish league football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and FC Barcelona at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 8, 2026. Barcelona won 1-2. (Photo by Thomas COEX / AFP)

Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga.

The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind.

Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium.

The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in.

The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages.

Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal.

From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten.

At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal.

Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range.

The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second.

The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards.

Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears.

Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere.

Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak.

Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal.

The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead.

Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season.

Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break.

Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0.

Villarreal beat Getafe 2-0 to move eighth and Celta Vigo and Levante shared a goalless draw.

World.title: NTI managers to Tinubu, education minister: Review admission cancellation
World.content:
…Says decision can jeopardise academic future of more than 21,000 students

The National Teachers’ Institute (NTI) Centre Managers’ Forum has appealed to President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, to review the cancellation of the institute’s programmes and the 2026 admissions, warning that the decision could jeopardise the academic future of more than 21,000 students.

The forum, in an appeal signed by its National Chairman, Dr Tam Loveday Frank Jumbo, and National Secretary, Dr Mamuda Inuwa Doguwa, urged the Federal Government to allow affected students to complete their programmes while necessary regulatory reforms are undertaken.

The appeal followed an announcement by the Federal Ministry of Education on November 7, cancelling all admissions into NTI’s National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session over alleged regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations.

The ministry also directed the institute to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, stating that NTI was not authorised to award NCE and university degrees.

Reacting to the development, the Centre Managers’ Forum said it received the announcement with concern, particularly because thousands of students had already secured admission, registered for their programmes and participated in academic activities.

According to the forum, many of the affected students had attended physical and virtual lectures and sat for their first-semester examinations in August 2026, with some awaiting the release of their results.

It said the students enrolled in good faith, believing they were gaining admission into a legitimate, government-owned institution operating under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Education.

The forum noted that for more than 45 years, NTI had provided educational opportunities to Nigerians who, because of financial constraints, work commitments, family responsibilities and geographical barriers, could not easily access conventional universities and colleges of education.

It claimed that the institute had provided educational opportunities to more than one million Nigerians, contributing to teacher development, human capital development and access to higher education across the country.

The forum argued that students should not bear the consequences of institutional or administrative shortcomings beyond their control, particularly after making financial commitments and participating in academic activities organised by the institute.

It also expressed confidence in the current Director-General, Professor S.S. Daura, saying efforts under his leadership had restored hope among students.

While acknowledging the Federal Government’s commitment to improving educational standards and ensuring regulatory compliance, the forum appealed to the minister to adopt what it described as a more inclusive and compassionate approach to resolving the matter.

Specifically, it asked the ministry to reconsider the cancellation of the programmes and 2026 admissions, allowing affected students to complete their studies.

It also called for a review of NTI’s operations, admission procedures and academic activities to ensure compliance with established regulatory guidelines.

Other requests included transitional arrangements for students already admitted, registered, taught and assessed, as well as consultations with relevant stakeholders, including the Centre Managers’ Forum, to develop a sustainable solution.

The forum maintained that educational reforms should strengthen institutions and improve quality without abruptly terminating the aspirations of students who had relied on government-owned institutions.

“Our appeal is not against educational reforms or quality assurance. Rather, it is a call for fairness, justice, compassion and a carefully considered transition that does not sacrifice the future of thousands of Nigerians,” it said.

However, the Federal Ministry of Education had explained that the decision followed violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on September 12, 2025.

In a statement issued by its Director of Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, the ministry said NCE admissions must comply with the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).

It also directed the National Universities Commission (NUC) to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the discontinuation of NTI’s degree-awarding arrangements.

The ministry clarified that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), would be permitted.

However, in a measure to protect students already enrolled, the ministry said the NCCE would conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones.

It added that eligible students could complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements.

The ministry further stressed that NTI’s statutory mandate remained teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development.

It said the mandate also covered pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations.

The ministry urged prospective students, parents and the general public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before seeking admission or making payments.

World.title: Bandits Burn 11 Family Members to Death in Zamfara
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Eleven members of a family have been burnt to death in their home by suspected bandits at Gidan Taba village in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward of Maradun Local Government Area in Zamfara State.

The incident, which occurred last Saturday night, has thrown the entire community into mourning and fear.

Confirming the sad development, the spokesperson of the state Police Command, DSP Yazid Abubakar, said the attack was carried out by suspected bandits.

According to him, the armed group stormed the house and gathered the entire household in one room.

He said the bandits thereafter set the room ablaze, burning all the occupants to death.

It was gathered that the victims belonged to the family of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani.

Sani is said to be a member of the local vigilante group operating in the area.

He had reportedly denied the bandits freedom of operation in the troubled area.

The bandits were said to have decided to eliminate him and his entire family in retaliation for his resistance.

The Zamfara State Police Command spokesman said police operatives are on the trail of the assailants, adding that the police are currently working to restore normalcy in the affected village.

World.title: SSDC Moves to Rescue Bille Kingdom   from  Gas Seepage Threats
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The South-South Development Commission (SSDC) has delivered humanitarian relief materials to residents of Bille Kingdom in Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State following persistent gas seepage and methane emissions that have contaminated underground water sources, rivers, and local wells.

The intervention, initiated by the Commission’s Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Ms Usoro Akpabio, is aimed at alleviating the hardship imposed on residents by the environmental crisis that has disrupted livelihoods, threatened food security, and affected access to safe drinking water.

Leading the SSDC delegation to the affected community, the Executive Director, Social Services and Human Capital Development, Preye Aganaba, conveyed the Commission’s assurance that Bille would not be abandoned.

Akpabio, in a statement, described Bille as a significant economic hub in Rivers State and the South-South region, warning that the environmental emergency posed serious humanitarian and economic consequences.

“The plight of the people of Bille is of great concern to the Commission. Their recovery remains a priority, and we want to assure them that they will not be overlooked in our developmental agenda,” she said.

She disclosed that the Commission provided 86 categories of food and non-food items, including rice, beans, garri, noodles, cooking oils, mattresses, mosquito nets, wrappers, buckets, sanitary pads, and baby diapers.

According to her, the intervention aligns with President Bola Tinubu’s directive to the Commission to provide relief to vulnerable communities and accelerate development across the six South-South states.

Akpabio added that the SSDC’s response was designed to complement the efforts of Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, the Rivers State Emergency Management Agency, and the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA).

She pledged the Commission’s continued commitment to environmental protection, disaster resilience, sustainable infrastructure, and livelihood restoration across the region.

Speaking on behalf of the Bille Council of Chiefs, its Chairman, Chief Bennett Okpoke, commended the SSDC for responding to the community’s plight but urged the federal and state governments to address the root cause of the crisis.

He said residents had endured prolonged gas and methane seepage, with devastating effects on their water sources, livelihoods and daily activities.

Okpoke appealed to relevant environmental and regulatory agencies to urgently develop a lasting solution to the pollution, warning that the community’s health and economic survival were at stake.

Also speaking, the NEMA’s Head of Operations for Bayelsa and Rivers States, Dr Chidi Ogundu, said the agency had approached the SSDC over the emergency and commended the Commission for its swift intervention.

He disclosed that an Environmental Impact Assessment had been conducted, with findings indicating significant adverse effects on the community.

Describing the situation as a collective responsibility, Ogundu said: “An injury to one is an injury to all.”

He further revealed that NEMA’s technical team had commenced efforts to address the community’s potable water challenges and reduce residents’ exposure to potential health hazards.

The relief materials, provided on behalf of the SSDC’s managing director, board chairman and management, were formally handed over to the community through NEMA.

The delegation was received by the Bille Council of Chiefs, representing His Royal Majesty, King Igbikingeri Ngowari Cornelius Herbert, Agbaniye-Jike XVIII.

World.title: PEFTI Relaunched as Innovation Institute to Revolutionise Higher Education
World.content:
Sunday Okobi

The award-winning institute of higher education, Performing Arts, Entrepreneurship, Fashion and Technology Innovations (PEFTI), has been relaunched as PEFTI Innovation Institute to revolutionise technical and higher education in Nigeria, the management has said.

Established in 2004, PEFTI is accredited by the Federal Ministry of Education, through the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), to offer two-year National Diploma programmes in Business Administration, Mass Communication, Music Technology, Multimedia Technology, and Fashion Design.

According to the PEFTI Registrar, Abiola Adenuga Adimora, a United States IVLP alumnus, in a statement yesterday, “PEFTI is revolutionising higher education in Nigeria. Over the past decades, we have produced award-winning alumni, including T.G. Omori, Tunde Olaoye, Fido, and Mr. Macaroni, among countless others. PEFTI methodology is Practical, Project-Oriented Professional Training. We celebrate our students and welcome learners who are ready to lead in their industries.”

She added that PEFTI offers three-month professional courses in Business, Film, Fashion, Music, and Multimedia Technology.

PEFTI is also accredited by NBTE as a TVET Skill Training Centre, and its school’s facility will serve as an iDICE Creative Hub, an initiative of the Bank of Industry (BOI)

Adimora stated that PEFTI Innovation Institute is located in Ajao Estate, Isolo, Lagos State, adding that: “We don’t just give students an education and experiences that set them up for success in a career. We help them succeed in their career—to discover a field they’re passionate about and dare to lead it.”

The registrar added that through hands-on learning, creative projects, and industry-relevant experiences, PEFTI equips students with the skills, knowledge, and confidence to excel in their chosen careers, to become entrepreneurs, and contribute meaningfully to their industries and society at large.

“PEFTI is a vibrant Creative Hub, supported by a strong professional network that fosters collaboration, produces creative content, develops emerging talents, and hosts events that connect students, industry professionals, and the wider creative community,” she said.

World.title: Hamzat Felicitates TBG,  Advocates Stronger Public-Private Partnership
World.content:
The Deputy Governor of Lagos State and All Ptogressives Congress(APC) gubernatorial candidate, Dr. Kadir Obafemi Hamzat, has congratulated the Thursday Business Group (TBG) on its 10th anniversary, commending its vision and contributions to business development while advocating stronger public-private partnerships to accelerate Nigeria’s economic resurgence.

Hamzat, who was represented by the Lagos State Commissioner for Transportation, Mr Seun Osiyemi, spoke at the Group’s 10th Founders’ Day Dinner and Awards held in Lagos. The event attracted business leaders, professionals, traditional rulers and public office holders to discuss the theme, “Economic Resurgence in Nigeria: Enterprise, Tax Responsibility and Government’s Role.”

In his keynote address, Hamzat described enterprise as the engine of economic growth, stressing that government must focus on creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive through consistent policies, infrastructure development, transparent taxation and improved access to finance.

“Government has no business with running enterprises. At best, we should be partners with business, with government creating the enabling environment that allows businesses to create the prosperity we desire,” he stated.

On taxation, he described tax payment as a civic responsibility and an essential component of nation-building, while acknowledging concerns over multiple taxation. He emphasised that government must demonstrate accountability by translating tax revenues into tangible benefits, particularly in infrastructure, power, security and essential social services.

“Tax is not a penalty; it is the subscription fee for civilisation,” he declared.

Outlining his economic vision for Lagos, Hamzat highlighted plans to grow annual investment from N1 trillion to N5 trillion by 2031, support the development of over one million MSMEs, establish four industrial parks and strengthen access to finance through the proposed N10 billion LASMECO facility. He also advocated harmonising government levies and expanding the tax net rather than increasing the burden on existing taxpayers.

In his goodwill message, former Governor of Lagos State and former Minister of Works and Housing, Mr Babatunde Raji Fashola, SAN, commended TBG for sustaining a platform for constructive business conversations and collective prosperity over the past decade.

“Among the many things young men could engage in on a Thursday, you have chosen to discuss progress and collective prosperity,” he remarked.

Fashola also underscored the relationship between taxation and democratic accountability, noting that citizens must be able to debate who pays taxes and how public revenue is utilised. He urged the Group to make its next decade one of greater innovation and leadership.

Earlier, TBG Guv’nor, Honourable Femi Adeyeye, acknowledged the contributions of the group’s founders, trustees, past Guvnors and members in building the organisation over the last ten years.

“Ten years ago, our founders had a vision to bring business-minded people together around a common purpose. Today, we are proud of how far that vision has brought us,” he said, adding that the next decade would be defined by greater collaboration, stronger businesses and lasting impact.

A major highlight of the evening was the presentation of awards to distinguished individuals for their contributions across the public and private sectors.

The event also featured an enterprise development intervention by the Kajola Foundation, which awarded N10 million to 14 beneficiaries of its Enterprise Bootcamp to strengthen their businesses, improve productivity and support sustainable growth.

The intervention reinforced the evening’s central message that Nigeria’s economic resurgence requires not only sound government policies and corporate investment but also practical support for entrepreneurs and small businesses.

As TBG enters its second decade, the Group reaffirmed its commitment to fostering business collaboration, responsible enterprise and initiatives that translate constructive dialogue into measurable economic and social impact.

World.title: CONCERNS OVER GROWING DEBT PROFILE
World.content:
The spate of borrowing is excessive

Nigeria’s burgeoning public debt stock has become a subject of intense debate within and outside the country. Multilateral institutions and corporate analysts have been unrelenting in their call for restraint on the level of borrowing, particularly under the present administration. According to the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026 released last week, Nigeria’s external debt stock increased to $145.02 billion at the end of 2025, representing a 6.6 per cent rise from the previous year. Since Nigeria’s external debt in 2015 stood at $83.21 billion, the latest figure represents an increase of about $61.8bn over the 10-year period, highlighting the growing scale of indebtedness.

While making explicit reference to excessive borrowing, former President Olusegun Obasanjo said generations are being increasingly mortgaged. “How did we get ourselves into this trap?” he asked. But amid these concerns, the federal government is defending its reduced request of $7.707 billion (approximately N10.79 trillion) to part-finance the 2026 budget deficit. “The objective is to increasingly direct new borrowing towards productive capital investment, while maintaining fiscal discipline, reducing financing pressures and ensuring that public debt translates into measurable economic value,” said President Bola Tinubu who has defended the decision. “Nigeria borrows to invest in roads, ports, rail and power that will generate growth, revenue and jobs for decades.”

Over the years, Nigerians have been fed with a steady diet that loans will impact positively on the economy and generate stronger growth. Indeed, borrowing is not essentially bad. And there is no doubt that Nigeria needs some borrowing to fix infrastructural and other development needs. However, public debt has been a dangerous drain, costly to sustain, and leaving all with a sense of bewilderment. In several cases, loans have translated to short-term consumption, rather than productive economic value. Public debt obligations have increasingly crippled fiscal space for many essential social services like public health and education.

It is concerning that public debt has climbed astronomically. According to the Debt Management Office (DMO), the debt stock further rose to about N167 trillion by mid-2026. The deal in the offing will only heighten the debt burden. Besides, the states and the FCT, many of which are also implicated in the current effort, are constantly under fiscal stress as debt services rose to uncomfortable levels, while recurrent expenditure is almost crowded out. But even more harrowing is that interest payments are money diverted from roads, schools, hospitals, electricity or social protection.

The World Bank reported recently that interest payments hit N7.7 trillion in the first half of 2026, an amount that far exceeded reported federal revenues. Even though the federal government discounted the figures, arguing that part of the debt was induced by subnational governments, there is no doubt that the ratio is still elevated. This is despite the marginal progress in increased revenue as well as in the current tax-to-GDP ratio.

Thus, though the federal government has always used infrastructure as an alibi for the rising borrowing, there are concerns about inefficient loan utilisation and poor debt management practices. Regrettably, whether the loans are well applied or not, meeting debt obligations is a given. The federal government should therefore listen to the wise counsel from within and outside the country to halt the journey to another debt trap.

Even if the now familiar refrain by government officials that “Nigeria does not have a debt problem,” is to be taken on its face value, we believe the wise counsel of Benjamin Franklin that “he who goes a borrowing goes a sorrowing,” should provide a useful guide. As it is for individuals, so it is for nations. Nigeria must stay within disciplined borrowing limits.

World.title: ADC AND FATE OF THE OPPOSITION
World.content:
For the African Democratic Congress, one courtroom after another is providing a gripping battleground in its quest to unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress.

Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, a Federal High Court sitting in Abuja has sacked the National Working Committee (NWC) of the party, putting its chances of victory at the next general elections in grave jeopardy.

The judgment has affected the primaries conducted by the National Working Committee led by David Mark, effectively stripping former vice president Atiku Abubakar of his nomination as its presidential candidate.

Nigerian politics has always provided plenty examples of ruthlessness. There used to be a lot of bloodshed in politics just after Nigeria returned to democracy in 1999. These days there isn’t as much bloodshed, but all manner of underhand tricks still go into our politics. Chief among these is the ruling party using all means available to disrupt the opposition.

From the moment the APC contentiously won the 2023 general elections and started failing almost immediately, it knew it would face an uphill task in the 2027 general elections. Its worst fears appeared to be confirmed when the ADC was formed, initially bringing together Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, the two runners-up in the 2023 election.

Once the ADC was formed, it was clear that the APC was panicking, and the attacks began almost immediately. Most of the attacks were generated from within the ADC, albeit by people largely believed to have been planted by the APC.

These attacks and the lurid promise of more to come tied into the chief reasons Peter Obi left the ADC for the NDC. Now, with this setback just months to the election itself, Nigeria’s flailing opposition faces a fight to give Nigerians options that have nothing to do with a government that has failed to meet the aspirations of Nigerians at all levels.

The ADC’s travails betray the pitfalls of playing opposition politics in Nigeria. Many Nigerians lack the mental fortitude to navigate the treacherous labyrinth of opposition politics, while many other Nigerians are available for peanuts to be used as pawns and saboteurs.

Despite the considerable political weight of Atiku, the ADC is running out of time to mount the kind of formidable challenge that can unsettle the ruling APC. Nigerians must also brace themselves for what is to come. It is now clear even to the blind that the battle to save the soul of Nigeria from the ruling APC will run through courtrooms on its way to going down to the wire. The fact that many Nigerians no longer trust the judiciary only adds to the growing intrigue.

But there is hope. Despite the many woes of the ADC, the NDC, where Peter Obi is the presidential candidate, offers Nigerians hope. As long as Peter Obi, a politician of rare class and grace, who is effectively a throwback to the good old days when Nigeria had selfless leaders willing to die in her service, runs, Nigerians will retain the choice to choose between darkness and light.

Ike Willie-Nwobu is a policy practitioner and social thinker. ikewilly9@gmail.com

World.title: Nwankwo, Bright Sprint to Double Gold  in Youth Olympic Games
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

Nigeria’s teenage sprinters, Rosemary Nwankwo and Gift Bright, yesterday emerged fastest male and female athletes of the ongoing 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

In the girls’ 100m event of the track & field, 17-year-old Nwankwo who is Team Nigeria Captain led the field to hit the finish line first in 11.16secs personal best time. Nwankwo left the silver and bronze for United Arab Emirates’ Arwa Ali (11.41) with Qatar’s Dana Salem picking the bronze with 11.48.

Nwankwo is the third Nigerian girl to win the Youth Olympic Games 100m gold, following in the footsteps of Josephine Omaka at the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010 and Rosemary Chukwuma in Argentina in 2018.

Nwankwo’s winning time came a little above the legal wind reading of 2.0m/s limit for record purposes. Her wind reading was +2.4 metres per second. It however did little to diminish the significance of her performance for Nigeria.

In the boys’ 100m, 15-year-old Bright completed the sprint double for Nigeria. He gave an outstanding performance in the boys’ final to win in a personal best of 10.28 seconds.

His gold was the first for Team Nigeria boys in the Youth Olympic Games 100m sprint.

China’s Zhang Hangyu finished second in 10.57, while Poland’s Szymon Dolega took bronze in 10.61.

Unlike the women’s final, Bright’s performance was achieved under legal wind conditions of +1.7m/s, making his 10.28-second mark eligible for recognition as a personal best.

It also takes Nigeria’s athletics gold medal tally at the Youth Olympic Games to five, further strengthening the country’s historical connection with the sprint events.

Nigeria also collected three silver medals at the 2018 edition, through Alaba Akintola in the men’s 100m and Ineh Oritsemeyiwa in the triple jump, among others.

Meanwhile, the Director General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Hon. Bukola Olopade, has urged Team Nigeria to surpass the country’s previous best performance at the Dakar 2026 Games coming to a close on November 12.

Yesterday, Ugoh Tejiri, advanced to the 400m semifinal event. Five athletes are representing Team Nigeria in the track and field event at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Some other athletes who had concluded their events have returned home from the Games.

World.title: 12 Governors Take Centre Stage in National Grassroots Sports Summit Countdown
World.content:
With barely 10 days to the National Grassroots Sports Development Summit 2026, attention is shifting to the critical role of state governments in transforming Nigeria’s sporting future.

A major highlight of the November 18–19 gathering at the Banquet Hall, State House, Presidential Villa, Abuja, will be the Governors’ Round Table, themed “Sub-National Leadership in Grassroots Sports Implementation.”

The session will spotlight 12 state governors in discussions aimed at moving grassroots sports development beyond policy declarations into practical implementation across communities.

Governors featured in the proposed session include AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq (Kwara), Hope Uzodimma (Imo), Douye Diri (Bayelsa), Abdullahi Sule (Nasarawa), Lucky Aiyedatiwa (Ondo), and Babajide Sanwo-Olu (Lagos).

Others are Babagana Zulum (Borno), Hyacinth Alia (Benue), Alex Otti (Abia), Peter Mbah (Enugu), Monday Okpebholo (Edo), and Uba Sani (Kaduna).

The initiative recognises that sustainable sporting excellence cannot be achieved through federal interventions alone, particularly when thousands of talented youngsters depend on facilities, competitions and development opportunities within their states.

According to the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Grassroots Sports Development, Hon. Adeyinka Anthony Adeboye, state governments remain indispensable partners in building an effective national talent-development structure.

The round table will examine school sports revival, community infrastructure, funding mechanisms, public-private partnerships and stronger collaboration between state and local governments.

It will also explore how states can establish measurable sporting development programmes capable of surviving changes in political leadership.

The summit, themed “Creating a New Pathway for Sustainable Grassroots Sports Development,” is designed to produce actionable recommendations for expanding sporting opportunities across Nigeria’s 774 local government areas.

The Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) serves as technical partner.

As preparations intensify, organisers believe the Governors’ Round Table could provide the necessary political commitment to translate national sporting ambitions into visible opportunities for young Nigerians.

For the summit, the message is straightforward: the next generation of Nigerian champions will emerge from communities, but their opportunities must be built through deliberate leadership and investment.

Geordin Hill-Lewis shows off his weight loss. Images via IG

Democratic Alliance (DA) leader and Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis is on a path to a healthier lifestyle, showing off visible weight loss at a voter station this week.

GEORDIN HILL-LEWIS ON WEIGHT LOSS
