World.title: Lemonal stevedore slapped with additional charge of damage to property, allowed to remain on previous bail
World.content:
Lemonal stevedore slapped with additional charge of damage to property, allowed to remain on previous bail

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Twenty-seven-year-old Jerry Malique August, a stevedore of Lemonal Village, appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, November 6, 2026, where he was charged with damage to property in connection with an incident for which he had previously been charged with aggravated assault.

August appeared before a magistrate in Court #5, represented by attorney Oscar Selgado, and pleaded not guilty to the new charge.

Prosecutors allege that on August 24, 2026, in Bermudian Landing Village, August damaged a four-door Chevrolet Cruze valued at $3,000.

During the arraignment, the magistrate raised the issue of bail, prompting Selgado to explain that his client had already secured High Court bail in connection with an aggravated assault charge arising from the same incident.

Selgado argued that requiring August to obtain bail again would be unfair, particularly since both charges originated from the same circumstances.

The prosecutor agreed with the submission, and August was allowed to remain on his existing bail without having to secure a new bail arrangement.

August had previously been remanded to the Belize Central Prison following his arraignment on the aggravated assault charge before successfully obtaining bail through the High Court.

His next court appearance is scheduled for November 13, 2026, when he is expected to receive disclosure in relation to both charges.

World.title: ‘Our lives were shattered’: Family of slain police officer Arsenio Cus delivers emotional statement as Khris Rosado awaits sentencing
World.content:
‘Our lives were shattered’: Family of slain police officer Arsenio Cus delivers emotional statement as Khris Rosado awaits sentencing

By Breaking Belize News Staff: An emotional victim impact statement from the sister of Police Constable Arsenio Cus brought the devastating consequences of his death into focus in the High Court on Friday, November 6, 2026, as businessman Khris Rosado continued to await sentencing for the fatal traffic accident that claimed the officer’s life.

Rosado, the owner of Thirsty Thursday nightclub, previously pleaded guilty to causing death by careless conduct in connection with the July 28, 2025 collision on the Philip Goldson Highway.

During Friday’s proceedings before Justice Derick Sylvester, Cus’s sister, Paulina Cus, described the profound grief and emotional trauma her family has endured since losing her brother more than a year ago.

“Our lives were shattered. His death left a void that altered our future,” she told the court, describing how the tragedy had changed their family forever.

She recalled how her brother was always willing to help his family, including providing financial assistance during the COVID-19 lockdowns.

Paulina also spoke about the trauma of seeing her brother’s lifeless body in his police uniform and the painful experience of identifying him for a post-mortem examination.

“Do you know what it was to identify your own brother for a post-mortem?” she asked.

She described suffering flashbacks and lasting emotional distress, while reflecting on the birthdays, holidays and family gatherings that her brother would never again share with his loved ones, including his daughters.

The emotional testimony also appeared to affect Rosado, who was visibly moved as he listened to the family’s account of their loss.

Justice Sylvester subsequently adjourned sentencing until Monday, November 9, 2026.

As previously reported by Breaking Belize News, Rosado pleaded guilty on June 16, 2026, to causing death by careless conduct following the fatal collision between Miles 6 and 7 on the Philip Goldson Highway.

Cus, 38, of Silver Creek Village, was riding his motorcycle from Ladyville toward Belize City when a vehicle entered his lane and struck him, causing severe injuries. He subsequently died from multiple blunt force traumatic injuries.

Police later located Rosado at his Ladyville residence, where investigators found a damaged 2009 Honda Ridgeline pickup truck believed to have been involved in the collision.

Forensic testing subsequently linked blood recovered from the vehicle to the deceased officer.

Rosado’s sentencing has been postponed several times since his guilty plea, including an October 1 adjournment.

The family now awaits Monday’s proceedings, when Justice Sylvester is expected to deliver his sentence.

World.title: Garrick Hemmans remains behind bars as firearm assault trial set for March 2027
World.content:
Garrick Hemmans remains behind bars as firearm assault trial set for March 2027

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Thirty-five-year-old Garrick Hemmans, also known as “Tamalito,” remains on remand at the Belize Central Prison after appearing in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, November 6, 2026, in connection with allegations that he fired several shots at a man in August.

Hemmans, who remains unrepresented, appeared before a Senior Magistrate in Court #2, where he was provided with 19 pages of disclosure and 12 photographs as evidence in the case.

The magistrate advised Hemmans to familiarize himself with the disclosed material and prepare for his trial, which has been scheduled for March 10 and 11, 2027.

As previously reported by Breaking Belize News, Hemmans was arraigned on August 28, 2026, on a charge of aggravated assault with a firearm upon 32-year-old technician Emory Williams. He pleaded not guilty and was denied bail due to the firearm-related nature of the offence.

The charge stems from a shooting incident on Rio Bravo Crescent in Belize City on August 25, 2026.

According to police, Williams was standing outside a residence around 7:28 p.m. when a maroon Nissan Murano approached from the direction of Tapir Street.

Williams alleged that Hemmans, who was seated in the front passenger seat, pulled out a firearm and fired several shots in his direction.

Fearing for his life, Williams reportedly ran behind a concrete fence and escaped without injury. The vehicle then sped away toward Fabers Road Extension.

Police processed the scene and recovered two expended 9mm Aguila shells and a bullet fragment.

Investigators subsequently located the Nissan Murano parked outside a residence on Jimmy Dyer Street, where another expended 9mm shell was reportedly discovered on the front passenger seat.

The vehicle was impounded, and Hemmans was detained later that night before being formally charged.

Hemmans remains on remand pending trial.

World.title: Devaun Garcia, previously freed of murder charge, granted $6,000 High Court bail in ammunition case
World.content:
Devaun Garcia, previously freed of murder charge, granted $6,000 High Court bail in ammunition case

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Twenty-one-year-old Devaun Garcia, who previously walked free from a murder charge after the prosecution discontinued its case, has been granted $6,000 bail by the High Court in connection with the alleged possession of three live rounds of ammunition.

Garcia appeared before Justice Candace Nanton on Friday, November 6, 2026, represented by attorney David McKoy, who argued that his client deserved bail, particularly since his two co-accused had already been released.

The prosecution raised no objection to bail, and Justice Nanton granted Garcia bail of $6,000, with two sureties of $3,000 each, subject to several conditions.

Garcia must report to the Raccoon Street Police Station every Monday and Friday, observe a curfew between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m., surrender his travel documents and refrain from contacting prosecution witnesses. He is also prohibited from leaving Belize without permission from the High Court.

The charges stem from an August 2 incident on Caesar Ridge Road in Belize City, where Garcia, along with 19-year-old Esmond Austin and 19-year-old Isani Conorquie, allegedly possessed three live 9mm Aguila rounds without a firearm licence.

According to police, officers responding to reports of an abandoned vehicle near the Yabra Bridge discovered a damaged black Ford Escape. During a search of the vehicle and surrounding area, officers reportedly recovered three live rounds of ammunition.

Police further allege that Garcia attempted to interfere with the investigation by grabbing ammunition from the vehicle and throwing it toward a nearby canal. The ammunition was subsequently recovered, and Garcia was additionally charged with obstruction.

All three men appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on August 3 and were initially remanded to the Belize Central Prison.

Garcia has previously faced several serious criminal allegations. In April 2025, he and George Hyde were freed from a murder charge involving the 2021 killing of 18-year-old Eaton Thompson of Mahogany Heights after the prosecution entered a nolle prosequi when its main witness could not be located.

In February 2026, Breaking Belize News reported that Garcia was remanded on firearm and ammunition charges following an incident in which police allegedly used drone surveillance to track a suspect who discarded a loaded 9mm pistol. Garcia had also previously secured bail in connection with an armed robbery allegation involving the BelChina Bridge.

Garcia maintains his innocence in the latest ammunition case, claiming that the bullets were planted by police.

His next scheduled appearance in the Magistrate’s Court is December 9, 2026.

World.title: Ector Soler to stand trial for manslaughter in fatal Ladyville motorcycle collision
World.content:
Ector Soler to stand trial for manslaughter in fatal Ladyville motorcycle collision

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Twenty-nine-year-old Ector Danielo Soler has been committed to stand trial in the High Court for manslaughter by negligence in connection with a fatal motorcycle collision that claimed the life of 40-year-old Celia Josefina Carballo Pleitez De Lazaro in May 2025.

Soler, a maintenance worker of Airport Plaza and resident of Ladyville, appeared unrepresented before the Chief Magistrate in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, November 6, 2026, where his preliminary inquiry concluded through a paper committal.

He was informed that his case would proceed to the January 2027 session of the High Court, expected to commence in mid-January.

As previously reported by Breaking Belize News, Soler was arraigned on September 26, 2025, on three indictable traffic offences: manslaughter by negligence, causing death by careless conduct, and driving without due care and attention.

The charges stem from a collision on May 25, 2025, between Miles 9 and 10 on the Philip Goldson Highway in Ladyville.

According to police investigations, 24-year-old Francisco Cortez was travelling southbound on a green Lifan motorcycle with his common-law wife, Celia, riding as a passenger.

The couple had reportedly stopped to purchase food near the Lord’s Bank junction and were returning to their home on Baltimore Road.

As Cortez approached the intersection with Marage Road around 8:00 p.m., he reportedly activated his left indicator and slowed down to make a turn.

Police allege that a red Ducati Monster motorcycle driven by Soler collided with the rear of Cortez’s motorcycle, throwing all three individuals onto the pavement.

Cortez and Soler sustained injuries, while Celia, a Guatemalan national, was transported to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital, where she was pronounced dead on arrival.

Following an investigation, the case file was submitted to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, which directed police to charge Soler.

Soler was initially granted bail of $7,000 following his September 2025 arraignment.

He will now face trial in the High Court, where the prosecution will be required to prove its case.

World.title: 19-year-old charged in $89,900 Burrell Boom home invasion granted $8,000 High Court bail
World.content:
19-year-old charged in $89,900 Burrell Boom home invasion granted $8,000 High Court bail

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Nineteen-year-old Adam Abraham Reynolds, accused of participating in a violent home invasion in Burrell Boom Village in which a businessman was tied up at gunpoint and robbed of nearly $90,000 in cash and valuables, has been granted bail by the High Court.

Reynolds, a labourer of Vista Del Mar, Ladyville, appeared before Justice Candace Nanton on Friday, November 6, 2026, after spending 16 days on remand at the Belize Central Prison.

His attorney, Norman Rodriguez, successfully applied for bail after the prosecution, representing the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, raised no objection.

Justice Nanton granted Reynolds bail in the sum of $8,000, with two sureties of $4,000 each, subject to several conditions.

Reynolds must report to the Burrell Boom Police Station every Friday, surrender his travel documents, refrain from contacting the complainant directly or indirectly, and remain at least 100 yards away from him. He must also attend all scheduled court appearances and avoid being arrested and charged with any new offences while on bail.

As previously reported by Breaking Belize News, Reynolds was charged with aggravated burglary following an October 14 home invasion at El Chiclero Resort in Burrell Boom Village.

Police allege that four men entered the residence of a 53-year-old businessman around 4:50 a.m., assaulted him, restrained him with duct tape and ransacked his home.

The intruders reportedly escaped with $30,000 in cash, gold chains valued at $12,000, electronic equipment and a 2017 Toyota Rush SUV valued at $45,000. The total value of the stolen property was estimated at $89,900.

Police subsequently located the stolen SUV in Santa Familia Village, Cayo District, on October 15. Investigators allege that Reynolds was inside the vehicle when officers approached, but he sped away before crashing and abandoning it.

Reynolds later surrendered to police in the presence of an attorney on October 19 and was arraigned the following day.

His next court appearance is scheduled for December 9, 2026.

Reynolds remains accused of aggravated burglary and has not been convicted.

World.title: Belize Zoo becomes a classroom for young conservationists
World.content:
Belize Zoo becomes a classroom for young conservationists

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Students from St Martin de Porres School traded their classroom for the Belize Zoo last week, spending a morning learning about conservation through games, interactive booths and hands on activities.

The event took place ahead of the evening celebration of Voices of the Corridor, which marked the completion of a key link in the Maya Forest Corridor.

Students explored aquatic ecosystems with the Savanna Field Station and the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS). They learned about the work of conservation rangers and field enforcement with WCS and Monkey Bay Wildlife Sanctuary, and got a closer look at biodiversity monitoring through camera trapping and bird observation.

Other booths focused on the dangers of fire and how teams protect the Maya Forest Corridor, as well as the role of sustainable agriculture in keeping landscapes healthy. Those activities were led by WCS, the Belize Maya Forest Trust, the Foundation for Wildlife Conservation, the Savanna Field Station and the Ministry of Natural Resources, Petroleum and Mining.

Organizers said the day gave students an introduction to the people, knowledge and daily work behind conservation in Belize.

World.title: Happy birthday, Shyne: Belize’s comeback king turns 48
World.content:
Happy birthday, Shyne: Belize’s comeback king turns 48

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Today, Belizean rapper and former politician Moses “Shyne” Barrow turns 48.

Like him or hate him, few Belizeans have lived a story quite like his.

Born in Belize City on November 8, 1978, Shyne grew up in Brooklyn, New York, and burst onto the hip hop scene in the late 1990s with Bad Boy Records. His debut album went platinum and made him one of the most talked about young voices in the music industry.

Then it all came crashing down. Shyne was convicted in connection with a 1999 New York nightclub shooting and spent close to a decade in prison. After his release, he was deported to Belize in 2009.

Many would have given up. Shyne didn’t.

He rebuilt his life at home, entered politics and in 2020 won the Mesopotamia seat in Belize City. He went on to become Leader of the UDP and Leader of the Opposition. Even after losing his seat in the 2025 general election, he has kept pushing forward.

This year, Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso declared April 25, 2026 as “Shyne Day” in Brooklyn and presented him with the Key to Brooklyn. He has also told his story in the Hulu documentary The Honorable Shyne, carrying Belize’s name to audiences around the world.

Happy birthday, Shyne.

World.title: JPL new boys Tru-Juice beat champions Portmore to retake lead
World.content:
Tyrone Mullings of Tru Juice FC shields the ball from a defender in Jamaica Premier League action. (Photo: Instagram/Fada_Mullings)

ST CATHERINE, Jamaica – Debutants Tru-Juice FC handed Portmore United their first loss of the Legend Jamaica Premier League season, holding off the defending champions 2-1 at Ferdie Neita Park on Sunday.

It is a fourth straight win for Tru-Juice as they raced to 20 points atop the JPL table, two more than second-placed Waterhouse FC who will play on Monday evening, with Racing United and Montego bay United tied on 16 points, two more than Mount Pleasant FA who beat Tivoli Gardens 2-1 to open their new facility in St Ann.

Alex Marshall gave Tru-Juice the lead in the 41st minute with his second goal of the season, while Tyrone Mullings scored his league leading eighth goal in the 60th minute to double the lead.

Marques Reid scored for Portmore United in the 68th minute but they were unable to close the gap any further and stayed in eighth place on 10 points.

Montego Bay United came from two goals down to play out a 2-2 draw against 12th place Molynes United at Jarrett Park, extending their winless run to four games. Tyrique Wilson gave Molynes the lead in the fifth minute and Rashawn Livingston added a second in the 10th but Jourdain Fletcher in the 28th minute and Devontae Campbell in the 40th minute cancelled the lead.

Molynes, taking orders for the first time from new coach Anthony Patrick, and who had lost their two previous games, got off to a fast start and were rewarded when Wilson’s free kick from about 22 yards went under the MBU wall and beat goalkeeper Davonnie Burton at his right post.

Livingston doubled the lead when he finished off a good move with a low hard shot from the right side into the far corner of the MBU goal.

Richardo Ramsey, who replaced Javon Gordon after 25 minutes, set up MBU’s first goal when he blocked a pass from a Molynes defender and Fletcher was given a chance to run at the goal and beat goalkeeper Jason Belfon and cut the deficit in the 28th minute.

Campbell brought the home team level when he dribbled from about 40 yards and gave Belfon no chance from close range.

Fletcher should have scored a third for MBU but his volley from inside the 18-yard box was wide of the target.

MBU dominated the game in the second half but just failed to get the winner with Ramsey redirecting a low hard cross over the cross bar from about a yard out late in the game.

Mount Pleasant opened their new facility with a come-from-behind win over Tivoli Gardens who took the lead in the 23rd minute through Mickel Graham.

Warner Brown equalised in the 53rd minute and Nickalia Fuller came off the bench to score the winner in the 70th minute.

Dunbeholden FC scored a late equaliser to get a 1-1 draw against Treasure Beach at the STETHS Sports Complex in Santa Cruz.

Daniel Hardy gave Treasure Beach the lead in the 74th minute but Nevaun Turner scored late, in time added, to give his team a share of the points.

Cavalier FC led Humble Lion 1-0 in their game at Effortville when it was called off with 15 minutes to be played due to heavy rain,

Sunday’s results

Humble Lion vs Cavalier FC- called off prematurely

Montego Bay United-2, Molynes United-2

Mount Pleasant FA-2, Tivoli Gardens FC-1

Portmore United-1, Tru-Juice FC-2

Treasure Beach FC-1, Dunbeholden FC-1

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Family seeking help to locate missing ‘mentally-challenged’ woman
World.content:
Rushelle Gordon

ST JAMES, Jamaica — A St James family is seeking the public’s help in locating a relative who has gone missing.

The missing woman is 36-year- old Rushelle Gordon, fondly called “Neeky”, who has been missing since Thursday, November 5.

Reports are that the woman and her mother were travelling in a taxi along Orange Street in the vicinity of Paradise Row when the vehicle stopped to allow two passengers to get off.

The woman had to come off to allow the passengers off. However, when the passengers came off, the driver drove off without the woman.

The car went a distance before her mother managed to disembark just around the corner and by the time she returned to the area where her daughter was, she was missing.

The daughter is nonverbal and, according to her family, has mental challenges which impacts her decision making.

She is dark complexion, medium built and is 5ft 6inches tall.

Information coming forward is that she was last seen in the Railway Lane/market area of Montego Bay after family members showed images of her in the area.

The police have been alerted and are actively trying to locate the woman.

World.title: Armed gangs backing squatters
World.content:
An aerial view of Flamingo Beach, Trelawny, where some of the land has been overrun by squatters, stalling a proposed development that includes resort and entertainment facilities in addition to a residential component.

Well-known attorney Gordon Brown says armed gang members from outside the community are thwarting his six-year-long effort to curb squatting on sections of 167 acres of land he owns in Flamingo Beach, Trelawny. Even a private security firm, he said, has refused the job of protecting the property from being further overrun.

Brown has submitted plans to the National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA) and the Trelawny Municipal Corporation (TMC) for an integrated development that includes resort and entertainment facilities in addition to a residential component, but he is unable to proceed as the land is littered with structures at various stages of construction.

In his view, apart from the TMC, which has publicly expressed concern about the stalled development, little has been done by State agencies to help him with his battle.

“Whilst I cannot say exactly how many acres have been squatted upon, what is unequivocal is that, since 2020, both personally and through the several attorneys who have assisted, I have made assiduous efforts to contain the festering squatting problem,” Brown said in a written response to the Jamaica Observer’s Real Estate on the Rock.

“In the supervening five years since filing suit I have respected the rule of law and complied with all orders of the court. Regrettably, my experience has proven yet again that, in our nation, those who abide by the law and show restraint are met with contempt or indifference. Those who flout it are given safe harbour by the authorities, especially if muscular action is visited upon them,” he added.

He listed a litany of failed attempts to arrest squatting taking place on the land, starting with his lawyers’ appeal to NEPA in early May 2020 to use its powers to “require the demolition of all illegal structures on the property”. He said NEPA posted warnings on all the structures on the site, but they were ignored and the squatting continued unabated.

According to Brown, in mid-January 2021, his attorneys served all the squatters with notices to quit, referencing NEPA’s May 2020 warning. In February, he said, his lawyers wrote to the superintendent of police for Trelawny, alerting him that his team may be needed if the squatters got rowdy after being served with notices to leave the property. Then in March 2021 he tried to hire private security to patrol and protect the land in an effort to move the process along.

“They carried out investigations and declined to accept the assignment, as their checks revealed the credible presence of armed gang members from other communities who were in place to resist any efforts to impede the illegal construction,” said Brown.

He said his lawyers then appealed to the commissioner of police, in late March 2021, alerting him to “rampant suspected criminality” in the area and the impact it was having on his property.

“This was copied to several parties, including the chief of defence staff, member of parliament and others, but we received no response, save from the TMC,” said Brown.

“Early April 2021 I met with the TMC to present the estate’s case and its need for coordinated action by the municipality and the police to curtail and demolish the structures. Subsequent to a meeting with the deputy superintendent of works of the TMC on-site, the property caretaker was ambushed by armed thugs who warned him not to erect the signage that we had agreed with the TMC should be put in place to advise the squatters of imminent action,” he added.

Brown then sought help from the courts, filing a suit in May 2021 in which he named all the then-known squatters

— about 10 of them

— and provided a “generic description” of a handful of others who were not known. In the suit, he sought an order for possession of the property. According to Brown, he was “granted an injunction restraining the squatters from damaging the site’s ecology, carrying out further construction activity upon the premises, and other relief”.

However, that did nothing to rein in the squatters, some of whom claim to own the land they occupy.

“Since that time there has been an explosion in the number of occupants. The injunction has been renewed pending final determination of the matter by the court. The occupants have falsely claimed that they have been in occupation of the premises for a period that would give them a possessory title to the parts of the premises occupied by them, but produced no evidence to support their claim. I have tendered video, aerial and geospatial evidence of the state of the premises as of the date of the court action [and before] which prove their claims untenable,” said Brown.

In explaining his claim to the land, he said he was the administrator of the estate of the late Carl Fei, an American who owned several parcels of land in Jamaica, including “approximately 167.25 acres at Flamingo Beach, Trelawny, near to the border of St James”.

“I was registered as the proprietor on November 11, 2005, but have been engaged with the affairs for the estate for many years prior to that date,” Brown told the Sunday Observer.

The Flamingo Beach land issue came to public attention in September when Falmouth Mayor C Junior Gager raised an alarm during the TMC’s regular monthly meeting. He cited Flamingo Beach as one example of the growing problem of squatting in Trelawny which has resulted in the municipal authority being inundated with complaints from frustrated landowners.

“There is a submitted plan here for that property that will help to build Trelawny, but we cannot proceed because there is this problem of squatting,” Gager said of Flamingo Beach, naming Brown as the owner of the land.

During the meeting the mayor also referenced significant squatting on sections of 344.5 acres of land in an area called Tilston, Hague, where one acre has been informally settled; and Hague Cave Island, where four acres of the property have similarly been occupied. He also pointed to Cooper’s Pen in Trelawny

— where approximately 12 acres of the property had been informally occupied

— which had made news headlines following an August 11 early-morning demolition of about 20 structures by the private owner.

There is also a major development planned for Cooper’s Pen and the landowner has been fighting a legal battle for years to get squatters off the land. Brown pointed to similarities between that case and his struggles at Flamingo Beach.

“This débâcle bears all the portents of another Cooper’s Pen, only with more visible, painful results,” he said.

He outlined the ways in which State agencies have failed to act effectively.

“The police have been given statements by parties duped into ‘purchasing’ lots at Flamingo Beach by unscrupulous persons and received necessary information to investigate and prosecute same. No one has been charged,” Brown said.

“I have made several overtures to the police in Trelawny and at the level of the high command for their assistance to address the burgeoning criminality, but with only token support, limited to police escorts whenever court orders are posted on-site. Even equipment bearing insignia and markings of the Jamaica Defence Force has been observed on the site, engaged in illegal activity,” he alleged.

Insisting there can be no excuse for squatting, Brown lay the blame at the feet of successive administrations who have skirted around the issue. He said there has been a “collective refusal” to craft plans to install basic infrastructure on the 550,000 acres of land believed to be in the Government’s possession; pursue transparent divestment methodology and pricing; and put in place the technical staff and enforcement personnel needed in municipal corporations across the country to review and inspect building sites.

Pointing out that the bulk of the country’s housing stock is informal but it is “futile” to demolish them because of non-compliance, Brown argued that many squatters genuinely want to be legitimate owners of property, but the State has failed to put the necessary channels in place.

“Many squatters pay for lands which they occupy

— just not the legitimate owner. Squatters spend large sums for palatial homes on lands they do not own. There is clearly no issue of their ability to afford land, which represents 10 per cent or marginally more of the cost of overall development,” he argued.

“Given an opportunity to acquire lands owned by Government legitimately, those in search of lands [who become squatters] would do so. However, the State must make lands affordable, while ensuring that both the subdivisions and intended development of them are orderly and comply with structural integrity for the safety and health of the intended inhabitants. Formal infrastructure in the form of paved roads and electricity are never a feature of communities that have been squatted,” Brown said.

“These services typically follow after an informal settlement has been established and there is pressure on a member of parliament to support it. These become far more costly to implement because there is no planning of these communities; service roads are twice as long, etc. It is therefore only logical for the State to lead with low-cost, basic infrastructure

— serviced lots in locations with sufficient proximity to main/arterial roads, etc,” Brown added.

He made it clear, however, that he was not excusing the behaviour of those who have stalled his plans at Flamingo Beach.

“These [plans] cannot exist nor be pursued in the context of lawlessness and criminality,” Brown told the Sunday Observer.

World.title: Nurse offers land for proposed Portland hospital
World.content:
Public health Nurse Elaine Linzi making the offer to give up five acres of her land as a site for a new hospital in Portland, last Thursday at the opening of Katus Blakey Dental Clinic in Manchioneal. (Photos: Everard Owen)

MANCHIONEAL, Portland — Hearing Health and Wellness Minister Dr Christopher Tufton saying Government was scouting land on which to house a hospital planned for Portland, United Kingdom citizen and public health Nurse Elaine Linzi last Thursday offered up unused property she owns in the parish. She now works at Manchioneal Health Centre in Portland.

“There seems to be a challenge re identifying a suitable area for the hospital and I’m offering you my land. I have five acres,“ she told Tufton as guests, gathered for the opening of Katus Blakey Dental Clinic in Manchioneal, listened keenly.

”Think out of the box and not always think [about only] Port Antonio. We have wonderful places right here in the east — flat, accessible, cool. All you need is electricity, water, and staff. It is between Kensington and Rural Hill,” Linzi added.

The health minister welcomed the offer, and asked for a round of applause for Linzi.

“It’s a good offer. Send us a note and… all of the team will look at it. The truth is, there’s a lot that goes into building a facility, recognising the needs of the parish in its totality. It’s not necessarily the capital; it could be anywhere on the outskirts… I’m just thinking of a convenient location” said the minister.

“Government is committed and have started a process with land identification. Over the next year we’ll give an update as to where we are to give you a hospital commensurate with the development of the parish,” he promised.

As Tufton noted, the existing hospital in Port Antonio is no longer able to meet the needs of the parish. He pointed out that earlier in the week, Member of Parliament for Portland Eastern Isat Buchanan had raised the issue in the House.

“The truth is, the demand on the facility is higher than the facility’s capacity to deliver. The location of the facility is a problem, because it has no space for expansion. The access to the facility is a challenge, especially when you have an emergency,” he said.

Tufton also pointed to the challenge being faced by many expectant mothers who now have to seek medical care at Annotto Bay Hospital in St Mary.

“We have to find a way to ensure that we develop our health services in keeping with what is required and the growth and the future prospects of the parish,” said Tufton.

Ahead of Linzi’s offer he indicated that talks are under way with Port Authority of Jamaica, which has plans for a development that is being worked on. He said there have also been discussions with the North East Regional Health Authority, National Land Agency, and “the Urban Development Corporation because they are the largest repository of land”, and there has been a suggestion that he should have a discussion with the College of Agriculture, Science, and Education “because they have a lot of land”.

“We’re going to do some sort of comparison to see what is available and what is the most suitable,” said Tufton.

He added that the Government would draw on lessons learned from projects such as Cornwall Regional and the Children’s Hospital in Montego Bay, as well as work done at Black River, Spanish Town, Falmouth, and Kingston Public hospitals.

“I’m here to announce to you that we appreciate and understand what is coming for Portland. We know that health services have to be improved, and we’re making provisions; we will keep you and your representatives abreast as to the progress. I’m hoping that during the course up to the end of this financial year, maybe sometime in the new year… we should at least have some idea as to where that is,” Tufton shared.

World.title: Romain Virgo bares his soul on My Woman & I
World.content:
Virgo’s latest single, My Woman & I was released on Friday, October 30, 2026Contributed

For Romain Virgo, vulnerability has never been something to shy away from. Whether through his music or in his personal life, the reggae singer believes there is value in allowing people to see the person behind the performer, even when the emotions being shared are difficult.

That openness is at the heart of his new single, My Woman & I, a deeply personal offering inspired by a period of uncertainty in his own relationship and a reminder that committed love is not necessarily love without struggle.

Written about a year ago, the song emerged at a time when Virgo and his wife, Elizabeth, were navigating some of the challenges that can arise in any relationship.

Rather than suppressing those feelings, the singer turned to music to process them, recording what was on his heart.

“Relationships and everything that comes with it, those moments when it feels like things aren’t going to work, that’s how I was feeling about my personal relationship in the moment,” he told the Jamaica Observer. “Relationships are like a roller-coaster ride and sometimes, as musicians, the best way to handle these things is to put it in the music. I put pen to paper and I just wrote how I was feeling and recorded it.”

For Virgo, the decision to draw on such a personal experience speaks to his commitment to authenticity. He wants listeners to recognise themselves in his music, particularly those who have experienced the uncertainty that can accompany a relationship while still believing in the possibility of working through it.

“The world, by now, knows me and knows that I am not afraid to show the real side of me. Whether through music or in real life, I am authentic always,” he said.

That willingness to be candid extends to the conversations surrounding the song at home.

When Virgo first played My Woman & I for his wife, her response was not quite the enthusiastic reception he might have hoped for.

“If I’m going to be as vulnerable as possible, the first time she heard this song, she hissed her teeth while laughing at the same time,” he recalled. “I would trouble her and tell her this is the song that she will probably hate the most.”

The reaction, however, appears to have softened. Virgo recently caught her singing the song, prompting a laugh when she remembered that she had supposedly disliked it.

For him, the moment reflects a growing understanding of how music allows him to work through his experiences, including those that are deeply personal.

His creative process, he explained, means drawing on what he is feeling in the moment rather than shying away from difficult emotions. More importantly, the song is not about presenting a relationship as perfect. Instead, Virgo hopes it will resonate with people who understand that commitment is sometimes tested by circumstances that cannot be resolved overnight.

“I hope this single will give people who look to music for their peace and to express themselves. I hope it gives them a sense of belonging,” he said. “I hope they hear someone who has been through some tough times when it comes to relationships and now that it just something that comes with the territory.”

His message to listeners is simple: Difficulty does not have to mean defeat.

“When you’re committed to something, you have to find ways to work through issues and keep showing up, don’t give up on love,” he said.

Though written a year ago, My Woman & I is only now making its way to listeners. Virgo explained that the timing was not right for its release earlier, particularly in the aftermath of Hurricane Melissa, when he delayed the release and promotion of several songs already in the pipeline.

With the time now right, the single will also serve as a precursor to a larger project currently in development. Sources suggest a 2027 release on Ineffable Records.

“This track will lead into something bigger. We working on a project that we can’t give too much details on just yet. Just know this single is a part of a bigger picture,” he said of the track produced by Mr G and revives the classic Dub Fire rhythm made famous on Dennis Brown’s Promised Land.

For now, My Woman & I offers listeners an intimate look at an artiste willing to turn his own experiences into music, with a message that extends beyond romance. Love, as Virgo presents it, is not simply about the moments when everything falls into place, but also the willingness to keep showing up when it does not.

My Woman & I was released on Friday, October 30, and is available on all digital platforms.

World.title: The 15-year challenge
World.content:
Inter Miami’s Lionel Messi (second left) deftly scores past Cavalier’s goalkeeper Vino Barclett (#1) as Jeovanni Laing (left) looks on during the Concacaf Champions Cup second-leg round-of-16 match at the National Stadium on Thursday, March 13, 2025. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

When Mount Pleasant FA and Cavalier FC represented Jamaica in the Concacaf Champions Cup it was a proud moment for local football. However, their participation also highlighted the gap between Jamaican clubs and the region’s top teams.

Clubs in Major League Soccer (MLS) and Mexico’s Liga MX have far greater financial resources, with budgets exceeding US$10 million (over $1.5 billion). This puts them well ahead of teams in the Legend Jamaica Premier League (JPL).

The difference is not just about players’ salaries. It also comes down to facilities, technical support, sports science, preparation, and the cost of competing internationally.

Mount Pleasant have done more than most Jamaican clubs to improve their operations. Under owner Peter Gould, the St Ann club has built its own training academy, hired experienced technical staff, and established itself as one of the leading teams in the Caribbean.

However, even with that investment, Mount Pleasant still have work to do to compete with the best in Concacaf.

Mount Pleasant Sporting Director Paul Christie says the club has made significant progress since 2022, but is still some way from achieving its continental ambitions.

“In 2022, when we were given the privilege of carrying out the mandate by owner Peter Gould, Mount Pleasant was 172nd in Concacaf’s club rating and 35th in the Caribbean,” Christie told the Sunday Observer. “Since then, we’re on the cusp of breaking into the top 50 in Concacaf, and we’re the #1 team in the Caribbean. Until we are able to satisfactorily compete at the Concacaf level, there’s still a lot of work to be done.”

The challenge extends beyond individual clubs. Professional Football Jamaica Limited (PFJL) Chief Executive Officer Owen Hill says the league must address several problems if Jamaican teams are to compete more regularly at the regional level.

One of the biggest challenges is the lack of stadiums that meet Concacaf’s requirements. This often forces clubs to play home matches overseas, increasing their expenses and taking away the advantage of playing in front of their supporters.

Hill pointed to Portmore United’s Caribbean Cup campaign as an example of the problem. He explained that the reigning JPL champions had to play a home match in Trinidad because suitable venues were unavailable in Jamaica.

“That was a home game – in Trinidad, why?! Trinidad is not even close to Jamaica, but the reason they played in Trinidad is primarily because of the economics of it. It’s cheaper to play in Trinidad than Jamaica,” Hill told the Observer.

Hill explained that the National Stadium was booked for the Independence Gala period, while Sabina Park was being used for the Caribbean Premier League. He said Portmore had no other suitable venue available and had to travel to Trinidad to fulfil the fixture.

Playing home matches overseas means clubs miss out on ticket sales and other income that could be used to improve their operations. It also limits the support they receive from local fans.

Hill wants clubs to eventually have their own stadiums that meet minimum Concacaf standards. This would not only give them a suitable home venue for international matches but also allow them to build stronger connections with their communities and generate income.

The PFJL is also working with Concacaf and the Jamaica Football Federation to adjust the domestic calendar around international competitions. However, Hill says clubs must also plan their training programmes and squad depth because fixture clashes cannot always be avoided.

The financial demands of international football are another concern. Hill says the PFJL supports clubs that qualify for regional competitions, while Concacaf subsidies have increased. However, the cost of travel, maintaining squads, and preparing for matches remain major challenges.

“Our clubs and, by extension, our economy, are not about to sustain that consistently, so what we try to do is incentivise the opportunities but also ensure that education happens very early,” Hill says.

The PFJL also wants Jamaican clubs to become stronger brands that can attract investment from the Diaspora and international sponsors. Hill admits that the response from overseas Jamaicans has so far been limited, but believes clubs can become more attractive to investors as the professional product improves.

The league has already reached some important milestones, including an expanded sponsorship agreement with Legend Beer, 360-degree broadcast coverage, and venue partnerships with Independence Park Limited.

Hill also sees the proposed redevelopment of Montego Bay Sports Complex as a model for future projects. He believes Jamaica needs at least 10 stadiums of a similar standard over the next decade to improve the facilities available to clubs and other sporting events.

However, better stadiums alone will not close the gap. Hill says clubs also need proper gyms, recovery facilities, and technical analysts who can study opponents and help coaches prepare their teams.

He believes the lack of those resources also affects how Jamaican football is viewed internationally. While the country’s players are recognised for their speed and athleticism, tactical preparation remains an area that needs improvement.

The long-term plan is to build clubs that can generate enough income through sponsorship, commercial activities, and player transfers to reinvest in their operations.

“When I talk about the vision, I’m saying no less than 10 to 15 years of building and toiling before we see some actual results, such as players being sold for solid amounts of money; transfer fees are now back into the club’s ecosystem to develop the club’s infrastructure at a minimum standard,” Hill says.

World.title: Growing appetite for the snip
World.content:
Medical diagram illustrates the human male reproductive system displaying the anatomical structures involved in a vasectomy procedure including the vas deferens ligation and cauterisation process alongside detailed notes on post-vasectomy physiology and the resulting blockage of the normal sperm pathway.

SOME are fathers who say their families are complete. Others are young men in their 20s and 30s who have decided that they never want children. They are among men seeking vasectomies in the Corporate Area, where some urologists say interest and requests are rising in their private practices.

The slight but notable increase suggests that more men are embracing an active role in contraception, say urologists, who point to varied motivations behind their patients’ decisions.

Consultant Urologist Dr Belinda Morrison-Blidgen, co-owner of the newly opened Urology and Cardiothoracic Centre in St Andrew, told the Jamaica Observer that while she has not observed a similar trend in the public health system, requests for the procedure have increased at her private practice.

Known colloquially as the snip, the procedure involves the cutting and then clamping or sealing of the vas deferens, a tube on each testicle that carries sperm to the urethra.

Morrison-Blidgen estimates that she now performs 10 vasectomies annually, a figure she acknowledged may appear modest, but represents a significant shift from a time when she performed none.

“For the men who already have children, they tend to say that they’ve had enough and they don’t want any more. And that’s usually after they’ve had like two or three children,” she said, adding that those patients also cite the expense of child-rearing as motivation for electing the procedure.

For some, the decision is also about sharing a responsibility traditionally left to women. Morrison-Blidgen said some men are choosing vasectomies to ease the burden on their wives, who have experienced side effects from other contraceptive methods.

“The men may have to put on a condom, but the women really are the ones who use permanent methods like implants or tubal ligation. Some of these women have side effects from those options. Women who take the pill, implants or hormonal options, they may have side effects,” she said.

According to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (ACOG), hormonal birth control like pills, patches, and vaginal rings often cause mild, temporary side effects, including spotting between periods, mild nausea, headaches, sore breasts, and weight gain.

Conversely, hormone-free options do not alter the body’s chemistry but can cause some discomfort where they are placed. According to the Mayo Clinic, a non-hormonal copper intrauterine device (IUD) avoids side effects like mood swings or nausea, but it can result in heavier menstruation and worse cramps.

“A lot of my patients are married men, and they are sympathetic to their wives and the side effects that they have from these pills or injectables, and they say, okay, they’re going to take that stress away from them,” Morrison-Blidgen said.

“The joy of it for the men is that with the vasectomy, it’s a local outpatient procedure done under local anaesthetic. So they don’t have to be put to sleep and it’s very quick, quick recovery time, minimal side effects, and it’s effective. So, they’ve opted to do that,” explained Morrison-Blidgen.

But perhaps the more intriguing aspect of the growing interest, she noted, is that young, childless men are also seeking vasectomies, having decided they do not want children at all.

“I’ve had a few of them who are in relationships, they’re not married, but they’ve just decided they do not want to have children at all. A lot of times they do not come with their partners, it’s just that they’ve never seen themselves having children and they don’t want it to ever happen.

These are men in their 20s and 30s who have made this decision, and I have to respect that,” she said. Morrison-Blidgen further noted that men who come seeking the operation are usually well informed about the process and are just hoping to move on with their sexual life without having to worry about pregnancies or their partners experiencing side effects.

“Most of the patients who come, they have already done their reading, and their background information is there. So, they know it is permanent. They know it’s simple and easy. They know that nobody can even tell that they’ve done it easily because it doesn’t change your rectal function.

“It doesn’t change your semen volume. You will still ejaculate; you still have a normal semen volume.

It’s just that there will be no sperm in that semen,” she said, adding that while a reversal is possible, the men who visit her practice want a permanent solution.

Dr Elon Thompson, owner of Westminster Medical Centre in St Andrew, told the Sunday Observer that relative to his private practice, those going through with the procedures are middle-aged men, who have children.

“Mostly they would be referrals or people who have developed a need, having thought about it and consulted with their partner, that this is the direction in which they would want to go.

But in terms of referrals for vasectomy, I would say, maybe three in a sixmonth period. But most times it is patients that I am already managing that are interested in doing it,” he noted.

The consultant urologist, who is also a Government senator, shared that he has seen growing interest among younger men, though many may decide against the procedure after learning more about it.

“Interest is one thing and actually doing the procedure is another. So, persons will want to find out what the process is, cost, and things like that and get an idea of what will happen after the procedure: ‘Will I have any pain? Will I have any side effects?’ — those things before they make their final decision.

I will say interest is definitely more than, let’s say five, six years ago, but in terms of the actual procedure, some persons are not necessarily sold for whatever reason,” he explained.

Reasons for electing the operation varied among his patients, he noted. But the most central motive, Thompson said, was to prevent pregnancies. “The main benefit clearly is if someone has satisfied themselves along with their partner, of course, that they want no children or no more children.

This is probably one of the most elective of procedures because persons really have to come forward to have it done after having a discussion with their partner.

And it has to be an informed discussion and decision on the part of the patient,” Thompson said, adding that some patients chose vasectomies because they considered the procedure less risky than the female alternative, tubal ligation.

One father of two teenagers told the Sunday Observer that the idea of getting a vasectomy gained traction over dinner as friends who had already had the procedure shared their experiences.

The man, who is between 40 and 50 years old, said that the prospect of going home the same day appealed to him. He also wanted to enjoy his sex life with his wife without worrying about another pregnancy.

He said condoms and the pill had not worked well for them, and a vasectomy would cost less than having his wife’s tubes tied. “A handful of people recommended that this was one of the best ways they found work best in their marriage.

And it was easy to do. It was a one-day procedure versus being in the hospital for three, four, five days,” he explained.

What he had not counted on was the pain. He recalled feeling a tugging sensation in his lower abdomen during the procedure, which he said took nearly two hours.

“It’s local anaesthesia so you might have a little bit of pain. None of that was explained by my friends.

So, what was supposed to be like a 45-minute to an hour session, it ended up being like an hour and a half, almost two hours for me, which was a little rough,” he recalled.

The recovery, however, was a matter of days and much simpler than what his wife would have to endure with a tubal ligation, he reasoned.

“I don’t think I even needed the medication for more than two days. I normally run and I was able to run a 3K in maybe a week after the whole thing,” he told the Sunday Observer.

He encouraged other men who feel their families are complete to consider a vasectomy, weigh the costs, and check what their insurance covers. “I think if you look at that option and the weigh the pros and the cons as the man, it’s beneficial, because the woman has to go through so much more,” he said.

“I know Jamaicans are still of the mindset that ‘man fi breed woman’ and all sorts of things. But to be honest, as much as Minister [of Health and Wellness] Tufton says we need to have more children, children are expensive.

“So, for those of us who are in committed relationships and planned for kids, if you want to… also have sex without the fear of pregnancy, condoms that you’re allergic to, or pills that cause people to put on weight or have side effects, this is one of the best approaches to take because you don’t have to worry about any of that,” he said, while urging men and their partners to be aware of their status, stressing that a vasectomy does not prevent sexually transmitted diseases.

In August this year a BBC story on why more men in their 20s in England are having vascetomies, reported National Health Service data showing that 26,385 vasectomies were performed at hospitals and clinics during 2024-25.

“This was 16 per cent more than in 2023-24,” the BBC report said.

“Men aged 35-39 had more procedures than any other age group, about 8,400 in 2024-25,” the report added.

Additionally, the BBC reported that “there had also been a slight rise on the previous year in younger men choosing to have the snip — about 950 vasectomies were performed on men aged under 30 in England during 2024-25”.

World.title: Loyalty At Heart
World.content:
In Citizen Magazine Issue 005, award-winning actress Sheryl Lee Ralph shares the spotlight with her daughter, stylist Ivy “Coco” Maurice, for “Loyalty at Heart”. (Photo: Rasaan Wyzard)

Plus…

For Sheryl Lee Ralph, style is a family affair. The Emmy, Critics Choice and Independent Spirit Award-winning actress joined her daughter, stylist Ivy “Coco” Maurice, for a striking fashion moment in Citizen Magazine Issue 005. Photographed in Kingston, Jamaica, in March, the mother-daughter duo wore designs by Bianca Saunders and Diotima, respectively, for ”Loyalty at Heart”, an editorial styled by Mecca James-Williams. Curated in the wake of Hurricane Melissa, the visual tribute turns its lens on Jamaican families, celebrating the bonds that endure and a shared allegiance to one another and home. A sentiment captured in its central message: “Loyal to one another, home in Jamaica”.

World.title: Wirecard fugitive claimed he toppled Sebastian Kurz in messages to Russian spy
World.content:
If substantiated, Marsalek’s claims would be a clear indicator of the Russian state interfering directly in the political leadership of an EU country. The Kremlin has long sought to sow division and destabilize governments across Europe, according to assessments by multiple security agencies.

Marsalek is one of the world’s most wanted men and has been on the run since June 2020 when his company, German tech giant Wirecard, collapsed with a €1.9 billion hole in its books.

Since his escape, he has been accused of working for the Kremlin for more than a decade while British police say he is involved in espionage on an “industrial” scale. He is wanted for fraud and is being investigated for spying in several European countries, including his native Austria.

Kurz was the world’s youngest leader when he first became chancellor of Austria in 2017 at the age of 31. But his stratospheric rise, which saw him hold the post twice, was marred by corruption allegations, including that public money was used for political advertising on his behalf.

When members of Marsalek’s spy ring, led by Roussev, were arrested in the U.K., police seized hundreds of thousands of messages detailing operations plotted from British soil.

Some of these messages were shared with authorities, including Austrian officials, who are currently investigating whether their spies provided information to Marsalek and, in turn, to Russia.

World.title: Europe will be represented in Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine, French foreign minister says
World.content:
“In recent weeks, Europeans have made their voices heard, expressing to the American mediator that no discussion concerning the future of the continent can disregard our expectations and demands,” Barrot told RTL.

European Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho said Friday the EU executive didn’t yet have details to share, but added that “it’s obviously up to the European Union to decide on matters which affect its security and on matters which are of its competence.”

The EU has scrambled to agree on who should represent it at the peace talks and who, if anyone, should be in contact with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni urged European Council President António Costa to settle the issue in a letter this week, prompting Costa to put it on the agenda of the Nov. 13 leaders’ summit. Meloni’s letter was partly prompted by a phone call Finland’s Alexander Stubb and Norway’s Jonas Gahr Støre made to Putin on Oct. 27, which took some European leaders by surprise.

Meanwhile, the European Commission hosted talks on Ukraine’s reconstruction on Wednesday, bringing together representatives from Ukraine, the U.S., U.K., Germany, France, NATO and the World Bank.

U.S. President Donald Trump spoke late Thursday of a “big, beautiful agreement,” after meeting with Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev, adding: “It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe.” The plan has brought anxiety among EU officials, who fear it risks sidelining the continent and emboldening Putin.

“We already have a European security architecture in place — NATO and European Union both have their respective roles,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Friday in response to the U.S. plan. “We must make sure Ukraine is integrated into this architecture. The problem remains that Russia keeps breaking the treaties that underpin it … Putin does not have a veto over European security.”

World.title: Russian strikes leave 600,000 in the dark in eastern Ukraine
World.content:
“Power company workers are already working to restore electricity. Their efforts are being hampered by constant Russian shelling,” said the region’s governor Oleksandr Hanzha, adding that hospitals and critical infrastructure are now relying on generators for power.

The blackout follows shelling in the region on Nov. 3 that damaged infrastructure in a key industrial region bordering active combat areas, and a wider attack the same day across Ukraine targeting energy facilities.

The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant also lost power overnight, with the International Atomic Energy Agency saying on Sunday morning it is now relying “on emergency diesel generators for reactor cooling and other essential nuclear safety and security functions.”

The attack comes as Kyiv and Moscow gear up for another round of US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week. Following the new wave of attacks on Saturday night Zelenskyy called on international partners to ramp up sanctions on Russia to hamper its capability to acquire or build more missiles.

“It is very important that they be synchronized across Europe and G7 jurisdictions. If the world does not have enough anti-ballistic capabilities to protect Ukrainian skies, then the missiles must be stopped on the production lines,” he said.

World.title: Security Sunday: Die neue Front der Bundeswehr in Litauen – mit Robertas Kaunas
World.content:
Eingeklemmt zwischen Kaliningrad und Belarus liegt die verwundbarste Stelle der NATO. Genau hier entsteht mit der Panzerbrigade 45 das wohl wichtigste Projekt der deutschen Zeitenwende. Bis 2027 sollen fast 5.000 deutsche Soldaten dauerhaft in Litauen stationiert werden.

Doch die Bedrohung durch Russland ist längst nicht mehr nur theoretisch: Drohnen, Desinformation und brennende Infrastruktur zeigen, dass der hybride Krieg Litauen bereits erreicht hat. Im Gespräch erklärt der litauische Verteidigungsminister Robertas Kaunas, wie real die Gefahr einer Invasion ist.

Die Folge beleuchtet, wie sich die baltischen Staaten wappnen und was Europa tun muss, falls die USA als Schutzmacht ausfallen. Eine präzise Einordnung, warum die Abschreckung an der Ostflanke über das Schicksal des Kontinents entscheidet und die Sicherheit in Vilnius letztlich die Sicherheit in Berlin bedeutet.

World.title: Ein Spaziergang mit Bodo Ramelow
World.content:
Share on LinkedIn

Share on WhatsApp

Share on X

Share via email

Die Welt spielt verrückt, doch im Präsidium des Bundestages herrscht überraschende Einigkeit. Bundestagsvizepräsident Bodo Ramelow (Die Linke) gibt im Gespräch mit Gordon Repinski einen seltenen Einblick in die überparteiliche Zusammenarbeit, auch bei Nachtschichten. Dabei wird deutlich, mit welcher Strategie das Gremium den Provokationen der AfD begegnet.

In seiner eigenen Partei brodelt es derweil gewaltig. Ramelow findet deutliche Worte zur Antisemitismus-Debatte innerhalb der Linken und kritisiert das taktische Lavieren einzelner Abgeordneter. Warum er trotzdem eine Gesinnungsprüfung ablehnt, aber klare rote Linien beim Existenzrecht Israels zieht, offenbart die tiefe Zerrissenheit seiner Partei.

Zudem verrät er, warum die Wahrnehmung der Linken im Bundestag derzeit auch von der Gruppe der „Silberlocken“ abhängt, wie sich die Silberlocken regelmäßig absprechen und warum er sich trotz aller Krisen nicht verrückt machen lässt.

Mit den Linken, aber auch der SPD und den Grünen beschäftigt sich auch der neue Podcast von POLITICO und WELT. In „Inside Links“ geht es jede Woche darum, wie in Deutschland womöglich eine neue linke Mehrheit entsteht, zu welchem Preis und wer künftig dabei möglicherweise am Regierungstisch sitzen könnte. „Inside Links“ gibt es auf den Podcast-Plattformen zu hören und zu sehen, unter anderem auch hier.
