World.title: Gauff bests Pegula in thrilling clash, Noskova beats Kostyuk in WTA Finals
World.content:
NEW YORK: Coco Gauff survived a tough ‌test from Jessica Pegula 6-4 6-7(5) 6-2 on the first day of round-robin play at the WTA Finals on Sunday, as Czech Linda Noskova cruised past Marta ​Kostyuk 6-2 6-4 in Indian Wells.

Gauff beat Pegula just three months ago in Cincinnati and had the right formula again, as the 2024 winner showed superb versatility in a clash between the top two Americans in the season-ending championship.

The frequent rivals were 5-5 in head-to-head before Sunday and appeared perfectly matched through a tight opening set, where Gauff got the break from the baseline on the fourth set point.

Pegula took ‌back the momentum, ‌winning the first three games of the ​second ‌set ⁠before Gauff ​dug ⁠in her heels, trimming the lead to 3-5. Gauff saved three set points in the 10th game to level it, finding her best tennis from the baseline.

Linda Noskova of Czechia comes to the net for a ball while playing Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine during day one of the FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells, California, on November 08, 2026. (Getty Images via AFP)

Gauff saved another two break points and shouted in celebration as she clinched the marathon, 10-minute 11th game. But Pegula saved match point in the 12th and found another gear in the tiebreak, taking the ⁠set with a lethal shot down the line.

Up a ‌break in the third set, Gauff extended ‌her lead to 5-2 when she ran up ​to the net and forced ‌her opponent into an error. She capped a terrific show with ‌a triumphant roar as Pegula sent one past the baseline on the third match point.

The eighth-ranked Noskova is keen for another accolade after her breakthrough win at Wimbledon this year and she got off to a fine start in her ‌WTA Finals debut, applying pressure from the baseline and at the net.

The pair traded early breaks before Noskova ⁠slammed her ⁠foot on the gas in the first set, where Kostyuk was unable to hold her serve until the seventh game.

The Ukrainian Kostyuk was a late addition to the competition after world number one Elena Rybakina pulled out sick, and she was never able to settle in against the Czech, who sent across 20 winners and sealed it with an unreturnable forehand strike to the back corner.

“I definitely wanted to give this week one last push of the season. It’s a long year, we all are kind of drained and injured and all the things ​together, but it’s one of ​the most important tournaments of the year,” said Noskova, who reached the semifinals at Indian Wells earlier this year.

World.title: Rubio says Trump’s war against Iran not ‘necessarily popular’ but needed to stop a nuclear threat
World.content:
HOMESTEAD AIR RESERVE BASE, Florida: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday that President Donald Trump launched the war against Iran even if it was not “necessarily popular” to safeguard the world from the country’s nuclear ambitions.

He would not comment directly about the Republican wipeout in Tuesday’s elections, which delivered a resounding rebuke to Trump. The unpopularity of the Iran war and its impact on gasoline prices and other parts of the economy helped Democrats seize control of Congress.

Asked about Vice President JD Vance’s social media post last week that largely blamed the war for the Republican losses, Rubio told reporters that Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and worked to stop the Islamic Republic from pursuing a nuclear weapon.

“He addressed it even though oftentimes the right thing to do for the country — confronting difficult challenges for the security of our country — doing it isn’t necessarily popular, but necessary,” Rubio said in Florida before heading to a Group of 7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris.

America’s top diplomat offered a robust defense of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Trump’s policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway where one-fifth of the world’s oil transited before the war.

Rubio’s comments also put him at odds with Vance amid speculation of both of their 2028 presidential ambitions. Trump told reporters Sunday that Vance was right — other than that his vice president should have also insisted it was the correct choice to go to war.

“I can tell you if I had it to do again, this historically — for history — will go down as one of the best things we ever did,” Trump said. “Because if they ever had a nuclear weapon, they would blow up the world.”

Iran has long maintained that its nuclear program is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kilograms (972 pounds) of uranium that is enriched up to 60 percent purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90 percent.

With no clear administration strategy to wind down the conflict and the Middle East on edge over the possibility of a return to major hostilities, mediators are trying to revive talks between the sides.

Rubio said, “I wouldn’t say we’re at the verge of a breakthrough.”

He reiterated that Trump prefers a diplomatic solution, but “right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic.”

Trump is set to meet Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House on Monday, according to his official schedule.

The Associated Press has reported that Iran was reviewing proposals presented by chief mediator Qatar aimed at addressing differences with the United States about Tehran’s nuclear program. But Iran was seen as unwilling to negotiate with the Trump administration over their atomic activities until the US agrees to several core conditions that Tehran has been demanding be part of any ceasefire agreement, officials have said.

Those include ending the US blockade on Iran’s ports, lifting sanctions, unfreezing its assets, issuing compensation for war damage and ending hostilities throughout the region, including Israeli operations in Lebanon.

While Rubio said there was no diplomatic breakthrough at hand, Trump told CNN in a phone interview Sunday that as long as the US sees progress in negotiations with Tehran and they sign a “strong agreement,” it’s “highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary” to resume strikes.

Trump said, however, that the US had identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, that it would strike if military action resumes.

The US military, meanwhile, still has carried out limited strikes on Iran, including against its air defenses, at least twice over the past week. It also fired on and disabled a commercial ship Saturday that the US says was trying to breach its naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Rubio acknowledged that the US will take defensive actions if needed.

“If there’s a clear and present threat to shipping or to our forces in the region, we have a right to defend ourselves,” Rubio said.

World.title: Trump says ‘only kidding’ about naming UFC chief executive as White House press secretary
World.content:
WEST PALM BEACH: President ​Donald Trump on Sunday said he was “only kidding” when he suggested UFC CEO Dana White could become his next White House press secretary, after a social media post a day earlier stirred speculation about recruiting his feisty ally and signaled a combative approach ‌to dealing ‌with Democrats as ​they ‌prepare ⁠to take control ​of Congress.

Trump ⁠said White, a prominent supporter, “loves the idea” of taking the job but insisted he had not been serious about the prospect, describing the suggestion as “just a little fun.”

“I will tell you, I was only ⁠kidding,” Trump told reporters, explaining that ‌he had posted ‌photographs of prominent UFC fighters as ​potential assistants to ‌White as part of the joke.

In Saturday’s ‌post, Trump described White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior” and suggested he bring several current or former UFC champions to serve as assistants, saying ‌they were needed to “defend us against the Lunatic Left.”

Trump said White would ⁠visit ⁠him at the White House on Monday, but added that the meeting was planned for other reasons.

White, who has led the Ultimate Fighting Championship for more than two decades, has been a close Trump ally and helped mobilize support for his 2024 presidential campaign.

He has also appeared alongside Trump at several political events and helped bring ​UFC fights to ​the White House lawn this year.

World.title: Deportation flight of Iranians from US scuttled at last minute, attorney says
World.content:
LOS ANGELES: A US deportation flight of Iranian nationals bound for Iran by way of Pakistan was abruptly canceled Sunday morning, according to an attorney who spoke to some of the detainees slated for repatriation.

At least eight Iranians were loaded onto a plane Sunday morning in Mesa, Arizona, for a deportation flight headed to the country of Georgia, then on to Pakistan, according to Ali Rahnama, an attorney with the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund who filed emergency motions on behalf of some of the Iranian detainees. The flight was canceled without explanation, he said.

Court documents unsealed days ago in a civil lawsuit filed by the fund showed the Trump administration as recently as mid-October said it had plans to deport the Iranians to Iran, even as the war there drags on, via an unnamed third country. The lawsuit was filed in July and alleges that the US government illegally shared confidential information about Iranians seeking asylum in the US with Iranian officials.

There were three deportation flights to Iran between September 2025 and January 2026, with over 100 Iranian nationals deported. But the administration’s confirmation of the new plans amid the war that began in February highlights its resolve in carrying out its hard-line immigration crackdown, which has involved ramping up removals, including to places that critics say could endanger the lives of the returnees.

Homeland Security refuses comment

In response to questions Sunday from The Associated Press, the press office of the US Department of Homeland Security provided a statement attributed to an unnamed spokesperson that said Immigration and Customs Enforcement does not comment on “prospective removal operations, including flight schedules, passenger manifests, destinations, or individual case details,” nor would the agency confirm future removal operations.

“As promised, the Trump Administration is employing all lawful options to carry out the largest deportation operation in history,” the statement said.

The administration did not specify in the October court records when the deportations would be carried out. But in the past week, roughly a dozen Iranian nationals in immigration detention said they were notified that they were scheduled for an upcoming deportation flight to Pakistan and then to Iran, according to numerous attorneys who have since confirmed those plans with DHS.

Advocacy group says detainees have been contacted by Iranian officials

According to Rahnama, the eight detainees who boarded the flight on Sunday were visited by a senior official with the Iranian Interests Section — an Iranian representative office in the Pakistani Embassy in Washington that handles consular affairs — and were told that the Iranian government would transport them from Pakistan to Iran.

In the litigation brought by the Iranian immigrant advocacy group, at least a dozen Iranian detainees have said they’ve been contacted by Iranian officials who had knowledge of sensitive information on their asylum claims.

US District Judge Ana C. Reyes, a nominee of President Joe Biden, has not ruled on the claims but ordered the US government to give the court 24-hour notice of any finalized plans to deport Iranians to Iran or to any other country, and five days’ written notice before any such deportation is carried out.

In a court filing Sunday, the defense fund laid out what it had learned about plans for a removal flight Sunday and argued that the administration may have violated the judge’s directive to give advance notice of deportation plans.

Later Sunday, the government filed court documents in the case, but they were sealed and inaccessible to the public.

Group says individuals could face persecution

The Iranian American Legal Defense Fund has called for a halt to the removal flights, saying in a news release that they would “reportedly mark the first deportation of Iranians to Iran since the US-Iran war began.”

The group’s executive director, Yasmin Chubin, said in a statement Sunday that it was difficult to comprehend why the US would forcibly deport Iranians, including asylum seekers, to Iran, amid ongoing military hostilities.

The consequences of removal, Chubin said, “could be irreversible and individuals may face persecution, torture, or death.”

At least one person who had been part of the scuttled flight volunteered to go back to Iran after nearly two years of detention, Rahnama said, out of desperation to leave what he described as inhumane imprisonment. It’s not clear how many other of the deportees may have volunteered to leave.

World.title: Pope Leo tells Argentina’s Trump ally Milei that leaders must know limits of power
World.content:
BUENOS AIRES: Pope Leo on Sunday urged Argentina to safeguard its democracy in a closely watched speech to President Javier Milei, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, during the ​second stop of a 12-day South American tour by the Catholic leader.

Leo told Milei, who has said he will seek reelection next year, that leaders must seek to better the lives of all their citizens and know the limits of their power. Milei’s austerity agenda has been criticized by the Church for hitting the poorest most, and the president has strongly supported the Iran war.

“Authority is most authentic when it is exercised as service,” the pope said in an address opening a three-day visit to Argentina, the first by a pope to the majority-Catholic country since 1987.

“Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them, and to direct their decisions toward the good of the entire community,” said Leo, who had to repeat himself after drawing loud applause for those words from a packed audience that gathered at the Palacio Libertad cultural center.

Leo is the first US-born pope and drew Trump’s ire earlier this year after denouncing the Iran war.

The pope, who made a historic choice for a Catholic leader to cast a ballot by mail in the US midterm elections last week, also said democracy requires ‌that people learn to ‌live together despite differences of opinion and have confidence in the rule of law.

“Democracy... is a part of Argentina’s heritage that ​needs to ‌be safeguarded,” ⁠said Leo, ​adding ⁠that it is strengthened by “the patient search for agreement, and through the ability to see those who think differently as fellow citizens with whom we share a common future.”

In his own address welcoming Leo to Argentina, Milei defended his libertarian policies, saying that the rights to life, liberty and property are the backbone of Argentina’s constitution and of Western democracies.

FIRST PAPAL VISIT IN 40 YEARS

Leo, 71, is making one of the most intense foreign trips by a Catholic leader in decades, less than a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery. The pope, who spoke for 25 minutes in his address on Sunday in a firm, clear voice, will tour four cities in Argentina through Wednesday.

After the pope’s arrival at Buenos Aires’ Jorge Newbery airport on Sunday, crowds thronged his route to downtown Buenos Aires, waving small Vatican and Argentine flags, while Catholic nuns in tan-colored religious habits chanted: “The pope is here, you can feel it.”

“It’s been almost 40 years, 39 exactly, that the pope hasn’t come to Argentina,” said Claudia Sona, who traveled from the northern province of ⁠Salta. “For Catholics, and I think for non-Catholics, this is a rebirth.”

Milei, a theatrical figure known for bombastic statements and an unkempt haircut, swept ‌to power in 2023 campaigning with a chainsaw as a symbol of the deep cuts to state spending he pledged to make ‌to shore up the country’s finances.

He has been accused of undermining democracy in Argentina with divisive rhetoric and attacks ​on the press.

The president has defended his austerity push as the only way to bring inflation ‌under control. Under his economic campaign, annual inflation has fallen from over 200 percent to 33 percent.

But surveys show his popularity has slipped ahead of elections next year as Argentines contend with ‌subsidy cuts, public-sector layoffs and business closures linked to squeezed household budgets.

STIMULUS SHOULD NOT TARGET POOR

Milei’s cuts have also reduced social services, such as disability benefits, and poverty remains a challenge despite dropping significantly after peaking during the president’s first year in office.

While Leo did not specifically refer to Milei’s austerity agenda in his address, he urged that Argentina’s efforts at economic stimulus not target the poorest.

“Efforts should be made to promote whatever creates opportunities, stimulates private initiative and ensures that economic growth also benefits those who are disadvantaged,” he said, in another of several lines that drew strong applause.

The pope, who has warned that artificial intelligence could lead the world down a ‌path of unending war, returned to the issue in Argentina, stressing that technological progress must be matched by “ethical consciousness” in remarks that touched on another of Milei’s priorities.

Milei has championed AI development and said he wants Argentina to become a major destination for data centers.

Leo ⁠is on an ambitious 50-event, three-country tour through November ⁠17. He first visited Uruguay before arriving in Argentina and will carry on to Peru on Wednesday.

The pope, who addresses national governments on each of his foreign visits, usually speaks in careful, diplomatic language but has emerged as a more forceful voice on the world stage recently, decrying the direction of global leadership.

Ahead of his arrival in Argentina, analysts said his remarks to Milei would be closely parsed by local politicians.

“Any interventions by Leo, particularly on poverty, the limits of markets or confrontational political rhetoric, could be read as implicit criticism of Milei and amplify existing opposition to the government’s approach,” said Nicolas Watson, a managing director at advisory firm Teneo.

Fortunato Mallimaci, a sociologist at Argentina’s Conicet research agency, said Leo’s visit to Argentina will create a sense of unity and energy among those who feel excluded by Milei’s economic program.

Over his 18-month papacy, Leo has urged world leaders to treat immigrants more humanely and called for action to address climate change, appeals that have put him at odds with Trump and other right-wing leaders.

EXPECTED TO DRAW MILLIONS IN ARGENTINA

The Vatican has described Leo’s tour as a “homecoming” for the pope, who served for decades as a missionary in Peru and became a Peruvian citizen. The tour is expected to draw large crowds, with Argentine officials estimating some 7 million will see the pope in their country.

The pope’s itinerary in Argentina includes visits to a care center for people with disabilities and a prison, underscoring his focus on highlighting groups that are often marginalized.

Milei was known for piling insults on Leo’s predecessor, Francis, an Argentine who never came home ​during his 12-year papacy. Despite calling Francis “an imbecile,” Milei eventually sought to repair relations and visited ​Francis at the Vatican.

In his speech on Sunday, Milei praised Francis in terms that would have been shocking to hear from the president in the past, calling the late pope, who died in April 2025, an inspiring and generous figure who was “without a doubt the most important Argentine in history.”

World.title: Rubio says progress made on postwar security framework for Ukraine, Europe
World.content:
WASHINGTON: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that progress had been made toward establishing a postwar security framework for Ukraine and Europe, as US-mediated negotiations between Russia and Ukraine prepare to resume this week in Abu Dhabi with European participation.

Rubio said discussions on security guarantees for Ukraine and the broader European continent had advanced, although no agreement had been finalized, and expressed hope that further progress could be made during the talks scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday.

“The entirety of the time we’ve been talking about Russia-Ukraine, the one thing that’s repeatedly come up is the need for security guarantees. What is the postwar security infrastructure of Ukraine and more broadly of the European continent going to look like?” Rubio told reporters.

“I think that’s what the president’s alluding to — is that there’s been some advances made in what that architecture could look like post-conflict,” he added.

“We obviously have to get past the conflict to get to that point. Nothing’s been finalized yet, and maybe some progress can be made in Abu Dhabi,” Rubio said.

His comments came as US President Donald Trump seeks to advance efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine, which began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Trump on Thursday predicted a “very big” deal with Moscow involving not only Ukraine but “all of Europe,” remarks that raised questions about the potential implications of any settlement for European security.

European participation

European countries are expected to participate in the Abu Dhabi discussions, with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot confirming on Sunday that France would send representatives.

“The Europeans will be well represented. France will be in Abu Dhabi to take part in these discussions,” Barrot told French radio station RTL, without identifying who would represent Paris.

US envoy Steve Witkoff said Washington would bring Russian and Ukrainian delegations together in the Emirati capital on November 10-11 to discuss ending the war, postwar security arrangements and measures to de-escalate the conflict.

Rubio is traveling to Paris for talks with G7 foreign ministers ahead of the negotiations.

Security guarantees on agenda

The security framework has emerged as a central issue in diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, particularly the question of how Ukraine’s security would be protected after any ceasefire or peace agreement and what role European countries and NATO would play.

Trump’s envoy Jared Kushner, who is also the president’s son-in-law, said US officials held “productive and substantive discussions” with Ukraine, NATO and European partners in Brussels on Thursday.

Those discussions focused on security guarantees for Ukraine and a broader European security architecture, according to Kushner.

Witkoff and Kushner are expected to represent the United States at the Abu Dhabi talks.

The discussions will test whether Washington can translate the progress reported on security arrangements into a framework acceptable to Kyiv, Moscow and European governments, amid continuing disagreements over the terms of a possible settlement.

No details of a proposed security arrangement have been made public, and the outcome of the negotiations remains uncertain.

World.title: Lens’ nightmare week worsens with late Marseille defeat
World.content:
PARIS: RC Lens’ nightmare week continued ‌as they conceded a late goal to lose 2-1 at home to Olympique de Marseille in Ligue 1 on Sunday after a humiliating 9-1 thrashing ​in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Lens fell behind in the second minute when Amine Gouiri scored for Marseille, following a defensive error, but Florian Thauvin pulled them level in the 20th.

They appeared on course to earn a point until Keyliane Abdallah struck with eight minutes remaining, the 20-year-old following up after Gouiri’s initial effort was blocked, to condemn the hosts to a ‌third successive defeat ‌in all competitions.

The defeat left Lens ​11th ‌in ⁠Ligue 1 ​and ⁠extended a miserable run that began when Olivier Giroud scored a late winner for Lille in last weekend’s derby.

Wednesday’s Champions League defeat to Como equalled the heaviest in the competition’s history and marked another low for last season’s Ligue 1 runners-up, whose fortunes have declined sharply since Pierre Sage left to take charge of Crystal ⁠Palace.

His replacement Dino Toppmoeller lasted only a matter ‌of weeks and Yannick Cahuzac’s position ‌is now also under scrutiny.

Marseille, meanwhile, have ​climbed to fourth after overcoming ‌their sluggish start to the campaign. They have won five ‌successive Ligue 1 matches and also beat Bayer Leverkusen in the Europa League on Thursday.

Earlier, Belgian defender Nathan Ngoy scored Lille’s winner in a 2-1 victory at Rennes that lifted them to second.

Lille have 21 points, ‌two behind leaders Paris St. Germain and one ahead of third-placed Paris FC. Marseille are fourth ⁠on 18 ⁠points, above Olympique Lyonnais, who lost 2-0 at Brest on Sunday.

Nice continued their resurgence with a 2-0 win at Angers, their fourth victory in five league matches. Sofiane Diop opened the scoring in the second minute before Jonathan Clauss sealed the points in the 78th.

The result lifted Nice to sixth, while Monaco slipped to seventh after conceding a 90th-minute equalizer in a 1-1 draw at promoted Le Mans.

Monaco, beaten 3-1 by Paris FC last weekend, have gone five league matches without a win.

Substitute Erwan ​Colas equalized from a corner ​to earn Le Mans a valuable point and lift them to 15th, outside the relegation zone.

World.title: Nvidia announces probe into CEO Huang amid reports China spied on him
World.content:
NEW YORK: Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced Sunday it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence.

Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that the woman, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing.

The executive, Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.

In a message to company employees released Sunday, Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologized to both his family and company staff.

“I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Asked about the report Sunday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he couldn’t comment, saying it was an “internal corporate matter.”

Jensen Huang is a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and close to President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race.

The Times said Huang’s relationship with the other Huang could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump’s planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China.

Nvidia said in a statement it opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” It did not name a country.

The statement added: “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.”

The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as “groundless speculation.”

‘Black eye moment’

China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.

Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world’s most valuable companies.

Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter.

Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang’s relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said.

Technology analyst Dan Ives, with the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said word of the probe is “a black eye moment” for Jensen Huang.

Ives predicted it will at the very least spark multiple congressional inquiries and “create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons.”

In the near-term Huang is expected to keep his job but risks being removed as Nvidia’s CEO depending on the board’s probe, Ives said in a statement.

“This will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally,” he said. “This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China, which remains a key battleground issue in DC.”

World.title: Train collision in Egypt’s Giza kills 4, injures 88: health ministry
World.content:
Al Ayyat – Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities.

Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.

The health ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area.

State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.

Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.

Several carriages lay on their side, AFP journalists at the scene reported. One end of a train had crumpled into a mangle of steel, while the end of the other — spliced open in the impact — had toppled off the tracks into an adjacent farm.

First responders and passersby helped lift one of the victims out of the wreckage in a black body bag, AFP images showed.

Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster.

In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo.

In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.

Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

World.title: Iraq reportedly delivers US message to Iran during Tehran visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – According to sources cited by Saudi-owned Al Hadath television, an Iraqi delegation headed to Tehran for an eight-hour diplomatic trip to convey a message from the United States to Iranian leaders.

The alleged visit coincides with rising tensions between Washington and Tehran, with Iraq increasingly aiming to position itself as a diplomatic middleman between the two nations.

The allegation was carried by Iran International and other Iranian media sites, and it linked the delegation’s travel to a recent phone call between US President Donald Trump and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, as well as a visit to Baghdad by US Special Envoy Tom Barrack.

However, neither Iraqi nor Iranian officials have officially acknowledged the claimed mission.

The identity of the delegation members, the nature of the supposed American message, and Tehran’s reaction are unclear.

The accusations come after a November 6 phone call between Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi, during which Hussein suggested forming a committee of regional foreign ministers to visit Washington and Tehran in an attempt to defuse tensions.

Iraq’s diplomatic attempts take place amid a background of differences over Iran’s nuclear program, security in the Strait of Hormuz, and the actions of Iran-aligned armed organizations in Iraq.

Baghdad has tight political and economic ties with Tehran while simultaneously working with Washington on security issues, putting Iraq in a potentially advantageous position to facilitate indirect contact between the two administrations.

World.title: Turkey to gradually hand over military base to Iraq as Baghdad-Ankara ties strengthen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkey will begin taking steps to gradually transfer control of the Bashiqa-Zilkan military base in northern Iraq to the Iraqi federal government, according to a joint announcement issued on Sunday, November 8.

According to the Office of Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, Baghdad and Ankara have also agreed to set up a joint security coordination committee to monitor efforts to restore full Iraqi government authority in Sinjar, Nineveh Governorate, and to end the presence of armed groups operating outside state control.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan struck an agreement in New York on September 23, leading to the announcement.

The two heads of state agreed to coordinate security measures in northern Iraq and plan for the eventual handover of the Turkish military station.

Turkey maintained a presence at the Bashiqa-Zilkan base near Mosul during the 2015 anti-ISIS battle.

However, the deployment sparked long-standing tensions, with Baghdad frequently objecting to Turkish forces operating on Iraqi soil without federal authority.

Turkey has also maintained military bases and carried out cross-border operations in northern Iraq against the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), which Ankara deems a terrorist group.

Baghdad has condemned transgressions of Iraqi sovereignty while expanding cooperation with Turkey to combat the group’s operations.

In April 2024, Erdoğan visited Baghdad and signed agreements on security, commerce, energy, water management, and infrastructure development, leading to an improvement in relations between the two nations.

In August 2024, Iraq and Turkey inked a military and security cooperation pact to improve information sharing, counterterrorism coordination, and military training.

Beyond security, Baghdad and Ankara are pursuing big economic projects, such as the Development Road Project, which intends to link Iraq’s southern ports to Turkey and European markets via new transportation infrastructure.

The anticipated surrender of Bashiqa-Zilkan is another step toward settling a long-standing border conflict, while Turkey continues to retain military posts in northern Iraq.

World.title: Chelsea shocked by Sunderland, Liverpool cruise
World.content:
London – Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 defeat at Premier League strugglers Sunderland, while Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win against lowly Crystal Palace on Sunday.

Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish.

Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season.

Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Alonso.

Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso was furious that Chelsea were not given a foul on Cole Palmer in the build-up to the spot-kick.

Liverpool had been beaten by Arsenal in the Premier League and Fenerbahce in the Champions League before arriving in south London, sparking pointed questions about Andoni Iraola in the former Bournemouth manager’s first season in charge at Anfield.

But Alexis Mac Allister headed Liverpool in front at Selhurst Park from Dominik Szoboszlai’s cross after 40 minutes.

Florian Wirtz bagged Liverpool’s second with a composed finish from Bradley Barcola’s cross in the 54th minute.

It was Wirtz’s first league goal this season and only the second in all competitions for the inconsistent German playmaker this term.

Alexander Isak finished off Wirtz’s pass in the 89th minute to wrap up fourth-placed Liverpool’s much-needed victory after a two-game losing streak.

It was Liverpool’s fourth consecutive away league win this season.

Eddie Nketiah’s stoppage-time penalty after a foul by Milos Kerkez was no consolation for Palace.

Palace manager Pierre Sage — hired to replace Oliver Glasner in the close-season is on the brink of being sacked after his side slumped to the bottom of the table following their seventh defeat in 10 league matches.

– Seagulls flying high –

Brighton extended their superb start to the season, climbing to second place with a 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium.

While Fabian Hurzeler’s side might not have the staying power to challenge Arsenal for the title, they have established themselves as contenders for a Champions League place.

Diego Gomez’s 25-yard rocket gave the Seagulls the lead in the 15th minute.

Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off for clattering Chema Andres in the face midway through the first half.

Pascal Gross doubled Brighton’s advantage with a 42nd minute penalty after Keane Lewis-Potter fouled Luka Vuskovic.

The Seagulls’ sixth win in their last seven league games lifted them above third-placed Manchester City and within five points of champions Arsenal, who beat Hull on Saturday.

Evanilson maintained his hot streak in Bournemouth’s 2-1 win at Ipswich.

The Cherries’ Brazilian forward struck with a clinical finish in the fifth minute, taking him to seven goals in his last eight games.

An own goal from Leif Davis in the 46th minute increased Bournemouth’s lead and Jack Clarke’s 73rd minute penalty wasn’t enough to rescue Ipswich.

In Sunday’s late game, Manchester United manager Michael Carrick cannot afford a defeat against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as he fights to save his job ahead of the international break.

United are without a victory in their last seven league games and have won just once in the top-flight this term.

They ended a miserable nine-match winless run in all competitions by coming from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday.

smg/ea

World.title: Spain’s Alcaraz wins Paris Masters for first time
World.content:
Paris – Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man that ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old Spaniard claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career.

Unlike their five-set quarter-final epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year — only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

In Italy, he will be seeking a first coronation at the season-ender.

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city.

But not for the first time in the French capital, Alcaraz won the title by saving match points en route — this time against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals in scenes reminiscent of his iconic Roland Garros final win against Italian Sinner last year.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level– both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.

– ‘Ten out of ten’ –

Serving at 1-2 in the first set, Alcaraz flirted with danger as he offered up four break points, but dug in to secure the hold when Shelton misfired at the end of a seven-minute long game.

Shelton then found himself two break points down in the seventh game but responded with a perfect drop volley and blistering passing shot to bring up deuce, before holding and keeping his nose in front.

Although both players threatened on the other’s serve and drew repeated gasps from the crowd with some audacious shot-making, the opener nonetheless required a tie-break to separate them.

A Shelton error at 4-4 followed by a leaping backhand smash by Alcaraz brought up two set points.

The first came and went when Alcaraz thundered the ball into the top of the net cord and the expectant arena froze in time as it rose and fell in seeming slow motion, only to land on the Spaniard’s side of the court.

Alcaraz was not to be denied a second time, however, as Shelton overcooked a forehand on the next point to cede the opener.

At 2-2 in the second set, Shelton let out a bellow of frustration after missing a groundstroke at 15-30 on Alcaraz’s serve, but the American could smile at the end of the game as a double fault and missed forehand produced the first break of the match.

Alcaraz had said after booking his spot in the final that his reflexes would need to be “ten out of ten” when facing Shelton’s serve and they were just that three games later as he levelled the set at four-all.

A deft exchange of angled drop shots ended by an Alcaraz winner down the line brought the Spaniard’s finger to his ear and the crowd again to their feet as Shelton suddenly found himself serving to keep the final alive.

He did so at the first time of asking but when required to serve again to force a breaker, Shelton cracked as Alcaraz again pounced to seal the title with a flicked backhand winner.

World.title: Iraq accelerates completion of 1,640 MW Anbar power plant
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has authorized authorities to repay overdue payments to the Chinese business that is building the Anbar Combined-Cycle Power Plant, a significant electrical project with a projected capacity of 1,640 megawatts.

The decision was issued at a meeting with business executives on Sunday, November 8, 2026, during which Al-Zaidi stressed the importance of maintaining construction quality and completing the project’s technical criteria.

SEPCOIII, a Chinese engineering and construction firm linked with state-owned PowerChina, is implementing the project.

The project, near Hit in Iraq’s western Anbar Governorate, is being built for the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity.

The facility will be powered by four gas turbines and two steam turbines, with combined-cycle technology used to create extra energy from heat generated during gas-fired power production.

Construction started in 2013 but was halted after the Islamic State group’s control of sections of Anbar.

Work restarted in late 2022, with the Chinese contractor taking over responsibility for finishing the project.

The plant is scheduled to receive natural gas from Anbar’s Akkas gas field.

The connecting pipeline must be completed, and stable fuel supplies are still required before the plant can be fully operational.

Once finished, the Anbar power plant is projected to improve energy supply across the province and add producing capacity to Iraq’s national grid.

World.title: Iraq’s Kurdish parties face government split as Baghdad’s influence grows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Political disputes between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), headed by Masoud Barzani, and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), led by Bafel Talabani, have prompted fears about the possibility of two opposing governments in Iraq’s Kurdistan.

The issue erupted when the KDP convened a parliamentary session in Erbil without the PUK’s participation.

Bafel Talabani, the head of the PUK, later announced his party’s resignation from the regional government, increasing the likelihood of a breakaway administration centered in Sulaymaniyah.

The KDP, headed by former Kurdistan Region President Masoud Barzani, is the region’s major political party, having primary bases in Erbil and Duhok.

The PUK, led by Bafel Talabani, the son of former Iraqi President Jalal Talabani, has its major stronghold in Sulaymaniyah.

Despite strong political conflicts, the two parties have traditionally shared power in the autonomous territory.

The widening split comes as Iraq’s federal government in Baghdad strengthens its control over disputed territory, notably Kirkuk and sections of Nineveh province, including Mosul.

Following the Kurdistan Region’s independence vote in 2017, Baghdad reasserted federal sovereignty over Kirkuk and numerous contested territories.

Mosul, however, remains under federal control, with Kurdish groups vying for political power in the surrounding districts.

A sustained schism between Barzani’s KDP and Talabani’s PUK might erode the Kurdistan Regional Government’s bargaining power with Baghdad over oil income, public-sector wages, budget transfers, and disputed territory.

The likelihood of rival Kurdish administrations has heightened fears about political fragmentation, possibly increasing Baghdad’s clout as the two parties battle to reach an agreement on a single regional government.

World.title: Erbil flash floods kill two, cause widespread damage
World.content:
Erbil (IraqiNews.com) – At least two people have died and widespread property damage has been reported after overnight flash floods struck Erbil, in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region, on Saturday, November 7.

Erbil’s governor acknowledged the deaths as rescue crews continued to react to floods in the city and neighboring regions. The casualties were believed to be a five-year-old youngster and a 24-year-old adult.

The flooding occurred when torrential rains inundated areas of the city, causing damage to houses, businesses, and infrastructure, with preliminary estimates indicating damage in the tens of millions of dollars.

According to Iraq’s Kurdistan Region Meteorological Department, Erbil received roughly 70 millimeters of rain in 24 hours.

For instance, Halabja got 80.6 millimeters over the same time with no corresponding destruction.

The disparity has sparked concerns about Erbil’s drainage infrastructure, urban planning, and preparation for inclement weather, especially given the city’s rapid urban development in recent years.

The catastrophe has also sparked political criticism, with media sources linked with opposing Kurdish political groups trading allegations about infrastructure management and government accountability.

Critics contend that recurring floods demonstrate the need for more investment in stormwater drainage infrastructure and better urban design to safeguard people and businesses.

Emergency response efforts continue as officials analyze the full scope of the devastation and aid impacted populations.

World.title: 'Dimagi Naxal' remark a brazen assault: Congress
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh on Sunday criticised Prime Minister

over his "Dimagi Naxals" remarks, accusing him of using the occasion of Diwali to target political rivals and alleging that his comments reflected a pattern of branding those who disagreed with his govt.

In a post on X, the Rajya Sabha MP said that Modi had not spared the country even on Diwali and objected to his remarks during his visit to Bastar, where he referred to "Dimagi Naxals".

"The Prime Minister has not spared the nation even on Diwali day his trademark abuse. He has once again spoken of what he calls dimagi naxals. He has used a very solemn non-political occasion, donned the uniform of the security forces, and hurled invectives at his political rivals.

This is a brazen assault on all institutional norms, but when has that ever stopped this man?" the Congress leader said.

Citing PM's earlier remarks on those demanding a caste census, Ramesh said Modi had described them as "urban naxals" on April 28, 2024, but later announced on April 30, 2025, that a caste census would be conducted as part of Census 2027.

Ramesh also referred to the farmers' protest against the three farm laws, alleging that PM Modi had called those opposing the laws supporters of a Naxal ideology in Sept 2020 before withdrawing the laws on Nov 19, 2021.

"The PM is clearly distraught, disturbed and desperate. Jhola-picking-up time is fast approaching," Ramesh added.

World.title: Watch: Diwali lights up Srinagar's Lal Chowk as tourists, locals celebrate at Ghanta Ghar
World.content:
Local Hindus and Muslims also joined the celebrations, with people lighting firecrackers.

NEW DELHI: Thousands of earthen lamps lit up Srinagar's iconic Lal Chowk on Sunday evening as tourists and local residents came together to celebrate Diwali around the city's historic clock tower, popularly known as Ghanta Ghar.Dozens of tourists gathered at the clock tower and lit diyas, illuminating the area around the landmark.Local Hindus and Muslims also joined the celebrations, with people lighting firecrackers.Ankush Chatterjee, a tourist from Kolkata, said he was delighted to celebrate the festival in Kashmir. "We are delighted to celebrate this year's Diwali in Kashmir. The atmosphere here is radiant," he told PTI.Diwali celebrations at Ghanta Ghar have become a regular sight in recent years, with tourists and residents gathering at Lal Chowk to mark the festival.Elsewhere in the Valley, security personnel celebrated Diwali by lighting lamps at their camps and distributing sweets.

World.title: PM Modi visits LK Advani on his birthday as veteran BJP leader enters 100th year
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday visited former deputy prime minister Lal Krishna Advani at his residence to greet him on his birthday, as the veteran BJP leader entered his 100th year.

The Bharatiya Janata Party also organised a havan at its headquarters to mark the occasion. Senior party leaders, including BJP national president Nitin Nabin, attended the ceremony, held between 10am and 10.30am.

PM Modi marked the occasion by writing an article on Advani's contribution to Indian politics and the BJP. In a post on X, the prime minister said he had recalled Advani's journey, from experiencing the Partition and rebuilding his life to strengthening the Jana Sangh, building the BJP and standing up to the Emergency.



He also referred to Advani's role in the Somnath-Ayodhya Rath Yatra and his time in government, besides highlighting his interests in reading, culture, cinema and writing.

PM Modi also credited Advani's leadership with expanding the BJP's political presence.

"Today, 8th November, is a landmark day. Respected L.K. Advani Ji enters his hundredth year. On this special occasion, my greetings to him. Iâve written an article in which Iâve highlighted his everlasting contribution to India," he said.





"I have recalled his journey, be it experiencing the horrors of Partition and rebuilding life from scratch, strengthening the Jana Sangh and building the BJP, standing up for democracy during the Emergency, leading the Somnath to Ayodhya Rath Yatra or serving the nation in government. Have also written about other aspects of Advani Ji - the voracious reader, his love for culture and cinema, a prolific writer and more," he added.

Nabin also extended birthday wishes to Advani, describing him as a guide to party workers and acknowledging his contribution to the organisation's growth and the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

Born on November 8, 1927, in Karachi, in present-day Pakistan, Advani joined the RSS in 1942. He served as BJP president for three terms between 1986 and 2005 and was India's deputy prime minister from 2002 to 2004. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024.

World.title: ‘Matter of personal faith’: Congress on Akhilesh Yadav’s proposed Ram Temple visit
World.content:

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Sunday described Samajwadi Party (SP) president and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Akhilesh Yadavâs proposed December 12 visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya as a âmatter of personal faith. "The two parties are allies in the state.Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam questioned why any political leader should object to the SP chief's proposed visit.âReligion is a matter of personal faith. Whether someone wants to visit a temple, mosque, gurudwara, church, Buddhist monastery, or Jain temple is entirely their personal choice,â he told ANI.âOur Constitution gives everyone the freedom of religion and worship. So why should any political leader have a problem with that?â the Congress leader asked.Gautam's remarks came amid attacks by BJP leaders, including Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and deputy chief minister Brijesh Pathak, on Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed Ram Temple visit. They cited the 1990 police firing on "kar sevaks" (volunteers), which took place when Akhilesh Yadav's father, Mulayam Singh Yadav, was the chief minister.This comes a day after SP leader Pawan Pandey claimed Akhilesh Yadav will visit Ayodhya with his family on December 12 to offer prayers at the Hanuman Garhi temple and seek blessings at the Ram Temple."On December 12th, the national president of the Samajwadi Party and former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh Yadav, will visit Ayodhya along with his family," Pandey said, referring to the BJP-led government, currently in its second term.Pandey also expressed confidence about the party's prospects in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, likely to be held in February-March next year."This government will be ousted, and the Samajwadi Party government will be formed, with Akhilesh Yadav becoming the chief minister," he remarked.This would be Akhilesh Yadav's first visit to the temple since its consecration in January 2024.

World.title: 'Why funding only for temples?' Congress's Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury on Bengal's Rs 1,000-crore plan
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury on Sunday questioned the BJP-led West Bengal government's proposed Rs 1,000 crore spending over the next two years to renovate and restore ancient temples and monasteries across the state under the 'Tirthakshetra Circuit'.

Speaking to reporters on the occasion of Kali Puja and Diwali, Chowdhury said the country did not belong to any one religion and that the government should adopt an inclusive approach.

"There are Gurdwaras and mosques, too; why is funding given only to temples? If resources are to be allocated, it must be done for everyone, for people of all religions. Our country does not belong to just one religion," he said.

He added that resources should be made available to people of all religions and urged the government not to create divisions among religious communities.



He also appealed to the government not to create divisions between communities and called for an approach that included everyone.

Meanwhile, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge extended Diwali greetings on Sunday, wishing people happiness, peace and harmony.

World.title: ‘Not a political book, but a personal one’: Sonia Gandhi ahead of memoir release
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Two days before the India release of her memoir, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Sunday described it as ânot a political book but a personal one," emphasising that she wanted to portray her family "honestly," as people she knew and loved.

âThis is not a political book, itâs a personal one. Much has been written about my family, but rarely with real insight into who they were, their motivations, their struggles, their very human flaws. I wanted to portray them honestly, as people I knew and loved,â the Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson wrote on X.

She gave a detailed account of how the book, titled "Belonging: A Journey of Love," came to be, in an article for The Hindu, which had published a

with her on Saturday.



"For most of my life, I kept my inner world to myself. Even after grief pulled me into politics, I held on to whatever privacy I could, and writing openly about my life felt almost unthinkable. Only after stepping back from the daily churn of public life could I see my own story clearly," Sonia Gandhi wrote in the article, referring to the assassination of her husband, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, who was India's youngest Prime Minister.





"When I did look back, one thread ran through all of it: love, and the loyalty that grows from it. It all began in England, where a 19-year-old woman from a small Italian town met a young Indian student (Rajiv Gandhi). It carried me into a new country and a new family, into a deep bond with my mother-in-law (Indira Gandhi), and through the years of raising our children," she added,

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"It also carried me through the unbearable, when I lost first my mother-in-law and then my husband to violence," the former Congress president wrote.

Published by HarperCollins India, Sonia Gandhi's memoir will be released in India on November 10, ending uncertainty over the book's domestic publication following an "impasse" between the author's representatives and Penguin Random House India.

The book covers major tragedies that impacted the Gandhi family, including the death of Sonia Gandhi's brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi in a plane crash, Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984 and Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.

The memoir also delves into political events surrounding the Congress' victory in the 2004 elections, when Sonia Gandhi declined to become Prime Minister and instead led the party and its alliance, which governed India till 2014.

World.title: Watch: Sonia, Priyanka take a trip down memory lane, recall Diwali with Rajiv Gandhi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisited memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.

In a conversation shared on social media, Sonia Gandhi recalled her fondness for Diwali, describing the elaborate decorations, traditional rituals and festive gatherings that marked the celebrations.

"Oh, Diwali I loved. So, Diwali was always beautiful," she recalled in a video shared on her Instagram account.

Recalling the traditional rituals, Sonia said a Ganesh idol was placed at the entrance of the house, where the first diya of the celebrations was lit. She added that the idol is now kept at her residence.

"At the entrance, there used to be a Ganesh Murti, which is now in my house. And so, we would do the first lighting of the diya in front of Ganesh Ji's Murti.



And it was always decorated. In those days, we didn't have those little lights everywhere, but we had diyas everywhere - around the pond, all along the roof, veranda, and along the path, wherever there was a path. So, it was very pretty," she said.

Priyanka Gandhi, the MP from Wayanad, also recalled how festivals were celebrated with great enthusiasm, with people from different walks of life gathering in the Gandhi family's garden.





Sonia remembered how the family would sometimes get carried away with firecrackers, while Priyanka recalled how her father, Rajiv Gandhi, would take them to Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi to buy crackers.

"Papa used to take us to Chandni Chowk to buy crackers. We used to go to Old Delhi to buy crackers," Priyanka recalled.

Sonia also remembered phuljhadis, or traditional sparklers, saying she enjoyed them, although she was less enthusiastic about some of the noisier fireworks.

Beyond the lights and firecrackers, Sonia said the atmosphere during the festive season remained particularly memorable. Recalling the weather during those celebrations, she spoke about the clear blue skies that formed the backdrop to the festivities.

"Weather at that time was beautiful. Blue skies and all, which you hardly see now. Yeah, it was lovely," she said.

Sonia also recalled that festivals were marked by Kashmiri cuisine and a traditional sweet rice preparation, a culinary tradition that continues in the family.

"And then, on festivals, we always used to have Kashmiri food and that sweet rice, like that, which we still make, by the way," she said.

Sonia Gandhi has also documented several personal experiences and significant moments from her life in her memoir, titled *Belonging: A Journey of Love*. The book is scheduled to be launched on November 10.
