The memoir chronicles Sonia Gandhi's journey, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance that brought her to India to the personal losses that profoundly shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country.

In the book, the 79-year-old Congress veteran, who holds the distinction of being the party's longest-serving president, revisits her childhood in Italy, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband, Rajiv Gandhi.

World.title: Special Sub-Inspector of Police beaten to death in Theni
World.content:
A Special Sub-Inspector (SSI) of Police, Senthilkumar, was beaten to death by a gang for questioning them about disrupting traffic at Samadharmapuram in Theni Allinagaram by bursting crackers in the middle of the road and making social media reels on the night of Deepavali.

The police said Senthilkumar, who is attached to the office of the Theni Deputy Superintendent of Police, was returning home after duty on Sunday night (November 8, 2026). He found some people bursting crackers in the middle of the road at Samadharmapuram and making reels at around 10:30 p.m.

The SSI, who was in civvies, scolded them to stop disrupting traffic and burst crackers on the road margin. When they ignored him, Mr. Senthilkumar started recording a video on his phone and sent it to his office.

Angered over this, the gang beat him. He collapsed unconscious and was rushed to a private hospital. Later, at Theni Government Medical College hospital, he was declared dead.

The Theni police are trying to identify the assailants through video footage of a closed-circuit television camera network.

World.title: Major fire breaks out in Mumbai's Dongri, dousing ops on; one dead in November 7 highrise blaze
World.content:
A major fire broke out in Mumbai's Dongri area late Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, engulfing several shops and hutments, civic officials and residents said.

The fire broke out at Haji Kasam Chawl, near Datta Mandir, on Dr Maheshwari Road, and spread across a large area.

While residents also reported hearing loud "explosion-like" sounds, it could not be independently confirmed.

The Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) declared it a Level-I fire call at 10.11 p.m., deploying a large number of its personnel along with those from the police, BEST, ward and 108 ambulance service for dousing operations.

"Efforts to bring the blaze under control are underway. Further details about the extent of damage and possible casualties are awaited," an official said.

In another incident, a fire broke out at Kamgar Stadium in Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Nagar in Dadar West at around 10.15 a.m. on Sunday (November 8).

The blaze, involving wooden and bamboo materials, was extinguished by the fire brigade at 10.32 a.m. No injuries were reported, an official said.

Meanwhile, a person was killed in a fire that broke out at a highrise residential building in Lokhandwala in Andheri West on Saturday (November 7) night, officials said.

World.title: Delhi's air quality slips into 'severe' category morning after Deepavali, AQI at 404
World.content:
Air quality across the national capital continued to deteriorate, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) slipping into the 'Severe' category in parts of Delhi the morning after Deepavali in the early hours on Monday (November 9, 2026), according to data shared by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

A thick layer of smog engulfed several parts of the city, significantly impairing visibility during the early morning hours, including around the Inderlok area.

According to the CPCB, the air quality station at ITO recorded an alarming AQI of 406 at around 4:20 a.m., categorising it as 'Severe'.

Meanwhile, several other key areas in the capital continued to reel under the 'Very Poor' air quality bracket. Rajiv Chowk clocked an AQI of 381 at 1:30 a.m., while the area surrounding South Extension registered an AQI of 360 at 4:00 a.m.

Meanwhile, Delhi Minister Kapil Mishra launched a scathing attack on Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, alleging that a campaign was being orchestrated at Mr. Kejriwal's residence to target the Hindu festival of Deepavali and Sanatan Dharma under the pretext of pollution.

In a post on X, Mr. Mishra claimed that leaders and paid celebrities would be rolled out to run a targeted narrative.

Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) is in force across Delhi-NCR.

Pollution 50 times WHO limits

With Delhiites bursting firecrackers way past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 50 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, official data showed.

The level of PM2.5 (a major pollutant) in Akshardham was 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data. This is about 50.73 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic meter for a 24-hour period.

The Delhi Government, ahead of Deepavali, had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.

The top court, on November 2, while permitting the manufacture, sale, and bursting of approved firecrackers, subjected it to specific timings for Deepavali night and directed to restore the complete ban on November 9.

(with inputs from ANI)

World.title: Police raid home of ex-President of Paraguay
World.content:
Police in Paraguay raided the home of ex-president Santiago Pena as part of a probe into a banking crisis that triggered his dismissal from office and criminal charges against him.

Authorities last week intervened to seize Ueno Bank, a popular online lender that held accounts for nearly half of Paraguay’s 6.5 million people, plus more than $800 million in government funds.

Its collapse rocked this small, normally stable country, leading to street protests. Mr. Pena is now being held in custody at a military facility.

Mr. Pena, who came to power in 2023, owned shares in the bank’s holding company, Ueno Holding, until he sold them last year.

He is accused of using his influence as president to steer millions in government deposits to Ueno Bank and of hiding or downplaying its financial woes even though he was warned about questionable loans and solvency issues.

Prosecutors announced in a statement that Mr. Pena’s home was raided as part of the probe into the bank collapse.

They say Ueno Bank received deposits from government entities even as it granted questionable loans to companies linked to Ueno executives.

Mr. Pena’s mansion outside Asuncion is part of the probe. The indictment says that in 2024 he received two loans from Ueno Bank totalling around $500,000 so he could build the house.

His monthly mortgage payment is $38,000 -- six times his monthly salary as president, the charging sheet says.

The Senate voted on Friday (November 6, 2026) to dismiss Mr. Pena, and Vice-President Pedro Alliana took his place.

Mr. Alliana said Sunday (November 8, 2026) the government has reimbursed 1.2 million Ueno Bank customers whose money was frozen in the collapse.

The disbursal totals around $158 million so far, and it will continue this week, he said.

World.title: Nvidia investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
World.content:
Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company's board of directors said Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The announcement came after Mr. Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing, The New York Times reported.

Mr. Huang apologised in a message to the company, according to the Times. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Nvidia's board said in a statement it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Mr. Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” the board said.

Mr. Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had discovered that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and determined that she was feeding information directly to Beijing. The two are not related, according to the Times.

Ms. Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years, according to the Times.

World.title: G7 Ministers meet on efforts to end Ukraine conflict, halt new Iran war
World.content:
Foreign Ministers of the G7 group meet in Paris from Monday (November 9, 2026) for two days of talks expected to see European powers press the United States to seek a fair settlement for Ukraine in the war against Russia and deter Washington from further military action against Iran.

Ministers from the leading industrialised nations of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States will be gathering with preoccupations strikingly similar to those of the last such meeting in March.

Russia’s war against Ukraine following the February 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbour is grinding towards its fifth anniversary. And Washington is still not ruling out new attacks against Iran even after the defeat of President Donald Trump’s Republicans in the midterms.

All eyes will be on U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio who is due to attend both days, unlike the March meeting where he only came for one.

This G7 ministerial meeting, one of the final acts of the French G7 presidency that saw President Emmanuel Macron host Donald Trump for the leaders’ summit this summer in the lakeside resort of Evian, had long been scheduled to be held in the southern port city of Marseille.

But at the last minute the event was moved to Paris, with only scheduling reasons given for the change.

The visit by Mr. Rubio — seen by U.S. media as a potential candidate to succeed Mr. Trump — will be his first abroad since the midterms. Washington will also in 2027 take over the G7 presidency from France.

‘Europeans will be represented’

The meeting coincides with U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) on ending the Ukraine war, with Europe concerned Kyiv must not be forced to accept disadvantageous conditions.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio that on this occasion “Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks”.

Mr. Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but “all of Europe”.

Jared Kushner, the U.S. President’s envoy and son-in-law, said the United States was working on “a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace”, a concept met with scepticism in the past by Europe.

On Iran, Mr. Trump has not ruled out new strikes, including at so-called Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. Europeans, however, are eager to see a resolution and shipping traffic return to normal in the Strait of Hormuz energy transit hub.

“We’re dealing with them now,” Mr. Trump said of the Iranians on Friday (November 6, 2026). “They want to make a deal very badly.”

The sidelines of the meeting will also see the French Finance Ministry hosting on Monday (November 9, 2026) a donor conference to raise funds to repair the dome protecting the nuclear reactor that exploded in Ukraine’s Chernobyl in 1986 after it was damaged in a Russian strike last year.

Around 500 million euros is required but only just over half has been raised so far with a target date of spring 2027 to muster the rest of the funds, the French finance ministry told AFP.

Even though the meeting was moved to Paris, Marseille will still host the launch of a network of 14 global ports uniting to combat drug trafficking, which has become a major scourge in the southern city, Barrot said.

As he addressed reporters while preparing to leave for France, Rubio declined to comment directly on Mr. Trump’s and the Republicans’ crushing loss in the U.S. midterm elections.

“It is not uncommon to have a division of power in this country,” Mr. Rubio told reporters, alluding to the fact that Trump will now see both houses of Congress controlled by the Democrats.

Asked about widespread protests in France, Rubio added that he was not worried and trusted U.S. counterparts on the ground who advised him it is safe to attend the G7 meeting.

World.title: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen evacuated, Embassy says
World.content:
Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen's Hodeidah and Sana'a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country, the Indian Embassy in Yemen said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

“All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals,” the mission said in a post on X.

Also Read | All 14 Indians in yacht incident off Yemen coast reported safe: Embassy

The Embassy of India to Yemen has successfully evacuated 19 Indian seafarers who were stranded in Hodeidah and Sana'a (Yemen) for the past two weeks. All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals. @MEAIndia — India in Yemen (@IndiaInYemen) November 8, 2026

The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe.

It is not immediately clear whether the 14 are among the 19 seafarers evacuated.

On October 23, the Indian mission had said all 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht near Hodeidah were safe and that it was in contact with relevant parties to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Some Arab media outlets had earlier quoted spokesperson Yahya Saree of the Yemen-based Houthi group as claiming that Saudi forces targeted the Indian yacht near Yuqar Island in the Red Sea, close to the Yemeni coast.

Mr. Saree had said the yacht was carrying 14 Indian nationals and that Houthi forces were rescuing them.

The incident came amid renewed escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, with attacks and counterattacks reported in recent days.

Saudi Arabia has intercepted Houthi missiles and drones, while Saudi-led coalition forces have carried out airstrikes in Yemen, raising fears of a return to wider conflict after relative calm under a 2022 truce.

The latest violence has also affected civilian and energy infrastructure and heightened concerns over security in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key international shipping route.

World.title: Pope Leo takes Milei to task as he visits divided Argentina
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV delivered a stinging critique of Argentina President Javier Milei's harsh austerity measures on Sunday (November 8, 2026), insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause.

"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," he said, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.

Pope Leo stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."

He spoke out in defence of the poor and pensioners, insisting that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" — a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.

And he told Mr. Milei, known for his foul-mouthed diatribes, that strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words."

The visit is the first by a pontiff to Argentina in nearly four decades and Pope Leo was met with calls to help mend deep divisions in the country after three years of austerity under Mr. Milei.

Pope Leo arrived in Buenos Aires from Uruguay, where he began his first trip to Latin America as Pope, the world's most Catholic continent that is becoming increasingly secular.

The visit is the first by a pontiff to the home country of the late Pope Francis in nearly four decades.

Mr. Milei famously insulted Pope Francis for his pro-poor teachings. Pope Leo said he was "retracing" Pope Francis's steps.

‘Unite us’

Argentines are hoping the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics will help unite the country, which is bitterly divided between supporters and opponents of Mr. Milei.

"Just like the World Cup unites us, hopefully the Pope will too," said Liliana Deblauwe, a 68-year-old retired teacher who waited with hundreds of people to see the Pope visit a monument to liberation hero Jose de San Martin.

Hundreds more chanting "Papa Leon" (Spanish for Leo) gathered outside the presidential palace, where he was hosted by Mr. Milei.

Brian Inacio Rodriguez, a 26-year-old job seeker, spent five days travelling overland from Ushuaia, at the very tip of South America, to see the pontiff. He said he hoped he brought "much peace to Argentina."

Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, Pope Leo is on an ambitious 12-day tour of the continent where he served nearly two decades as a missionary.

In Uruguay, he condemned drug violence and urged an end to child poverty.

The Argentine stage of his visit aims to boost the flagging faith of a country left disappointed by Pope Francis's failure to visit during his papacy. It will also act as a litmus test of support for the Church. Some 57.7% of people identified as Catholic in a recent University of Buenos Aires poll, down from around 90% in the 1960s.

Pope Leo will visit a home for disabled people and a prison and celebrate three open-air masses. The Church has said it expects a total of seven million faithful at the various events.

‘Imbecile’ Francis

Mr. Milei came to office on a promise to revive Argentina's ailing economy and tame runaway inflation by shrinking the welfare state, targeting public hospitals, universities and pensioners in particular.

The poverty rate has swung wildly since he came to power — increasing to 32.3% in September.

A close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, with a similar combative style, Mr. Milei had a tense relationship with Pope Francis.

On the campaign trail the cost-cutting economist called his countryman an "imbecile" for championing social justice.

Once in office, however, he softened his tone but he continues to heap insults on the press and opposition.

His relationship with Pope Leo has so far been cordial, but the local Catholic Church has heavily criticised him for treating key social services solely as a budgetary constraint.

Mr. Milei has also been criticised for restricting several democratic freedoms, including the right to protest. But he maintains a loyal supporter base for drastically reducing inflation.

World.title: Minister supports creation of up to 12 provinces
World.content:
• Khawaja Asif says new units should be created on administrative grounds, not linguistic, ethnic or political lines

• Calls for transfer of powers, resources from provincial capitals to local institutions

• MQM-P renews demand for new administrative units; calls for ending ‘deprivation’ of urban Sindh

SIALKOT / KARACHI: As a debate around the possible creation of new administrative units rages in the country, another federal minister on Sunday voiced his support for the proposal, but warned against carving out units on linguistic, ethnic or political lines.

Outspoken Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who has previously voiced his support for the suggestion — first put forward by his cabinet colleague Mohsin Naqvi — said that the existing concentration of authority in provincial capitals was preventing government services and resources from reaching people at the local level.

Speaking to Geo News, Mr Asif said the idea of creating new provinces had been debated for the past two months, stressing that the country could have as many as 12 if the exercise was driven by administrative needs rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations.

He argued that Pakistan’s growing population called for smaller administrative units capable of delivering public services more effectively, adding that decision-making should not be confined to provincial capitals such as Lahore, Karachi, Quetta and Peshawar.

Stressing the need to bring administrative authority closer to the people, Mr Asif also questioned the existing arrangement for distributing financial resources, insisting that funds provided by the federal government remained largely under the control of provincial administrations, instead of reaching local government institutions.

He maintained that local bodies, which were supposed to benefit from these resources, continued to depend on provincial governments for funds and authority.

The minister also urged political leaders to change their attitude towards the exercise of power, saying that as politicians, there was a temptation to exercise all the power themselves.

Public representatives must remember that their authority was entrusted to them by the people, he said.

Referring to past administrative arrangements, Mr Asif recalled the One Unit scheme, under which the provinces of West Pakistan were merged into a single administrative unit before the arrangement was eventually abolished.

He also pointed to Afghanistan, saying the number of its provinces had increased from around eight or 10 to more than 30.

The defence minister’s remarks come amid reports of a plan to divide Pakistan into 12 provinces through a possible 28th Constitutional Amendment, with a nationwide referendum also being contemplated.

Media reports suggested that the proposed restructuring could involve dividing Punjab into four provinces, KP and Balochistan into three each, and Sindh into two.

MQM-P renews demand

Meanwhile, the Muttahida Qaumi Mov­e­ment-Pakistan (MQM-P) on Sunday vowed to mobilise its entire organisational network and parliamentary leadership for the upcoming local government elections eyeing a “historic win”, while renewing its demand for the creation of new administrative units in Sindh to ensure the devolution of powers and resources to the grassroots level.

The resolve was expressed at a high-level meeting of the party’s political and administrative leadership, chaired by MQM-P Convener and Federal Minister Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui at its Bahadurabad headquarters.

According to a press release, the meeting discussed a strategy to address the long-standing grievances of urban Sindh, accelerate Karachi’s development and prepare for upcoming political and local government contests.

The party leadership stressed that the establishment of new administrative units was essential to empower people at the grassroots level and ensure the equitable provision of basic municipal services.

It maintained that the devolution of authority and resources to lower tiers of government was necessary to address the administrative and civic challenges facing urban centres.

Dr Siddiqui directed parliamentarians and organisational departments to become actively involved at the neighbourhood level and mobilise workers and residents across the city ahead of the local government elections.

Speaking at the meeting, Dr Siddiqui said ending the deprivation of urban Sindh, establishing new administrative units and winning the local government elections were among the party’s foremost priorities.

“The reconstruction and development of Karachi and other major urban centres of Sindh, transparent utilisation of public funds and the protection of citizens’ fundamental rights remained at the heart of the party’s political agenda,” a statement issued after the meeting quoted him as saying.

He added that no political or administrative obstacle would be allowed to stand in the way of public welfare and development.

The meeting also underscored the party’s determination to “restore the rightful representation of urban communities in local governance through electoral success and a stronger grassroots organisational presence”.

Imran Ayub in Karachi also contributed to this report

Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

World.title: PML-N retains both Gujranwala's NA-77 and Sahiwal's PP-203, unofficial results show
World.content:
LAHORE: The ruling PML-N retained Gujranwala’s National Assembly constituency NA-77 and Sahiwal’s Punjab Assembly constituency PP-203 in Sunday’s by-election.

Both seats had fallen vacant after the deaths of their respective lawmakers in September. Polling in the constituencies began at 8am and concluded at 5pm, with the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) reporting an uninterrupted and largely peaceful process.

In NA-77, PML-N candidate Rashid Basheer Virk was among 11 candidates contesting for the seat left vacant after the Sept 11 demise of his father, Chaudhry Mehmood Bashir Virk, a five-time MNA.

He secured victory by bagging 43,365 votes, while Pakistan Markazi Muslim League’s (PMML) Mohammad Ibrahim remained runner-up with 30,218 ballots, according to the Form-47 seen by Dawn.

Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned.

In PP-203 of Chichawatni, PML-N’s Muhammad Asad Hanif Jutt won with 42,114 votes, defeating his closest rival, Muhammad Awais Mahmood of Tehreek-i-Ehsas Pakistan (TEP), who secured 24,512 votes, according to its Form-47.

Both by-elections were marked by a low voter turnout, with 15.7 per cent in NA-77 and 27.6pc recorded in PP-203, according to Forms 47.

The by-poll was held following the death of PML-N MPA Chaudhry Muhammad Hanif Jutt. This was the second time that a by-election was held in the constituency after the 2024 general elections.

Notices were also issued to several PML-N lawmakers for alleged violations of the election code, mostly over visiting polling stations in the two constituencies.

Earlier in the day, Chief Election Commissioner Sikander Sultan Raja visited the provincial election chief’s office, where he was briefed on the polling process in both constituencies, ECP said.

After the balloting process concluded, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, whose PML-N is in power in the province, made multiple posts on X, claiming her party was in the lead in both NA-77 and PP-203.

In one post, CM Maryam wrote, “This electoral victory is no ordinary victory. It is a resounding public rebuke to conspiracy peddlers, hate mongers and those who refuse to read the writing on the wall.”

She contended that the results portrayed that the “politics of delivery is far more enduring than the politics of hate and revenge”.

“I am glad politics has returned to delivery and performance. Wake up and smell the coffee… or keep sleeping in denial!” the PML-N leader added.

Notices over alleged electoral conduct violations

While the polling was under way, notices, copies of which are available with Dawn, were issued to Punjab MPA Qudsia Batool, MNA Saira Afzal Tarar and Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Culture Shazia Rizwan for alleged violation of the Code of Conduct after reports emerged on social media that the three had visited various polling stations within NA-77, a statement issued by the office of the provincial election commissioner said.

Notices were also issued over alleged violations of the Code of Conduct to PML-N’s MNA Syeda Nosheen Iftikhar and MPA Hina Arshad Warraich for allegedly visiting polling stations.

The officials were directed to appear at the Election Complex in Gujranwala for an explanation at 3pm.

Separately, PML-N leader and Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari claimed in a post on X that supporters of PMML candidate Qazi Ibrahim Gujjar were caught “openly stamping ballots” with the election commission staff present.

Acting on the complaint, the provincial election commissioner said the returning officer concerned has been directed to probe the matter and submit a report.

On Saturday, the ECP took notice of an alleged violation of the Code of Conduct by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar during by-election campaigning in NA-77 .

According to a cause list issued on Sunday, Tarar, along with Virk, Batool and others, has been summoned to appear at the next hearing on Nov 12.

According to the ECP, the minister visited the constituency by helicopter and addressed a campaign event for Rashid, violating a provision in the Code of Conduct , which bars public office holders from participating in campaign activities.

ECP has sought a report from the district monitoring officer and the district returning officer to inquire into the matter. The watchdog also said that the result of the constituency could be withheld until a final decision is made on the matter.

Meanwhile, notices were also issued to PML-N MPAs Malik Qasim Nadeem and Motiya Begum for allegedly visiting several polling stations in Chichawatni’s PP-203 on the polling day.

The notices issued by the district monitoring officer, seen by Dawn, accused both of violating Para 48 of the Code of Conduct, which bars “all kinds of campaigns” and canvassing within a 400-metre radius of a polling station.

The MPAs were asked to appear either in person or through counsel at the Municipal Committee Office at 5pm on Nov 9 (Monday) to clarify their position.

Polling in PP-203

The seat was initially won in 2024 by independent candidate Rai Murtaza Iqbal, backed by the PTI, with 55,874 votes against Jutt, who polled 35,163 votes.

However, Iqbal, along with four other PTI-backed parliamentarians, was disqualified and denotified by the ECP following their conviction by an anti-terrorism court in Faisalabad on July 31.

Subsequently, the ECP scheduled a by-election for Nov 23, 2025, which was won by Jutt with 46,820 votes. His closest rival, independent candidate Falik Sher, secured 10,975 votes.

Jutt died of cardiac arrest on Sept 17 this year, necessitating Sunday’s by-election in the constituency.

Around 1,370 polling personnel, including 574 women and 796 men, were deputed at 185 polling stations across the constituency.

District Police Officer Usman Tipu said 1,100 personnel had been deployed to ensure security during the by-election.

A total of 185 polling stations had been established in the constituency, including 11 in Category A, 37 in Category B and 137 in Category C.

A comprehensive traffic management plan had also been devised, with more than 65 personnel assigned duties.

World.title: Heatwaves in Punjab threaten agriculture, food security: UN
World.content:
• Report says fruit yields plunge 50pc; heat stress spreads livestock disease, cuts milk output

• Shrinking incomes, food spoilage limit rural families’ healthy diets

• Women bear brunt of crisis due to heavy outdoor labour; preterm birth risk jumps 26pc in severe weather

ISLAMABAD: Increasingly frequent and severe heatwaves in Punjab’s rain-fed rural areas are disrupting agricultural production, reducing household incomes and worsening food insecurity, particularly among women and vulnerable communities, according to a report by United Nations (UN) agencies.

The assessment “Extreme Heat and Agriculture”, was published jointly by the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

It warns that rising temperatures have emerged as one of the most serious and acute hazards facing global food production, threatening the livelihoods of billions of people while inflicting immediate economic and nutritional damage on vulnerable farming communities.

“The effects of extreme heat on production are stark, as heat wav­es have led to significant declines in crop yields,” the report said.

In the high-rainfall zones of Punjab, fruit productivity has fallen by as much as 50 per cent, the agencies found.

Livestock operations across the region are also severely affected. Large ruminants produce less milk under heat stress, and small ruminants face increased outbreaks of foot-and-mouth disease, the report said.

For rural families dependent on farming, the loss of agricultural output directly translates into reduced household income and diminishes their ability to purchase basic food staples.

The crisis is compounded by the accelerated spoilage of vegetables, dairy products and other perishable goods in extreme temperatures. That widespread spoilage further reduces local food availability and drives up market prices.

As a result, rural families face a double burden. They produce less diverse and nutritious food for their own consumption while simultaneously losing the agricultural income they rely on to purchase food from markets. “This double burden severely limits their access to healthy diets,” the report said.

Although entire communities are affected, women generally bear a disproportionate share of the burden, the UN agencies found. Women in Punjab play an essential role in agricultural activities, including harvesting, collecting water and carrying out physically demanding household responsibilities.

This exposes them to high temperatures for extended periods, increasing their risk of heat-related illnesses and other health complications.

Those health risks are particularly acute for pregnant and lactating women, who have greater nutritional and dietary needs that are often the first to be compromised during periods of household food scarcity.

Research cited in the report indicates that each 1°C rise in temperature is associated with a 4pc increase in the likelihood of preterm birth. During heat waves, the risk of preterm birth jumps to 26pc, according to the report.

Additional social inequalities exacerbate women’s vulnerabilities to extreme heat. Despite their critical role in farming, women often lack ownership of land and other assets, necessary to access credit and financial services that could aid adaptation.

With limited access to climate information and early warning systems, they are often less prepared to respond to heat events.

Rural women’s coping strategies, such as reducing their own food intake to prioritise other family members, which can further compromise their health and resilience, reflect broader patterns of gender discrimination that amplify their vulnerability in times of climate crisis, the report said.

Beyond the localised crisis in Punjab, the FAO and the WMO warned that extreme heat is acting as a powerful risk multiplier with direct and indirect impacts across all agricultural subsectors worldwide.

Rising temperatures amplify existing environmental hazards such as drought, heighten the risk of destructive wildfires and create complex compound impacts.

Those converging threats endanger not only global agricultural production, but also the physical health of agricultural workers who labour on the front lines of the growing climate threat.

The fingerprints of extreme heat on agriculture are already visible worldwide, and the analysis of scientific evidence confirms that heat is driving significant productivity losses.

Under high-emission scenarios, nearly half the world’s cattle could be exposed to dangerous heat by 2100, with annual losses nearing $40bn, although under a low-emission scenario, impacts from livestock exposure to extreme heat are reduced by nearly two-thirds.

In aquatic systems, marine heatwaves have already caused repeated mass mortality events and are forcing entire fish stocks to migrate in search of cooler water. Fruit and nut trees and natural forests are also subject to production losses and the growing risk of more frequent and intense wildfires.

Together, those global agricultural losses create a dangerous environmental feedback loop, the report concluded. When heat-driven shortfalls in crop and livestock production prompt farmers to clear additional land for agricultural expansion to compensate for lost yields, the resulting land-use changes increase greenhouse gas emissions — fuelling further climate change.

Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

World.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan agree to settle old boundary disputes
World.content:
KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and GB Chief Minister Amjad Hussain meet in Islamabad.—Dawn

GILGIT/MANSEHRA: In a move towards resolving decades-old territorial issues, Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi have agreed to initiate negotiations to settle boundary disputes between the two regions, including those involving Shandur Top, Babusar Top and areas surrounding the Diamer-Bhasha and Dassu dams.

The agreement came during a meeting between the two leaders in Islamabad on Sunday, where they discussed matters of mutual interest, including territorial disputes, improved air connectivity to Gilgit-Baltistan and the training of relevant officials.

According to a statement issued by the GB Chief Minister’s Secre­tariat, both leaders agreed that the boundary disputes would be taken up by the chief secretaries of the two regions, before being referred to their respective political leadership for deliberations.

South Air offers to operate flights to northern areas

The initiative aims to resolve disputes involving villages along the KP-GB boundary through mutual understanding and amicable negotiations.

An official attending the meeting told Dawn that the two sides had agreed to pursue a peaceful settlement of the long-standing disputes, which have repeatedly triggered tensions and violent clashes between communities living along the disputed territories.

Disputes between KP and GB persist over several strategically important areas, including Shandur Top, Babusar Top and parts of Kohistan.

Shandur Top, home to the world’s highest polo ground at around 12,500 feet, is claimed by both provinces, with the matter under consideration by a provincial boundary commission.

Babusar Top, linking Man­sehra with Diamer through Kaghan Valley, is another contested area whose ownership and juri­sdiction remain unresolved by the federal government. The dispute has also surfaced in land acquisition and compensation claims, prompting the Peshawar High Court to direct the NHA and KP government to clear outstanding payments to landowners whose properties were acquired in 2001 for road expansion.

Another major dispute concerns the Harban tribe of Kohistan and the Thor tribe of Diamer over an eight-kilometre stretch near the Diamer-Bhasha Dam. A 2014 clash over the land claimed the lives of five people and left 15 injured.

A 24-member jirga defused the decades-old dispute in 2022, paving the way for official demarcation and compensation payments to affected Kohistan settlers.

However, other territorial and ownership questions, including those concerning areas near the Dassu Dam and Babusar Top, have continued to complicate relations between communities on both sides of the provincial boundary.

Air connectivity

Apart from territorial matters, the Islamabad meeting also focused on improving air connectivity between Gilgit and Islamabad, where passengers have long faced difficulties because of limited flight operations and frequent cancellations.

At present, PIA operates a 44-seat ATR aircraft on the Islamabad-Gilgit route. The limited seating capacity, coupled with weather-related cancellations, has made air travel particularly difficult for patients, tourists and government officials who depend on the service.

The operational limitations of Gilgit airport, which cannot accommodate larger aircraft, further restrict travel options.

During the meeting, representatives of the private airline South Air also held discussions with the GB chief minister regarding the introduction of additional air services.

According to an official source, it was agreed that aircraft would be acquired on lease against a guarantee provided by the GB government, while South Air would operate flights under a joint-venture arrangement.

The proposed service is expected to introduce weather-compliant aircraft on the Isla­mabad-Gilgit route, potentially improving the reliability of air travel for residents and visitors.
